# Quality-filter sweep — ATR vs footprint gates (2026-10-02)

Question: is there a better breakout-bar quality filter than the
ATR-normalized range gate? Ran the full momentum replay head-to-head
(`scripts/momentumStudy.ts --offline --sweep`), 648 sessions, split
2026-01-01, plus the Globex-hour-filtered mirror of the live config.
Outcome: `pnl > 0` = win; PF from summed point P&L; expR = net ÷ trades ÷
mean risk. "rr" = minBreakRangeR (range ÷ ATR14).

## Momentum — all hours

| variant | n | WR | PF | net pts | expR |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| prod (no ATR) | 2228 | 74.6% | 2.56 | +4476 | 0.42 |
| prod+rr0.85 (was live) | 2184 | 75.0% | 2.60 | +4468 | 0.42 |
| **prod+rr1.0** | 2129 | **75.5%** | **2.68** | **+4483** | 0.43 |
| prod+rr1.2 | 1970 | 76.4% | 2.84 | +4406 | **0.45** |
| prod+stack | 2147 | 74.8% | 2.60 | +4399 | 0.42 |
| prod+churnVeto | 1961 | 74.5% | 2.48 | +3663 | 0.40 |
| prod+poc / +pocMove / +both | 1610–2089 | 74.3–75.0% | 2.46–2.58 | +3105–4240 | 0.40–0.42 |
| prod+quietBefore | 999 | 72.9% | 2.39 | +1877 | 0.39 |
| prod+diag1 | 1339 | 75.5% | 2.69 | +2888 | 0.43 |
| prod+rr1.0+diag1 | 1268 | 76.6% | 2.83 | +2884 | 0.45 |
| prod+rr1.0+diag2 | 740 | 77.4% | 3.03 | +1864 | 0.48 |
| prod+rr1.0+eff1.5 / eff2 | 223–510 | 71.7–73.5% | 2.31–2.51 | +418–999 | 0.38–0.41 |

## Momentum — Globex-filtered (live-equivalent)

| variant | n | WR | PF | net pts | expR |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| prod (no ATR) | 2208 | 74.8% | 2.60 | +4480 | 0.42 |
| prod+rr0.85 (was live) | 2166 | 75.2% | 2.65 | +4475 | 0.43 |
| **prod+rr1.0** | 2114 | **75.6%** | **2.71** | **+4482** | 0.44 |
| prod+rr1.2 | 1959 | 76.5% | 2.87 | +4394 | **0.46** |
| prod+rr1.0+diag1 | 1254 | 76.7% | 2.89 | +2876 | 0.46 |
| prod+rr1.0+diag2 | 733 | 77.5% | 3.05 | +1846 | 0.48 |

## Expansion sweep (same archive)

| variant | n | WR | PF | net pts | expR |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| exp1.4s | 6129 | 77.3% | 2.94 | +14441 | 0.47 |
| **exp1.6s (live)** | 4893 | **78.1%** | **3.05** | +12107 | 0.48 |
| exp1.8s / exp2.0s | 2989–3810 | 78.0–78.1% | 3.04 | +7624–9591 | 0.48 |
| exp1.6s+poc / +pocMove | 3453–4652 | 77.8–78.0% | 2.97–2.99 | +8297–11323 | 0.47 |
| exp1.6s+core | 3910 | 78.8% | 3.23 | +10100 | 0.50 |

## Verdict

1. **No footprint gate beats ATR-range as the quality filter.** Stack,
   churn veto, POC position/migration, quiet-before, efficiency density
   and diagonal imbalance all either subtract total net or match ATR at a
   fraction of the sample. ATR-normalized range stays.
2. **The ATR gate itself was set one notch too loose.** rr1.0 strictly
   dominates rr0.85 on WR, PF and total net in both sweeps — applied to
   `MOM_PROD` (2026-10-02). rr1.2 is the "fewer, better trades" option
   (best expR) at a ~90-pt total-net cost.
3. **Diagonal imbalance (diag) is the one footprint gate with real
   quality signal** (+1.5–1.9 pp WR, PF 2.89–3.05 with rr1.0) — but at
   IMB_MIN=10 lots it cuts the sample and total net ~35–60%. It is a
   valid "high-conviction mode", not a replacement. Available as
   `minBreakDiag` (momentum detector), default off.
4. **Expansion config is already at the knee**: 1.6×ATR + stack; POC
   gates subtract trades without quality.
5. New detector knobs (`minBreakEffR`, `minBreakDiag`) ship default-off;
   the self-improvement miner can propose them later when live data
   supports it.

# Side-filter study — "when should the card take ONLY longs / ONLY shorts?" (2026-10-09)

> Question: *"which condition combination tells us with the highest
> certainty: during this time, only take the longs / only take the shorts?"*
> Answer measured on the card's own replayable signal stream — the same
> 3,298 replayed trades that carry the 76.8% WR / PF 2.93 baseline — not on
> day-direction folklore. CLI: `web/scripts/sideFilterStudy.ts` (+ trade-row
> dump for the instant pair/triple search).

## Method

esStudy/almanac replay discipline: MOM_PROD flush + EXP_PROD, sequential
one-trade-at-a-time, pessimistic same-bar exit, 0.5 pt cost, 60-bar time
exit, split 2026-01-01, Wilson 95% CIs. Per-trade context (lookahead-free
at entry): entry-hour bucket, session ALN pattern (P1–P4/"early"), HTF
daily structure from the prior 65 RTH sessions, gap vs prior RTH close
(small <0.5% · mid 0.5–1.5% · large >1.5%, signed), FOMC window.

Baseline: all 76.8% WR / PF 2.93 / +2.39 pts · longs 78.6% / 3.26 / +2.56 ·
shorts 75.0% / 2.65 / +2.22. **Because both sides are strongly positive
almost everywhere, "only one side" must be earned by DOMINANCE (expectancy
gap between the sides), not by the loser being negative.**

## The answer — measured one-sided cells (sorted by certainty)

| # | Rule (only take…) | n | WR [CI] | PF | avg pts | train / test | opposite side |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **ONLY LONGS — gap 0.5–1.5% DOWN + overnight tape (ALN early) + no FOMC** | 57 | **88%** [77–94] | — | **+5.19** | 88% / 88% | 72% / +2.12 |
| 2 | ONLY LONGS — gap 0.5–1.5% DOWN (any hour/HTF) | 102 | 79.4% [71–86] | 3.97 | +3.90 | 77% / 83% | 70% / +2.06 |
| 3 | ONLY LONGS — gap 0.5–1.5% UP + late-night 23–02 ET | 104 | 86% [78–91] | 6.31 | +3.40 | 83% / 93% | 80% / +2.52 |
| 4 | ONLY LONGS — gap 0.5–1.5% UP + HTF bear | 106 | 85% [77–90] | 5.92 | +3.73 | 81% / 92% | 73% / +2.38 |
| 5 | ONLY LONGS — ALN P3 + HTF bear | 117 | 83% [75–89] | 4.80 | +3.47 | 83% / 83% | 71% / +1.74 |
| 6 | ONLY LONGS — ALN P3 + small gap down | 89 | 88% [79–93] | 7.27 | +3.65 | 90% / 85% | 70% / +1.93 |
| 7 | ONLY LONGS — small gap down + evening 18–22 ET | 184 | 85% [79–89] | 5.45 | +3.17 | 84% / 87% | 71% / +2.04 |
| 8 | **ONLY SHORTS — gap ≥1.5% UP (large gap up)** | 33 | 78.8% [62–89] | 3.50 | +3.16 | 80% / 77% | 59.6% / +0.47 |
| 9 | ONLY SHORTS — pre-open 08–09 ET (no FOMC) | 38 | 89% [76–96] | 11.03 | +4.42 | 87% / 100%* | 66% / +1.49 |
| 10 | ONLY LONGS — ALN P2 (Asia engulfs London, chop) | 46 | 73.9% [60–84] | 2.49 | +2.23 | 77% / 69%† | 55.6% / **−0.47** |

\* test n=8 — monitor, do not gate. † test n=16 — just under the bar.
The #1 cell (mid-down gap + overnight tape + non-FOMC) is the single
highest-certainty one-sided statement in the archive: +5.19 pts avg at 88%
WR with train/test agreement and the opposite side at +2.12.

**The gap regime at entry is the dominant filter axis.** Longs win after
every mid gap (down AND up — buying the tape's failed flushes after a
moderate overnight move); shorts only after LARGE gaps up (the day is
already priced, the card's failed-breakout shorts get paid). Small gaps:
mild long tilt (large n, both sides positive).

## Falsified on the card (as valuable as the positives)

- **"Only shorts in HTF-bear regimes" — FALSE on the card.** Bear-regime
  LONGS are the best cell in the HTF axis (79.6% WR / +2.91, train 80 /
  test 79); shorts in bear 77.4%. The card's failed-flush long buys
  work in bear tapes; do not side-filter by HTF alone (consistent with
  htf-short-pullback's "don't veto counter-trend" finding).
- **"Only one side on FOMC days" — FALSE.** Both sides ≈ 84% WR / PF ≈ 5
  (dominance 0.00): trade everything, it's the best cell in the almanac.
- **"Only longs in bull HTF" — weak.** Bull-regime dominance is just
  0.38 pts (longs +2.46 vs shorts +2.08) — a tint, not a filter.
- **Prime 03–07 ET: no side filter** (dominance 0.12) — both sides are
  the best of the day; the window, not the side, is the edge there.

## Honest bounds

- ~150 cells + ~30 combinations were measured — multiple testing is real.
  The adopted statements are the ones where train/test agree AND the
  mechanism is legible (gap economics, pre-open fade, chop containment).
  Per house rules: **journal chips first, forward-log, gates only after
  the same walk-forward pass that every other filter needed.**
- Several cells are thin (large-gap cells n=33–47, pre-open test n=8,
  P2 test n=16). Treat #1/#2/#3/#4/#6/#7/#8 as the workhorse set
  (n≥57 with agreement); #9/#10 as watch-items.
- Replay is market-entry (the almanac convention); the live EXP path is
  the retrace limit variant (68% WR / PF 1.29) — the dominance gaps
  should be re-measured on `EXP_RETRACE` before any sizing change.

## Wired (2026-10-09) — chips + journal, labels only, never gates

- **Card journal chips** — `web/lib/sideFilter.ts` (`sideFilterChips`, 6
  unit tests) prints the in-memory cells on the live momentum card chip
  line, with features recorded into the journal for every card AND skip:
  - `P2 LONG-ONLY 74%` (ALN P2, entries ≥ 08:00 ET)
  - `P4 23–02 SHORT-ONLY 84%` (ALN P4, late-night window)
  - `08–09 SHORT-ONLY 89%` (pre-open hour, FOMC/pre-FOMC days excluded)
- **Briefing chips** — `lib/biasChips.ts` `sideLeanChips` adds the
  gap/HTF-dependent cells to the macro-watch bias block (server-side, where
  the prior RTH close + HTF structure live): mid gap down/up → longs,
  large gap up → shorts, P3+bear → longs, P4 late-night → shorts, pre-open
  → shorts. They ride first in the briefing card's chip line and in
  `scripts/biasChips.ts`.
- The gap-regime cells are NOT card chips: the live card path holds no
  prior-session close in memory (no-network hot path) — they live in the
  briefing, which already reads the archive.
- House discipline unchanged: labels recorded in the journal forward-log;
  a gate or sizing change would need its own walk-forward pass first.

## Standard report — rerun 2026-10-10 on the consolidated engine

`web/lib/backtestEngine.ts` migration (user consolidation 2026-10-10):
stats now come from `coreStats`/`wilson95`/`propViability`; this closes
the gaps the report standard's worked example (§7) pointed at in this
study's original baseline row.

| cohort | n | WR [CI95] | avg win | avg loss | payoff | exp (pts) | exp (R) | PF | SQN | maxDD (pts) | Sharpe (sess) | conc top10 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| all | 3,298 | **76.8%** [75.4–78.2] | +4.72 | 5.34 | 0.88 | **+2.39** | **+0.43** | **2.93** | 29.1 | 62.1 | 0.98 | 6.9% |
| train | 2,319 | 75.6% [73.8–77.3] | +4.16 | 4.98 | 0.84 | +1.93 | +0.40 | 2.59 | 22.2 | 62.1 | 0.89 | 8.9% |
| test | 979 | 79.8% [77.1–82.2] | +5.98 | 6.38 | 0.94 | +3.48 | +0.50 | 3.69 | 19.6 | 36.8 | 1.25 | 15.7% |

| stage | rules | n trades | trading days | total profit | best day | consist | min-days | breach | pass | payouts | outcome |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| eval | Rapid EOD 50k | 3,298 | 641 | $133,927 | $1,021 | ✓ | ✓ | — | 2024-01-30 ($3,391) | — | PASS 2024-01-30 · consist ✓ |
| funded | Rapid EOD 50k | 3,298 | 641 | $133,927 | $1,021 | — | — | — | — | 264 | payouts 264 · floor $131,927 locked |
| eval (test-only) | Rapid EOD 50k | 979 | 180 | $46,084 | $1,021 | — | — | — | 2026-01-13 ($3,667) | — | PASS 2026-01-13 · consist ✓ |

P(pass before breach) = 100% · median days to pass = 641 · maxDD $867 =
43% of MLL (500 reshuffles)

`VERDICT: edge real · significance — · stability train/test WR gap −4.2 pts
· holdout n/a (validation pipeline) · viability PASS (P=1.00)`

# Winner/loser atlas — session delta, session-extreme targets, and the loss anatomy

> First measurement pass over the full NQ archive: **649 sessions** (2023-12-18
> → 2026-10-05), the three production families replayed with their live plan
> shapes (MOM failed-flush 1R · EXP huge-bar expansion 1R · RTH soft 0.75R;
> first-touch, 60-bar time exit, 0.5 pt cost, sequential one-trade-at-a-time),
> canonical split 2026-01-01. Machinery: `web/scripts/winnerLoserAtlas.ts`
> (archive replay + per-trade session context, CSV dump at
> `docs/data/winner-loser-atlas-2026-10-05.csv`) and `web/scripts/winnerLoserLive.ts`
> (the same features recomputed on the reconciled live `trades` rows in Neon).
>
> Session context is computed lookahead-free at the entry bar: cumulative
> buy−sell since the session open and the session high/low **at entry time**.
> Cells: "agrees/against" = trade direction vs the sign of session cumΔ;
> "ATH-retest" = |target − session extreme| ≤ 0.5 with the target NOT beyond
> it; "fresh-air" = target beyond the session extreme by > 0.25 pts.
>
> **Headline:** (1) gating a direction against the session cumulative delta
> buys nothing — pooled 79.8% WR / +2.99 pts vs 79.7% / +2.90, and in the
> flush family counter-delta is the *better* cell; (2) the dangerous target
> is not the "not defined" fresh-air high — it is the **exact ATH retest**
> (target sitting on the session extreme, pooled +0.70 vs +2.96 baseline,
> weak in all three families, and *no* exit management — including
> breakeven-at-1R — rescues it); fresh-air targets are fine to best, and
> only MOM's fresh-air cell profits from a BE@1R runner (+0.18); (3) the
> dominant loss mode everywhere is the stop-run — 60–72% of stop-outs print
> a return beyond the entry within 10 bars, and 0% of losing trades ever
> touched +1R first, so breakeven ladders can only ever change winners, never
> rescue losers.

---

## 1. Q1 — should a direction against the session cumΔ be gated? No.

| Cell | MOM flush 1R | EXP expansion 1R | RTH soft 0.75R |
|---|---|---|---|
| ALL | 1,559 · 75.4% · +2.18 | 2,935 · 77.4% · +2.50 | 2,794 · 84.6% · +3.86 |
| agrees w/ cumΔ | 75.1% · +2.15 | 77.2% · +2.52 | **85.2% · +3.97** |
| against cumΔ | **75.9% · +2.21** | **77.8% · +2.48** | 83.8% · +3.72 |
| strongest-against (Δ ≤ −800 vs dir) | 75.3% · +2.16 | 78.5% · +2.61 | 83.3% · +3.67 |
| veto against, \|Δ\| ≥ 400 | Δexp +0.01 | Δexp +0.01 | Δexp +0.12 (test 4.27 → **4.22**) |

Pooled: agrees n=4,198 +2.99 vs against n=3,090 +2.90 — flat. The flush
family is the cleanest statement: a failed-flush long is *by construction* a
counter-delta trade (sellers dominated the session, yet failed to break the
low), and it is the best cell. Even the extreme bands (session delta ≥ 800
against the trade) carry family-average expectancy. The only family with a
visible gap (RTH, +0.25 exp) does not survive the train/test split when the
veto is applied — test expectancy goes **down** (4.27 → 4.22).

The live tape agrees: on 2026-10-01 the session cumΔ ran from −717 to
−7,464, and the 12 winners were mostly counter-delta **longs** (only 4/12
agreed) while 13 of 19 losses were with-delta shorts.

**Verdict: no gate.** Consistent with `counterBiasVeto.ts` (day-bias veto
≈ 0) and the ES Δ− chip being a journal label, never a gate. Keep cumΔ as a
journal chip; do not filter on it.

## 2. Q2 — target at the session high/low: two cells, opposite answers

| Cell | MOM | EXP | RTH | pooled |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **ATH-retest** (target ON the extreme ±0.5) | 27 · 63.0% · +0.75 | 37 · 62.2% · +0.84 | 44 · 70.5% · +0.55 | **108 · 65.7% · +0.70** |
| **fresh-air** (target beyond by > 0.25) | 231 · 77.5% · **+2.81** | 436 · 75.0% · +2.26 | 0 | 667 · 75.9% · +2.45 |
| inside range (baseline reference) | 75.2% · +2.08 | 78.0% · +2.56 | 84.7% · +3.89 | +2.96 (all trades) |

The user's instinct is half right. **"Session all-time high" = the exact
retest** — price has been rejected at that level all session — is a genuinely
weak cell in every family (WR −15 pp, expectancy +0.55–0.84 vs family
baselines of +2.2–3.9). It is rare (~1.5% of trades, n=108 pooled). **The
"not defined high" = fresh air** is the opposite: not dangerous at all, and
for the MOM flush family it is the single best cell in the whole family
(+2.81, PF 3.27).

Management variants on each cell (0.5 pt cost, 60-bar exit):

| Variant | MOM ATH-retest | MOM fresh-air | EXP ATH-retest | EXP fresh-air | RTH ATH-retest |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| base (fixed target) | +0.75 | +2.81 | +0.84 | +2.26 | +0.55 |
| target capped @extreme | +0.71 | +2.65 | +0.80 | +2.22 | +0.54 |
| early bank 0.5R | +0.66 | +1.27 | +0.77 | +1.13 | **−0.11** |
| early bank 0.75R | +0.02 | +2.16 | +0.45 | +1.91 | +0.55 |
| runner BE@1R ladder | **−0.14** | **+2.98** | +0.04 | +1.83 | +0.61 |
| ½ fixed + ½ runner | +0.31 | +2.90 | +0.44 | +2.05 | +0.58 |

- **Nothing rescues the ATH-retest cell.** Capping, early banking, and
  breakeven ladders all leave it at +0.0…+0.8 — and the BE@1R runner makes
  MOM's cell *negative*. The breakeven idea cannot work there because the
  losers never get near 1R: 0% of stop-outs touched +1R first (see §3).
  The right "care" is recognizing the cell and skipping or sizing down —
  it is a ~1.5%-frequency drag of ~0.03 pts/trade overall, so the cheapest
  correct action is journal-awareness, not new machinery.
- **Fresh air needs no extra care.** MOM fresh-air is the family's best
  cell; the only variant that adds to it is the BE@1R runner (+2.98,
  +0.18). EXP fresh-air is mildly below family (+2.26 vs +2.50) and every
  variant makes it worse — leave it at the fixed target. RTH never prints
  a fresh-air target (0.75R target, n=0).
- Breakeven-at-1R is therefore **not a general loss-saver** — see §3.

## 3. Q3 — winner vs loser atlas

**Loss anatomy (the single biggest pattern).** Every stop-out bar in all
three families was checked for a 10-bar return beyond the entry:

| Family | stop-outs | run-back ≤10 bars | touched +0.5R first | touched +1R first |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| MOM flush | 383 | **65%** | 54% | 0% |
| EXP expansion | 659 | **60%** | 62% | 0% |
| RTH soft | 430 | **72%** | 26% | 0% |

Live 2026-10-01: 11 of 19 losses were labeled stop-runs (58%). Two
consequences: (a) the tape runs our stops ~2/3 of the time — this is the
background behind the stop-run studies, and widening stops was already
measured to buy ~0 (the run-back does not convert into expectancy);
(b) **no losing trade ever reached +1R first**, so breakeven-at-1R can only
ever convert *winners* into runners — it is a winner-management tool, not a
loss filter. MOM/EXP losers reach ~half-R then reverse (median MFE +0.54R /
+0.63R); RTH losers mostly die on the very next bar (median held 1 bar, only
26% touched +0.5R).

**Feature medians, winners vs losers** (readable per family in the script
output; the durable signals):

- MOM `deltaFromFlush`: winners **+10** vs losers **−28** — in the flush
  family, losers have order-flow delta *bleeding against the trade* between
  the flush and the entry bar (RTH mirrors: −22 vs −85).
- RTH candle quality: losers have smaller `breakRangeR` (1.23 vs 1.38),
  lower `atr14` (9 vs 10), tighter `riskPts` (7.25 vs 8.38) — the weak-bar
  RTH trades lose; the ≥1.0×ATR gate is doing real work.
- EXP `distToExt`: losers 28.5 vs winners 32.6 — expansion trades fired
  closer to the session extreme lose more often (same story as the
  fresh-air/ATH-retest split).

**Cells:**

- **Shorts are the weaker side only in MOM** (72.9% / +1.90 vs longs 78.0% /
  +2.46); EXP and RTH sides are near-equal (RTH long 85.7% / short 83.5%).
- **Tuesday is the weakest day in all three families** (pooled +2.65 vs
  +3.04 on other days; MOM +2.01, EXP +2.36, RTH +3.28 — each below its
  family mean). Friday is MOM-weak (+1.83) but fine for EXP/RTH. Monday is
  strong for MOM/EXP — consistent with `seasonal-almanac-2026-10-05.md`.
- **After-loss trades are not worse** (pooled +2.92 vs +2.82 after a win;
  MOM +2.57 after a loss vs +2.00 after a win). Longest same-day losing
  streak per family: 3–4. No revenge-trade penalty — shrinking after losses
  buys nothing (matches `sizing-dynamics-2026-10-02.md`).
- **First RTH card of the day is disproportionately good** (+5.33 vs +3.86);
  MOM/EXP first-of-day ≈ average.
- EXP **close bucket** (16:00–17:00 ET) is the family's weak bucket
  (67.1% WR, +1.42, n=74) — already reflected in `ticketVeto.ts`
  (`momentum_expansion/close/short` +0.75); the atlas says the whole close
  bucket is weak, not just shorts.

## 4. Standing caveats

1. This is a **scratch sweep, not a validation**: no account sim, and the
   veto rows are filter-only (the occupancy effect of removing a trade is
   not replayed — same limitation as `counterBiasVeto.ts`).
2. Small cells: ATH-retest n = 27/37/44 per family (108 pooled) — the
   direction is consistent across all three families, but per-family Wilson
   CIs are wide.
3. Same house rules as every replay: first-touch scoring, 0.5 pt cost,
   pessimistic same-bar stop-first exits, mid-price for archive closes.

*Educational research only — not financial advice.*
es-features-study:
# ES cross-asset features — final backtest (full coverage)

> Final study over the complete ES archive: **649/649 sessions with ES twins**
> (Dec 2023 → Oct 2026), canonical split 2026-01-01. All-card baseline
> includes the RTH soft card (--rth). Machinery: `web/lib/esJoin.ts` (join +
> features, 11 unit tests), `web/scripts/esStudy.ts` (replay + splits). Same
> discipline as momentumStudy: MOM_PROD + EXP_PROD + SOFT_PROD, pessimistic
> same-bar scoring, 0.5 pt cost, 60-bar exit, Wilson CIs.
>
> Coverage: 2,119 flush trades, 16,524 all-card trades — 100% ES-covered.
> Baselines (all cards): 81.0% WR (train 80.8 / test 81.4). Flush cards:
> 75.3% (train 74.2 / test 77.7). The 2026 test window is the easier tape —
> every comparison below is within-window.

---

## 1. Flush agreement — no adoptable signal

ES flushed the same side and held its own extreme at the NQ flush bar.

| Bucket | n | WR all | WR test | note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| agree | 569 | 75.6% | 80.5% | agree-long test 85.7% (n=56) — small, monitor |
| neutral | 1,530 | 75.3% | 76.9% | |
| diverge | 20 | 70.0% | — | too rare to matter |

Overall tie; the test-window agree-long cell is interesting but n=56.
**Not adopted. Watch agree-long in live journaling.**

## 2. Breakdown gate — REJECTED as a veto; ADOPTED as a tier (BROAD CONFIRM)

Veto NQ cards when ES printed a new session extreme in the 5 bars before
entry — measured at full coverage:

| Group | n | WR | PF | avgPts | test WR |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| baseline (gate off) | 16,524 | 81.0% | 3.33 | 2.98 | 81.4% |
| kept (gate on) | 15,895 | 80.8% | 3.29 | 2.95 | 81.2% |
| **vetoed** | **629** | **85.2%** | **4.84** | **3.86** | **87.4%** |

The vetoed group is the BEST group in every cut: +4.2 pts over baseline,
train 84.3% / test 87.4%, longs 84.8% and shorts 85.4% both positive. A fresh
ES session extreme before an NQ entry is **broad-tape confirmation of the
move** (ES leads, the NQ breakout resolves it) — the exact opposite of a
stand-aside reason.

**Adopted as a tier-up label `BROAD CONFIRM`** — the card prints it when ES
made a fresh session extreme in the 5 bars before entry. Journaled like every
threshold: it earns a higher baseline only after ~100 live instances.

## 3. ES delta sign — one robust rule (shorts vs negative delta)

Sign of ES cumulative delta at the flush bar. Cross-window consistency
(Jun–Sep 2024 · Jan–Aug 2025 · 2026 test):

| Cell | window 1 | window 2 | final test | all-time |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **neg × short** | 62.2% | 66.4% | **67.8%** (n=90) | 70.2% (n=369) |
| pos × short | 78.9% | 64.5% | 76.0% (n=208) | 73.3% |
| pos × long | 72.9% | 75.8% | **82.5%** (n=212) | 78.2% |
| neg × long | 73.6% | 76.2% | 79.4% (n=97) | 77.3% |

**neg × short is the worst cell in every single window** — the one
cross-window-robust delta rule. Story: NQ rallying while the broad tape
distributes = genuine rotation into tech; fading it (the short card) fails.
pos × long only separated in the 2026 window — not robust.

**Candidate: a warning chip (not a hard veto) on short cards when ES
cum-delta < 0 at the flush.** Hard veto only after live journaling confirms
the 67.8% test read.

## 4. RS band — coherent stretch-fade pattern

NQ−ES points-spread z-score, trailing 60 min at entry (test window):

| Cell | test WR | n | vs mirror |
|---|---|---|---|
| **weak × long** | **84.2%** | 292 | strong × long 79.7% |
| **strong × short** | **84.0%** | 418 | neutral × short 80.1% |
| neutral × long | 82.9% | 1,041 | |
| weak × short | 81.1% | 719 | |

Both winning cells tell the same story: the card pays when NQ has been
**stretched against the trade direction** for the past hour (longs after NQ
underperformed ES; shorts after NQ outperformed) — fading the relative
stretch, not chasing it. Both hold in test with real n and a coherent
mechanism. The earlier small-sample scare (weak-long "69.7%") is dead at
scale.

**Candidate tier labels: `RS STRETCH` on weak-long / strong-short cards.**
Journal-only for now.

---

## Verdicts

| Feature | Verdict |
|---|---|
| Flush agreement | not adopted (monitor agree-long) |
| ES fresh extreme before entry | **ADOPT as `BROAD CONFIRM` tier-up label** |
| ES delta negative × short | candidate warning chip (journal first) |
| RS stretch (weak-long, strong-short) | candidate tier labels (journal first) |

One adoption, three monitored candidates, and a rejected gate that became the
adoption — the numbers did their job before anything touched the live feed.
Nothing here votes direction or fires a card; ES remains context/tier only.

*Educational research only — not financial advice.*

# All strategies — unified results (2026-10-05)

One uniform treatment across every bar-based strategy family in the
codebase, so families are directly comparable: own signal stop (entry −
1×risk where the detector stores no stop) · 1R target · 60-bar time exit
· 0.5pt round trip · sequential one-trade-at-a-time per family · all 649
sessions (Dec 2023 → Oct 2026). `web/scripts/allStrategiesStudy.ts`.

| Family | Signals | Trades | WR | PF | Net pts | expR | 2024 | 2025 | 2026 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| momentum (failed-flush) | 2,121 | 1,559 | 75.4% | 2.71 | 3,394 | +0.44 | 76.6% | 72.1% | 78.8% |
| expansion (huge-bar) | 4,909 | 2,935 | 77.4% | 2.97 | 7,344 | +0.47 | 78.4% | 75.5% | 78.9% |
| mom+exp (time-ordered, live) | 7,030 | 3,171 | 76.7% | 2.86 | 7,565 | +0.46 | 77.4% | 75.0% | 78.2% |
| mom+exp (optimizer order) | 7,030 | 2,326 | 76.4% | 2.86 | 5,456 | +0.46 | 75.9% | 74.3% | 79.9% |
| rth soft-continuation | 10,860 | 2,794 | 76.9% | **3.22** | 12,250 | +0.51 | 76.0% | 77.9% | 77.4% |
| open drive | 554 | 554 | 69.5% | 2.21 | 7,116 | +0.37 | 65.2% | 68.2% | 76.7% |
| open pullback | 460 | 330 | 67.3% | 2.06 | 1,807 | +0.34 | 61.5% | 70.2% | 75.8% |
| open sniper | 167 | 167 | 81.4% | 4.17 | 1,964 | +0.60 | 77.6% | 75.0% | 97.6% |
| sweep-reclaim v2 | 17,358 | 7,064 | 54.8% | 1.10 | 3,596 | +0.05 | 54.9% | 53.7% | 55.8% |
| balance break | 4,140 | 3,207 | 52.0% | 1.05 | 1,464 | +0.02 | 51.3% | 51.7% | 53.8% |

## Which family is which

- **momentum (failed-flush)** — the flagship LVN-reversal scalp: a flush
  below a level that fails and reclaims with a one-sided bar. Live.
- **expansion (huge-bar)** — the huge-bar breakout trigger. Live.
- **mom+exp** — the pair the feed actually trades; the second row is the
  same pair in time order (what a real feed executes), the third is the
  mom-first order all the optimization studies used (reproduces the
  published baseline n=2,326 / 76.4% / 2.86 exactly).
- **rth soft-continuation** — 9:30+ continuation of the overnight trend.
  Live but tagged experimental; highest PF of the live families.
- **open drive / pullback / sniper** — first-hour open plays (sniper is a
  resting-limit variant). Gated by FEED_* env; sniper's 81.4%/4.17 sits on
  only 167 trades (2026 WR 97.6% — small-sample, treat with suspicion).
- **sweep-reclaim v2** — liquidity-sweep reversal. Research-only; at 1R
  it is a coin flip minus costs (PF 1.10, expR +0.05) — matches its own
  study's verdict.
- **balance break** — failed balance-area breakout. Research-only;
  PF 1.05, expR +0.02 — no edge at 1R (its own study found the edge only
  in narrow counter-side cells).
- **absorption / one-sided reclaim** (footprint-based, separate pipeline,
  not in this run) — published: aligned stack ~45% WR / PF ~2.2
  (docs/research/FOOTPRINT_REVERSAL_RESEARCH.md).
- **options/gamma and price-action location** — context boxes, not trade
  strategies.

## Cost reality check

All numbers above are at 0.5pt. At the measured live cost (0.95pt),
expR +0.02–0.05 families (sweep-reclaim, balance break) go NEGATIVE —
they sit below the cost floor entirely. The viable families at real
costs are momentum/expansion/RTH (expR +0.44–0.51 gross of sizing).

## Where the optimization fits

The entire sizing/stop/target campaign (sizing-optimizer doc) applies to
the **mom+exp pair only** — that is the live-traded family. Baseline
76.4% / PF 2.86 / $160,711 → new pick (0.35× stop · 2.25R · 60-bar) at
×2 under measured costs: 69.2% / PF 2.78 / $359,716 PASS.

entry-quality-study:
# Winner/loser atlas — session delta, session-extreme targets, and the loss anatomy

> First measurement pass over the full NQ archive: **649 sessions** (2023-12-18
> → 2026-10-05), the three production families replayed with their live plan
> shapes (MOM failed-flush 1R · EXP huge-bar expansion 1R · RTH soft 0.75R;
> first-touch, 60-bar time exit, 0.5 pt cost, sequential one-trade-at-a-time),
> canonical split 2026-01-01. Machinery: `web/scripts/winnerLoserAtlas.ts`
> (archive replay + per-trade session context, CSV dump at
> `docs/data/winner-loser-atlas-2026-10-05.csv`) and `web/scripts/winnerLoserLive.ts`
> (the same features recomputed on the reconciled live `trades` rows in Neon).
>
> Session context is computed lookahead-free at the entry bar: cumulative
> buy−sell since the session open and the session high/low **at entry time**.
> Cells: "agrees/against" = trade direction vs the sign of session cumΔ;
> "ATH-retest" = |target − session extreme| ≤ 0.5 with the target NOT beyond
> it; "fresh-air" = target beyond the session extreme by > 0.25 pts.
>
> **Headline:** (1) gating a direction against the session cumulative delta
> buys nothing — pooled 79.8% WR / +2.99 pts vs 79.7% / +2.90, and in the
> flush family counter-delta is the *better* cell; (2) the dangerous target
> is not the "not defined" fresh-air high — it is the **exact ATH retest**
> (target sitting on the session extreme, pooled +0.70 vs +2.96 baseline,
> weak in all three families, and *no* exit management — including
> breakeven-at-1R — rescues it); fresh-air targets are fine to best, and
> only MOM's fresh-air cell profits from a BE@1R runner (+0.18); (3) the
> dominant loss mode everywhere is the stop-run — 60–72% of stop-outs print
> a return beyond the entry within 10 bars, and 0% of losing trades ever
> touched +1R first, so breakeven ladders can only ever change winners, never
> rescue losers.

---

## 1. Q1 — should a direction against the session cumΔ be gated? No.

| Cell | MOM flush 1R | EXP expansion 1R | RTH soft 0.75R |
|---|---|---|---|
| ALL | 1,559 · 75.4% · +2.18 | 2,935 · 77.4% · +2.50 | 2,794 · 84.6% · +3.86 |
| agrees w/ cumΔ | 75.1% · +2.15 | 77.2% · +2.52 | **85.2% · +3.97** |
| against cumΔ | **75.9% · +2.21** | **77.8% · +2.48** | 83.8% · +3.72 |
| strongest-against (Δ ≤ −800 vs dir) | 75.3% · +2.16 | 78.5% · +2.61 | 83.3% · +3.67 |
| veto against, \|Δ\| ≥ 400 | Δexp +0.01 | Δexp +0.01 | Δexp +0.12 (test 4.27 → **4.22**) |

Pooled: agrees n=4,198 +2.99 vs against n=3,090 +2.90 — flat. The flush
family is the cleanest statement: a failed-flush long is *by construction* a
counter-delta trade (sellers dominated the session, yet failed to break the
low), and it is the best cell. Even the extreme bands (session delta ≥ 800
against the trade) carry family-average expectancy. The only family with a
visible gap (RTH, +0.25 exp) does not survive the train/test split when the
veto is applied — test expectancy goes **down** (4.27 → 4.22).

The live tape agrees: on 2026-10-01 the session cumΔ ran from −717 to
−7,464, and the 12 winners were mostly counter-delta **longs** (only 4/12
agreed) while 13 of 19 losses were with-delta shorts.

**Verdict: no gate.** Consistent with `counterBiasVeto.ts` (day-bias veto
≈ 0) and the ES Δ− chip being a journal label, never a gate. Keep cumΔ as a
journal chip; do not filter on it.

## 2. Q2 — target at the session high/low: two cells, opposite answers

| Cell | MOM | EXP | RTH | pooled |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **ATH-retest** (target ON the extreme ±0.5) | 27 · 63.0% · +0.75 | 37 · 62.2% · +0.84 | 44 · 70.5% · +0.55 | **108 · 65.7% · +0.70** |
| **fresh-air** (target beyond by > 0.25) | 231 · 77.5% · **+2.81** | 436 · 75.0% · +2.26 | 0 | 667 · 75.9% · +2.45 |
| inside range (baseline reference) | 75.2% · +2.08 | 78.0% · +2.56 | 84.7% · +3.89 | +2.96 (all trades) |

The user's instinct is half right. **"Session all-time high" = the exact
retest** — price has been rejected at that level all session — is a genuinely
weak cell in every family (WR −15 pp, expectancy +0.55–0.84 vs family
baselines of +2.2–3.9). It is rare (~1.5% of trades, n=108 pooled). **The
"not defined high" = fresh air** is the opposite: not dangerous at all, and
for the MOM flush family it is the single best cell in the whole family
(+2.81, PF 3.27).

Management variants on each cell (0.5 pt cost, 60-bar exit):

| Variant | MOM ATH-retest | MOM fresh-air | EXP ATH-retest | EXP fresh-air | RTH ATH-retest |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| base (fixed target) | +0.75 | +2.81 | +0.84 | +2.26 | +0.55 |
| target capped @extreme | +0.71 | +2.65 | +0.80 | +2.22 | +0.54 |
| early bank 0.5R | +0.66 | +1.27 | +0.77 | +1.13 | **−0.11** |
| early bank 0.75R | +0.02 | +2.16 | +0.45 | +1.91 | +0.55 |
| runner BE@1R ladder | **−0.14** | **+2.98** | +0.04 | +1.83 | +0.61 |
| ½ fixed + ½ runner | +0.31 | +2.90 | +0.44 | +2.05 | +0.58 |

- **Nothing rescues the ATH-retest cell.** Capping, early banking, and
  breakeven ladders all leave it at +0.0…+0.8 — and the BE@1R runner makes
  MOM's cell *negative*. The breakeven idea cannot work there because the
  losers never get near 1R: 0% of stop-outs touched +1R first (see §3).
  The right "care" is recognizing the cell and skipping or sizing down —
  it is a ~1.5%-frequency drag of ~0.03 pts/trade overall, so the cheapest
  correct action is journal-awareness, not new machinery.
- **Fresh air needs no extra care.** MOM fresh-air is the family's best
  cell; the only variant that adds to it is the BE@1R runner (+2.98,
  +0.18). EXP fresh-air is mildly below family (+2.26 vs +2.50) and every
  variant makes it worse — leave it at the fixed target. RTH never prints
  a fresh-air target (0.75R target, n=0).
- Breakeven-at-1R is therefore **not a general loss-saver** — see §3.

## 3. Q3 — winner vs loser atlas

**Loss anatomy (the single biggest pattern).** Every stop-out bar in all
three families was checked for a 10-bar return beyond the entry:

| Family | stop-outs | run-back ≤10 bars | touched +0.5R first | touched +1R first |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| MOM flush | 383 | **65%** | 54% | 0% |
| EXP expansion | 659 | **60%** | 62% | 0% |
| RTH soft | 430 | **72%** | 26% | 0% |

Live 2026-10-01: 11 of 19 losses were labeled stop-runs (58%). Two
consequences: (a) the tape runs our stops ~2/3 of the time — this is the
background behind the stop-run studies, and widening stops was already
measured to buy ~0 (the run-back does not convert into expectancy);
(b) **no losing trade ever reached +1R first**, so breakeven-at-1R can only
ever convert *winners* into runners — it is a winner-management tool, not a
loss filter. MOM/EXP losers reach ~half-R then reverse (median MFE +0.54R /
+0.63R); RTH losers mostly die on the very next bar (median held 1 bar, only
26% touched +0.5R).

**Feature medians, winners vs losers** (readable per family in the script
output; the durable signals):

- MOM `deltaFromFlush`: winners **+10** vs losers **−28** — in the flush
  family, losers have order-flow delta *bleeding against the trade* between
  the flush and the entry bar (RTH mirrors: −22 vs −85).
- RTH candle quality: losers have smaller `breakRangeR` (1.23 vs 1.38),
  lower `atr14` (9 vs 10), tighter `riskPts` (7.25 vs 8.38) — the weak-bar
  RTH trades lose; the ≥1.0×ATR gate is doing real work.
- EXP `distToExt`: losers 28.5 vs winners 32.6 — expansion trades fired
  closer to the session extreme lose more often (same story as the
  fresh-air/ATH-retest split).

**Cells:**

- **Shorts are the weaker side only in MOM** (72.9% / +1.90 vs longs 78.0% /
  +2.46); EXP and RTH sides are near-equal (RTH long 85.7% / short 83.5%).
- **Tuesday is the weakest day in all three families** (pooled +2.65 vs
  +3.04 on other days; MOM +2.01, EXP +2.36, RTH +3.28 — each below its
  family mean). Friday is MOM-weak (+1.83) but fine for EXP/RTH. Monday is
  strong for MOM/EXP — consistent with `seasonal-almanac-2026-10-05.md`.
- **After-loss trades are not worse** (pooled +2.92 vs +2.82 after a win;
  MOM +2.57 after a loss vs +2.00 after a win). Longest same-day losing
  streak per family: 3–4. No revenge-trade penalty — shrinking after losses
  buys nothing (matches `sizing-dynamics-2026-10-02.md`).
- **First RTH card of the day is disproportionately good** (+5.33 vs +3.86);
  MOM/EXP first-of-day ≈ average.
- EXP **close bucket** (16:00–17:00 ET) is the family's weak bucket
  (67.1% WR, +1.42, n=74) — already reflected in `ticketVeto.ts`
  (`momentum_expansion/close/short` +0.75); the atlas says the whole close
  bucket is weak, not just shorts.

## 4. Standing caveats

1. This is a **scratch sweep, not a validation**: no account sim, and the
   veto rows are filter-only (the occupancy effect of removing a trade is
   not replayed — same limitation as `counterBiasVeto.ts`).
2. Small cells: ATH-retest n = 27/37/44 per family (108 pooled) — the
   direction is consistent across all three families, but per-family Wilson
   CIs are wide.
3. Same house rules as every replay: first-touch scoring, 0.5 pt cost,
   pessimistic same-bar stop-first exits, mid-price for archive closes.

*Educational research only — not financial advice.*
context-veto-stoprun:
# Context vetoes + stop-run study (2026-10-02)

Follow-up on trade-review findings #2 (expansion context filter) and #3
(stop-run clustering). Method: the same 648-session archive (2023-12 →
2026-09), lookahead-free, sequential one-trade-at-a-time replay, first-touch
scoring, 0.5 pt round-trip cost, 60-bar time exit, train/test split
2026-01-01, MFF Rapid EOD 50k account sim. Runners:
`scripts/momentumStudy.ts --mode veto` and `scripts/stopRunStudy.ts`.

## 1. Expansion context vetoes — REJECTED (all variants)

The 22:50 (counter-trend short) and 00:41 (double-top long) losses suggested
three gates: session cumulative-delta agreement, session-VWAP side, and a
swing-extreme (double-top) veto. All measured in the replay:

| Variant | n | WR | PF | expR | Total $ |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| exp base | 4,845 | 78.1% | 3.06 | 0.45 | $361,100 |
| exp+cumD | 2,874 | 77.7% | 2.98 | 0.44 | $210,975 |
| exp+vwap | 2,999 | 77.4% | 2.93 | 0.44 | $216,485 |
| exp+both | 2,308 | 77.3% | 2.93 | 0.44 | $166,487 |
| exp+swing.25 | 2,542 | 76.9% | 2.81 | 0.43 | $179,631 |
| exp+swing.5 | 2,492 | 76.8% | 2.81 | 0.43 | $176,014 |

**Every veto removes trades at or ABOVE the survivors' quality.** The removed
subsets had higher win rates than the kept trades (e.g. the swing-vetoed
double-top entries went ~79% — the tape *rewards* a huge one-sided bar at a
clean double top). The huge-bar continuation edge does not care about session
trend, VWAP position, or double tops. The two review losses were in-model
noise, exactly as suspected. `EXP_PROD` stays unchanged; the knobs
(`sessionTrend`, `swingVetoTolPts`) remain for future sweeps.

## 2. Flush-trigger overhead veto — per-trade gain, volume cost

The 21:18 case (breakout into overhead congestion) operationalized as
`requireTrailProgress`: the breakout bar must clear the trailing N-bar high
(long) / low (short):

| Variant | n | WR | PF | expR | Total $ |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| mom base | 2,106 | 75.7% | 2.72 | 0.40 | $138,306 |
| mom+trail20 | 1,296 | 77.1% | 2.95 | 0.43 | $91,393 |
| mom+trail60 | 744 | 76.1% | 2.88 | 0.41 | $50,139 |
| mom+trail120 | 543 | 77.5% | 3.25 | 0.44 | $39,330 |

trail20 is the only veto in the whole study that isolates a genuinely worse
subset: the 810 vetoed trades averaged 1.82 pts vs 2.32 for the survivors,
and the vetoed group carried the 21:18-style losses. Per-trade expectancy
improves +7.5%, test PF 3.23 → 3.46. But it removes 39% of flush cards and
33% of flush dollars — at fixed 9-contract sizing that is real income lost.
**Verdict: opt-in quality filter (`requireTrailProgress: true`), not a
default.** trail60/120 cut further with no per-trade gain — reject.

## 3. Stop-run clustering + padding — the 3-of-5 night was noise

Every stopped trade measured for stopDepth (pts probed beyond the stop) and
postStopFav (pts run back in the trade direction over the next 30 bars).
A "stop-run" = depth ≤ 0.75 (stopped at the tick) AND fav ≥ 1R.

- **Stop-runs are 5% of stops** for both triggers — and that share is flat
  at every reversal threshold (0.5R–2R). The 19:15 / 00:41 / 01:27 pattern
  is a small-sample anecdote, not a systematic leak.
- **No hour clustering.** Run share by hour: 00:00 6%, 01:00 5%, 02:00 2%
  vs 5% overall — the 00:00–02:00 ET hypothesis is rejected. (16:00 shows
  13% on 24 stops — the EOD close hour, thin and near-zero dollars.)
- **Padding does not pay, anywhere.** WR and PF degrade monotonically with
  pad size (exp: 78.1/3.06 at 0.5 → 71.7/2.27 at 1.5), per-trade expectancy
  falls (2.48 → 2.03 pts), and the worst-day tail gets WORSE (exp pad 1.0:
  −$974 vs −$704; night 1.5: −$1,190). The hour-conditional night pad
  (00–02 ET) moved net +1.1–1.5% at the cost of WR — noise, with a worse
  tail. The structural stop at pad 0.5 is the measured optimum; the
  "safe ticks come from the 80% hit rates, not from widening" line in the
  playbook is now confirmed by a dedicated sweep.

Side-finding: flush **shorts** are the weakest cell in the whole study
(72.7% WR, PF 2.32 vs flush longs 78.6/3.24) — same disease as the retired
sweep-reclaim fade. A direction/context study for flush shorts is the next
candidate, not stop placement.

## Implemented

- `lib/momentum.ts`: `ExpansionConfig.sessionTrend` ("none"|"cumDelta"|
  "vwap"|"both"), `swingVetoTolPts`, `swingLookback`; `MomConfig.
  requireTrailProgress` + `trailProgBars`; `stopPadNight` on both (the
  hour-conditional pad, off by default). Expansion signals now carry real
  session `cumDelta` / `distVwapPts`.
- `scripts/momentumStudy.ts`: `--mode veto` variant family.
- `scripts/stopRunStudy.ts`: the clustering + pad-sweep runner.
- Tests: 5 new unit tests in `tests/momentum.test.ts` (all 25 pass).
- **Prod configs unchanged** — `EXP_PROD` and `MOM_PROD` behave exactly as
  before; every gate here is opt-in.

# HTF counter-trend shorts — "are the losing shorts really bullish-pullback shorts?" (2026-10-02)

The question from the trade logs: *several losing trades looked like shorts taken on
longer-timeframe bullish pullbacks — can we improve that?*

**TL;DR.** The instinct is right about the *cell* but wrong about the *fix*.
Shorts fired while the higher-timeframe trend is bullish are the weakest short
cell in the whole system (and they do get stop-run more), but over 649 sessions /
12,460 sequential trades that cell still wins **80.6%** with PF 3.20 — the huge-bar
continuation trigger is regime-robust. **Every hard veto tested removes a
profitable subset of trades and costs money.** The live losses were a small-sample
streak (the two sessions in the logs were one-way +110 pt / +250 pt up tapes) plus
execution leaks that are already fixed (absolute brackets, verified re-send). The
improvements that *do* pay: regime-aware sizing (optional), an early-Globex short
discipline (new finding), regime context printed on the trade card, and one opt-in
quality knob for the worst sub-cell — not a veto.

Data: live audit `web/scripts/htfTrendLive.ts`; replay `web/scripts/htfRegimeStudy.ts`
(649-session R2 archive, lookahead-free, sequential one-trade-at-a-time, first-touch
scoring, 0.5 pt cost, 60-bar time exit, train/test split 2026-01-01, MFF Rapid EOD
50k sim). External evidence: `htf-trend-filter-research.md`.

---

## 1. The live logs — what actually happened

25 matched live trades (Oct 1 Globex + Oct 2 RTH). Regime = 15m EMA20 vs EMA50
(slope-confirmed) + price vs 1m EMA200, computed from the archive tape at entry.

| Cell (live) | n | W | L | WR | gross $ |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| short, HTF bullish (BULL15 + above EMA200) | 4 | 1 | 3 | **25%** | **−$305** |
| short, HTF mixed | 9 | 4 | 3 | 44% | +$89 |
| long, HTF bullish | 5 | 2 | 3 | 40% | −$160 |
| long, HTF mixed | 7 | 5 | 0 | 71% | +$732 |

The six losing shorts, with their regime context at entry:

| # | ET | family | regime read at entry | $ | note |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 7 | 22:50 | expansion | **BULL15**, slope +16, above EMA200 & VWAP, sess +81 pts | −200.5 | textbook counter-trend short at the top of a one-way up night |
| 11 | 01:27 | flush | **BULL15**, above VWAP, ret240 +70 | −130.0 | would have WON with the structural stop (bracket-anchoring leak, now fixed) |
| 37 | 10:46 | RTH | **BULL15**, above EMA200, prevRangePos 1.99 (2 ranges above prior day) | −118.5 | short into a parabolic +250 pt up day |
| 65 | 11:46 | RTH | mixed 15m, above VWAP, 1h drop in an up day | −49.5 | hit target *then* stopped — stop-run |
| 74 | 13:14 | RTH | bearish 4h (ret240 −104), below EMA200/VWAP | −220.5 | NOT a bull-pullback short — bear continuation squeezed (flushVol 1047) |
| 292 | 14:38 | RTH | bearish (ret240 −224, below EMA200) | −99.0 | not a bull-pullback short either |

**Verdict on the live sample: 3 of 6 losing shorts were clean counter-trend shorts
in a bullish HTF (4 of 6 if #65 counts), and they were the expensive ones.** But n=4
is noise: the replay says that exact cell wins ~78–80%.

## 2. The replay truth — 12,460 sequential trades, 649 sessions

Baseline (flush + expansion + RTH soft, prod configs, sequential):

| cell | n | WR | PF | expR | net |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| long \| BEAR15 | 1,936 | 84.0% | 4.05 | 0.44 | +6,940 |
| long \| BULL15 | 3,018 | 82.7% | 3.73 | 0.41 | +9,096 |
| long \| MIXED | 1,143 | 84.8% | 4.18 | 0.46 | +3,907 |
| short \| BEAR15 | 2,119 | 81.9% | 3.52 | 0.40 | +7,239 |
| **short \| BULL15** | 2,861 | **80.6%** | **3.20** | **0.37** | +7,976 |
| short \| MIXED | 1,156 | 79.4% | 3.15 | 0.36 | +3,540 |
| short \| EARLY (first ~75 min) | 110 | **73.6%** | **2.30** | 0.37 | +224 |

The asymmetry is real but modest: counter-trend shorts lose ~1.3 pts of WR and
~0.03R of expectancy vs with-trend shorts — **every cell remains strongly positive.**
The same gradient holds per family (expansion: shorts 82.5% bear / 79.3% bull;
flush: 73.3% / 73.0%) and on the daily axis:

| daily context, shorts | n | WR | PF |
|---|---|---|---|
| gap up (open above prior close) | 3,598 | 79.9% | 3.15 |
| gap flat/down | 2,648 | 81.8% | 3.47 |
| gap up + BULL15 | 1,665 | 79.6% | 3.07 |
| gap up + BULL15 + **below VWAP** | 127 | **71.7%** | **2.21** |
| BULL15 + below VWAP | 214 | 73.4% | 2.57 |

**The genuinely weak sub-cells (still net-positive):**

1. **Shorts below session VWAP while the 15m trend is bullish** — "shorting the
   pullback below value in an uptrend": 73.4% WR, PF 2.57 (214 trades). With a
   daily gap up on top: 71.7%, PF 2.21 (127 trades). This is the closest
   operational match to the user's hypothesis.
2. **EARLY-regime shorts** — first ~75 min of the Globex session (before the 15m
   regime can even form): 73.6% WR, 26.4% stop rate, **9.1% tick-stop rate**
   (vs 3.3% for bear-regime shorts).
3. **Hour pattern for shorts (momentum hours):** 18:00 ET 70.2% · 19:00 72.8% ·
   20:00 65.3% · 21:00 70.3% · 22:00 73.2% · 23:00 73.6% — the first four Globex
   hours are the weakest for shorts (plus the thin 16:00 EOD hour at 65.9%).
4. **Trendless (MIXED) shorts:** 79.4% overall; within flush-only, 69.5% — choppy
   tape without a clean 15m trend is worse for shorts than a clean bull trend.

**Stop-run asymmetry (the "it always stops me out" feeling is partly real):**
tick-stop share (stopped within 10% of the stop) by cell — short|BULL15 **4.5%** vs
short|BEAR15 3.3% and long|BULL15 3.7% vs long|BEAR15 2.7%. Counter-trend shorts get
tick-stopped ~36% more often — consistent with the external evidence (stops cluster
just beyond obvious levels; counter-trend stops are the liquidity the trend feeds on).
Still, 4.5% ≠ a leak; the stop-run clustering study already showed pad increases
make the tail worse, so the 0.5 pt pad stays.

## 3. Would a veto help? No — every veto removes profitable trades

Same replay, shorts skipped pre-scoring (lane freed for the next signal — honest):

| variant | n | WR (all) | WR (test) | PF (test) | vetoed subset | total $ |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| base | 12,460 | 82.0% | 83.1% | 3.78 | — | 818,347 |
| noShortBull15 | 9,977 | 82.3% | 82.9% | 3.73 | 3,333 trades, **80.6% WR**, +9,214 pts | 667,047 |
| noShortBull15+A200 | 10,435 | 82.1% | 82.7% | 3.70 | 2,735 trades, **81.1% WR** | 693,963 |
| noShortPullbackUp (ret60<0, ret240>0) | 11,674 | 82.0% | 83.0% | 3.77 | 1,157 trades, **81.5% WR** | 765,035 |
| noShortBelowE20Bull | 12,193 | 82.2% | 83.2% | 3.80 | 496 trades, **77.0% WR** | 804,556 |
| noShortMixed | 11,624 | 82.3% | 83.0% | 3.72 | 1,429 trades, 78.8% WR | 770,121 |
| noShortVwapBelow | 10,064 | 82.5% | **83.9%** | **3.99** | 3,226 trades, 79.7% WR | 671,375 |
| noShortVwapBelowBull | 12,278 | 82.2% | 83.3% | 3.82 | 300 trades, **75.3% WR** | 811,264 |
| noShortCumD>0 | 9,921 | 82.2% | 82.5% | 3.65 | 3,451 trades, 80.2% WR | 659,447 |

**Every vetoed subset is profitable — most at 75–81% WR.** Skipping them converts
$15k–$150k of income into "quality" that is barely measurable per-trade. The only
variant with a better test profile (noShortVwapBelow) still throws away $147k.
This is the same verdict as the earlier session-trend veto study
(`context-veto-stoprun-2026-10-02.md`: cumDelta/VWAP gates rejected for
expansion) — the huge-bar continuation edge does not care about the regime it fires
in, because it is *momentum continuation*, not a discretionary fade. A 79% cell in a
bull tape is not the same trade as the discretionary counter-trend fade the
literature warns about (see §5).

## 4. Size instead of skip — the knob that actually trades risk for income

Same trades, weak-tier shorts at half size (dollarize at 50% of the $170 budget):

| variant | net $ | worst day | max DD (eval) |
|---|---|---|---|
| size base | 818,347 | −776 (2024-10-17) | −776 |
| halfShortBull15 | 732,289 | **−598** | −601 |
| halfShortBull15+A200 | 748,345 | −731 | −731 |
| halfShortVwapBelow | 731,313 | −658 | −658 |
| halfShortVwapBelowBull | 813,807 | −776 | −776 |
| halfWeakShortTier (bull+<VWAP ∪ trendless shorts) | 780,192 | −776 | −776 |
| halfShortPullbackUp | 787,965 | −687 | −687 |
| zeroWeakShortTier | 742,036 | −776 | −776 |

Half-sizing *all* BULL15 shorts shaves the worst day 23% (−776 → −598) at a −10.5%
income cost. Half-sizing only the narrow weak tier (bull + below-VWAP) costs <1% of
income with no measurable tail change. Given the prop floor ($2,000 EOD-trailing vs
−$776 worst day), the base sizing is the right default — the half-size knob exists
for psychological smoothing, not because the account needs it.

## 5. Why the literature expects this pattern (external research)

Full citations in `htf-trend-filter-research.md`. The condensed logic:

- **Trend alignment is the default edge.** Time-series momentum is positive in
  essentially every futures market for 100+ years (Moskowitz–Ooi–Pedersen 2012;
  Hurst et al. 2017). Intraday continuation is measurable too (Gao et al. 2018:
  first half-hour predicts last half-hour). AQR's "Hold the Dip": 196 systematic
  buy-the-dip variants ALL underperform; dip-buying is "usually positioned opposite
  momentum". Estrada (155 years): returns after down months are *lower* than
  average (9.1% vs 11.0%). So the prior that counter-trend entries are worse is
  sound — and our data shows the same direction, just with a much smaller
  magnitude than the literature's cross-sectional effect, because our entries are
  momentum-triggered (huge one-sided bar), not discretionary fades.
- **Mechanics of why counter-trend shorts bleed:** passive absorption at pullback
  lows (Bookmap), buyers happy to pay up through a pullback (Axia CVD divergence),
  and stop cascades — stops are positive-feedback orders that cluster and fire in
  waves (Osler, NY Fed SR 150; Cont–Kukanov–Stoikov). Our tick-stop table (§2)
  shows the same signature: bull-regime shorts get tick-stopped ~36% more often.
- **How professionals handle it:** on trend days, trade with-trend only (Axia,
  SMB); counter-trend only with multi-clue confluence (Axia open-drive short needed
  3+ stacked context clues). Quant systems implement it as a regime *gate*, but the
  gates in the literature exist for setups that are already marginal — our cells
  are 73–85% WR, which is why the gates don't pay here.
- **Validation discipline:** the marginal test used here (does the veto remove a
  genuinely worse subset? does it hold on the test split?) is exactly the
  anti-overfit protocol the literature prescribes (Bailey et al. PBO; walk-forward
  folds; treat regime as a sticky 5m/15m state, not a 1m signal). We also inherit
  the repo's walk-forward rule for auto-applied insights.

## 6. What to actually do (ranked)

1. **Do not veto counter-trend shorts.** They are ~80% WR with PF 3.2 and
   contribute +7,976 pts. The two review nights were a one-way-tape streak + leaks
   now fixed (absolute structural brackets, verified re-send, stale-entry guard).
2. **Early-Globex short discipline (new finding, strongest actionable).** Shorts
   in the first ~75 min of the session (EARLY regime: 73.6% WR, 26% stops, 9.1%
   tick-stops) and broadly 18:00–21:00 ET (65–73% WR) are the weakest shorts in the
   system — worse than bull-regime shorts. Options: (a) `hour_veto` override for
   momentum shorts 18:00–19:15 ET (opt-in, dashboard-approvable today); (b) require
   A+ overlap (flush+expansion same bar) for shorts before 19:15; (c) half-size.
   This matches the existing first-of-day research direction and is backed by the
   replay hour table.
3. **Regime-aware half-size knob (optional, default OFF).** Add a `size_scale`
   gate to `web/lib/strategyOverrides.ts` (value `{ scale: 0.5, side: "short",
   on: "bull15_belowVwap" }`). Data: halfShortBull15 −10.5% income for −23% worst
   day; the narrow tier costs <1%. Activate only if the trader wants smoothing.
4. **Print the regime on the card.** The momentum/RTH card should carry the HTF
   context the trader is missing when the alert fires: `HTF: BULL15 (15m EMA20>
   EMA50) · above/below session VWAP · gap direction vs prior close` plus a
   `counter-trend short — consider half size` tag for the bull+below-VWAP cell.
   Small `signalText.ts`/`mechanism.ts` addition; no behavior change. This directly
   answers "I feel like…" by making the context explicit per card.
5. **Feed the regime features to the nightly miner.** Persist `htfRegime` (15m EMA
   state, VWAP side, gap, early flag) onto `trades.features` so
   `strategyInsights.ts` can propose trend-filter/hour-veto rules with evidence;
   its walk-forward gate already protects against overfit auto-application.
6. **Opt-in quality knob (precedent: `requireTrailProgress`).** A
   `counterTrendShortGuard` config on the detectors: skip shorts when
   gap-up + BULL15 + below VWAP (127 trades, 71.7% WR, PF 2.21 — the one cell
   where the vetoed subset is clearly worse than the kept set). The measured
   wider version (bull + below-VWAP, 300 trades, 75.3% WR) saves ~$7k over
   2.75y at 2.4% signal cost — a quality filter for the ugliest sub-cell,
   default OFF in prod configs, exposed as a lab variant.
7. **Keep journaling.** The live journal (31 trades) is still inside the model's
   noise band; the 80.6% cell produces 3–5 loss streaks routinely. The
   `htfTrendLive.ts` audit is re-runnable after any night
   (`node --import scripts/ts-loader.mjs ./scripts/htfTrendLive.ts`).

## 7. Method notes and caveats

- Archive minutes carry high/low and buy/sell only (no true o/c); every price used
  is the mid, same as the lab. MFE/MAE and tick-stop proxies inherit that.
- 15m EMA regime requires ≥5 completed 15m buckets (75 min); earlier trades are
  tagged EARLY instead of classified — which itself surfaced the early-session
  finding (a benefit, not a bug).
- The replay is per-session (no cross-session state), so "HTF" here means intraday
  session structure (15m EMA / EMA200 / session VWAP / prior-day gap) — the honest
  higher timeframes available to a Globex scalper. A true daily-candle trend
  (e.g., 20-day SMA on daily closes) is NOT yet measurable from the archive and is
  the natural follow-up if deeper history arrives (Databento/CME).
- Train/test split 2026-01-01 throughout; the walk-forward gate in the miner is the
  production guard for any auto-applied rule.

## Files

- `web/scripts/htfTrendLive.ts` — live-trade HTF audit (runs against Neon `trades`
  + R2 archive).
- `web/scripts/htfRegimeStudy.ts` — full regime + veto + sizing study
  (`--include-rth`, `--dump`, `--max`, `--split` supported).
- `htf-trend-filter-research.md` — external literature review (subagent
  research, all claims cited).

# Full-gates replay — cap sweep + counter-gate under the whole live rule stack (2026-10-08)

Scratch: `web/scripts/fullGatesScratch.ts` (untracked). 651 sessions, 10,814
cards, live-style brackets (limit TTL 9m, 0.5× stop, 2.5R target, HORIZON 60).
Sequencing order per day: news blackout (newsGate 2026 calendar) → signal
window (marketHours + 2026 holidays) → one-position-at-a-time (blocked cards
DROPPED forever, not re-simulated) → RTH cap → counter-gate (winner memory
from the sequenced trades' real exits) → day-plan in $ (daily floor −250,
profit arm +400, give-back, consistency 900; exits always settle). Fees
$1.90/RT included. Account sim: eval RAPID_EOD_50K, chronological.

## A) Cap sweep (counter-gate ON, MIN15/PTS5)

| cap | n | WR | avg pts | PF | net $ (0.95/side) | net $ (1.90/side) | acct total | max dd | eval | day halts floor/arm/giveback/consist |
|-----|---|----|---------|----|-------------------|-------------------|------------|--------|------|-------------------------------------|
| 3 | 1,480 | 37.1% | +1.23 | 1.45 | $6,582 | −$24,534 | $6,582 | −$4,321 | **FAIL** (breach 2024-04-03) | 85 / 18 / 0 / 0 |
| 4 | 1,846 | 37.2% | +1.17 | 1.44 | $6,378 | −$34,800 | — | −$7,016 | FAIL | 130 / 33 / 1 / 1 |
| 5 | 2,103 | 37.6% | +1.17 | 1.46 | $8,498 | −$40,480 | — | −$8,715 | FAIL | 157 / 46 / 4 / 1 |
| 6 | 2,239 | 37.7% | +1.19 | 1.48 | $9,604 | −$43,542 | — | −$9,820 | FAIL | 174 / 55 / 7 / 2 |
| NOCAP | 2,312 | 37.9% | +1.19 | 1.49 | $10,194 | −$45,409 | — | −$9,818 | FAIL (2024-03-14) | 180 / 60 / 10 / 3 |

Every cap config fails the eval on the raw detector tape. Total $ rises with
the cap but max dd rises faster — **cap 3 is the least-worst** (smallest dd,
best PF-per-$, still FAIL).

## B) Counter-gate sensitivity (cap 3 fixed)

OFF, MIN15/PTS5, MIN30/PTS5 are **identical — gate drops = 0 in every run**.
With one-position-at-a-time, a card can only fire ≥60 bars after the prior
FILLED entry, and no winning card ever holds ≥45 bars (466 target-wins,
83 stop-wins, 0 time-exit wins) — so no successor can ever land within
15/30 min of an opposite winner's exit. **In the sequenced world the
counter-gate is structurally inert.** Live has no one-at-a-time block in
checkRth, so live sits in the no-block regime — where the gate skipped
~346 cards and the gated cells underperform baseline (−0.4…−1.1 pts/trade).
The gate-ON decision is therefore live-relevant, zero-effect in this mode.

## Sequencing vs the earlier no-block runs

- 10,814 cards → full-gates accepts only 17–26% (news drops 5 · window 2 ·
  one-at-a-time 4,189–6,704 · cap 0–4,729 · day-plan 68–1,285).
- NOCAP dd: −$16,911 (no-block) → **−$9,818** (full gates cut ~42%).
- cap3 dd: −$3,448 → −$4,321 (slightly worse — the daily floor cuts the
  recovery cards that would have followed a red open).

## Verdict + the real gap

No cap or gate config makes the raw detector tape pass the eval. The live
system DOES pass — because the layers this replay cannot reproduce are the
ones doing the heavy lifting: **strategy overrides** (live trims ~80% of
these cards), the tape gate (meaningless offline — archive bars are
candle-confirmed by definition), and family vetoes. Offline replay validates
the DETECTOR; the live JOURNAL (daybook, liveRescore, winnerLoserLive)
validates the live stack. Decisions kept: cap 3 stays; counter-gate stays ON
(owner-approved, no-block-relevant) — with this document as the honest record
of why each replay regime says what it says.

## Verdict

# RTH limit-entry redesign — 2026-10-06

## Problem

Live RTH soft-continuation trades executed as MARKET entries with brackets
anchored at the SIGNAL price (`CROSSTRADE_REST=1` absolute prices). In a
fast tape the fill drifts from the signal between bar close and dispatch
(measured live 2026-10-06: 19.25 / 10.5 / 2.25 pts on the three RTH cards):

- fill beyond the absolute take-profit → CrossTrade OCO closes instantly
  (the 2026-10-04 failure mode, twice on 2026-10-06) → −0.5/−0.25 scratches;
- fill near the take-profit → target only ~0.75 pts away → fee-eaten
  "win" (−$4.80 net on the 15:35 card);
- fill far from the stop → silently enlarged risk.

All three 2026-10-06 RTH cards lost net (−$27.90) and the signal dashboard
still scored them as wins — the outcome column is signal-level scoring,
not execution.

## Studies (all three scripts replay the 650-session archive)

### rthStaleGateStudy.ts — can a pre-dispatch stale gate save market entries?

- Gate: skip when adverse move > k×risk OR favorable move > targetDist − 1.5
  (the tape ltp at card-fire time — what the live feed actually sees).
- Cell A (signal-level scoring): the gate forfeits the family's best trades
  (+11.9k pts at k=0.5, 93% WR) — the RTH edge LIVES in moved-market trades.
- Cell B (drift-aware fills, $1.90/RT): those "winners" are scratches and
  mis-anchored stop-outs in reality. No-gate baseline: PF 0.50, 1,081
  scratches, −$67k, BREACH. The gate removes all scratches and avoids a
  net-losing set, but the kept set stays PF ~0.55 — mitigation, not a cure.
- **Verdict: gate rejected** — it also hurts the limit-entry configs below.

### rthDriftOptimizer.ts — does ANY config survive fees under realistic fills?

112 configs (stop × target × market/limit × gate). Only resting-LIMIT
entries survive; every market config breaches. Top: s0.5/t2.5 limit
+$13.8k PASS; s0.5/t2.0 limit +$3.0k PASS; current live config −$67k.

### rthLimitValidation.ts — train/OOS validation of the surviving configs

Train (< 2026-01-01): PASS + PF ≥ 1.2 + dd ≥ −1900 → 8/24 qualify, all
PASS out-of-sample:

| config | train | OOS 2026 | 2024 / 2025 / 2026 | total @$1.90/RT |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| s0.5 t2.5 limit | +$8.1k | +$5.7k PASS | −$1.3k / +$10.2k / +$5.7k all PASS | +$13.8k |
| s0.5 t2.5 limit 3/day | +$2.2k | +$2.7k PASS | all PASS | +$4.9k |
| s0.5 t2.0 limit 3/day | +$1.2k | +$1.6k PASS | all PASS | +$2.7k |
| s0.5 t2.0 limit | +$0.7k | +$2.3k PASS | all PASS | +$3.0k |

TTL sweep on the winner: 10 bars +$17.6k (dd −$1.1k) > 5 bars +$13.8k >
3 bars BREACH. Fee sensitivity: positive through ~$2.10/RT (measured live
fee = $1.90/RT); negative at $2.40/RT.

## Change shipped

- `lib/signalFeed.ts` — `rthLimitParams()` + the RTH limit-entry path
  (resting limit at the signal price via the existing `placeOrder({limitPrice})`
  and execWatch limit lifecycle: fill-or-expire, cancel on expiry).
  **OFF by default** (`RTH_LIMIT_ENTRIES=1` enables; knobs
  `RTH_LIMIT_STOP_MULT` 0.5, `RTH_LIMIT_TARGET_R` 2.5, `RTH_LIMIT_TTL_MS`
  default 9 min — under the 10-min watcher give-up clock so expiry takes
  the clean `limit_expired` path).
- `tests/rthLimitEntry.test.ts` — param parsing.

## Live ops

- `FEED_RTH=0` applied to the `nq-dashboard` Coolify env 2026-10-06
  (approved) — the losing market-order RTH path is off until the
  limit-entry redesign is enabled (explicit approval + env change first).
- Momentum family untouched (already resting-limit via the retrace path).

# RTH counter-signal gate — research note (2026-10-07)

Follow-up to the post-mortem question "should a fresh opposite-side RTH card
close to a winning RTH exit be gated harder?" (trade 9: 12:54 short stopped in
6s, 13 min after the 12:44 long hit target in the same zone).

## Study

`web/scripts/counterGateScratch.ts` (untracked scratch, research input — NOT
validation per EXEC_CHANGE_POLICY): 86 sessions 2026-06-01..2026-10-06 from R2,
live-style replay (detectSoftMomentum SOFT_PROD, resting-limit entry TTL 9 min,
0.5× stop, 2.5R target, HORIZON 60, no one-at-a-time block — live `checkRth`
has none), n = 1013 filled cards. Cells = cards fired within N minutes of an
opposite-side RTH card's WINNING exit, within M points of that exit:

| cell | n | WR | avg pts | PF |
|------|---|----|---------|----|
| baseline | 1013 | 37.4% | +0.99 | 1.36 |
| 5×∞ | 28 | 39.3% | +2.26 | 1.91 |
| 10×∞ | 64 | 29.7% | +0.15 | 1.05 |
| 15×∞ | 99 | 33.3% | +0.60 | 1.21 |
| 30×∞ | 194 | 35.6% | +0.82 | 1.30 |
| 5×5 | 8 | 12.5% | −2.02 | 0.31 |
| 10×5 | 18 | 16.7% | −1.51 | 0.51 |
| 15×5 | 27 | 29.6% | −0.14 | 0.95 |
| 30×5 | 45 | 28.9% | −0.31 | 0.89 |

## Verdict

- **Time-only gating is NOT justified** — the ∞-distance cells are ≈ baseline
  or better.
- **Distance gating (≤5 pts from a winner's exit) is directionally consistent**
  (all four M≤5 cells negative, PF 0.31–0.95) but thin (n = 8–45). After an
  opposite-side **loss** the cards are positive (PF 1.04–1.58), so the WIN
  trigger is the right one.
- Caveats: the offline archive does not reproduce trade 9 itself (live fires
  ~3–4 RTH cards/day vs 13.7 offline; 1-min footprint cannot see 6-second
  intra-bar stops) — this validates a pattern, not the event. The
  rthLimitValidation harness's 60-bar one-at-a-time block makes the effect
  structurally unmeasurable in that harness (all cells empty).

## Proposal (flagged, NOT applied)

`RTH_COUNTER_GATE_MIN=15` / `RTH_COUNTER_GATE_PTS=5` — skip an RTH card whose
entry is within 5 pts of an opposite-side RTH card's winning exit in the last
15 min. Master off by default; enabling requires explicit owner approval and a
full `scripts/rthOptimizer.ts` campaign re-validation extended with a
live-style no-block replay variant (the current harness cannot see this
effect).

## Status 2026-10-08 — APPLIED (owner-approved)

The owner approved enabling the gate on 2026-10-08. It shipped as
`RTH_COUNTER_GATE_MIN=15` / `RTH_COUNTER_GATE_PTS=5` on `nq-dashboard`, with
the full implementation in `web/lib/rthExitLog.ts` (winner-exit ring buffer +
pure gate decision), the exit learning in `web/lib/execWatch.ts`
(open-position tracking at fill confirmation + a 30s flat-transition poll that
derives the exit price from the session fills), and the veto in
`web/lib/signalFeed.ts` (RTH section — skip + `recordSkip` journal).

Daybook documentation (the requirement): the two knobs are in the daybook
settings snapshot, so the boot record's `variationId` changes with them and
every deploy carrying them is fingerprint-visible; every vetoed card lands in
the daybook as a `signal` record with
`reason: "counter-gate (opposite <side> winner Nm ago within P pts)"` and
`rejectedBy` in its features; every winning RTH exit that arms the gate is
logged by execWatch as `[rth-exit] <side> winner logged — exit …`. To disable:
set both envs to `0` on the Coolify app (owner approval required to change).

### Full-archive validation (651 sessions, 9,009 cards — 2026-10-08)

> **Sequenced-replay nuance (2026-10-08, docs/research/full-gates-replay-2026-10-08.md):**
> under one-position-at-a-time sequencing the counter-gate is structurally
> inert (0 drops in every config — no card can land within 15/30 min of a
> winner's exit because winners never hold ≥45 bars and successors fire ≥60
> bars after a filled entry). LIVE has no one-at-a-time block in checkRth, so
> live sits in the no-block regime where the gate's measured effect lives.
> The gate-ON decision stands; its benefit is live-path only.

Live-style no-block replay (limit TTL 9m, 0.5× stop, 2.5R target, HORIZON 60,
no cap). TRAIN = 2023-12-18..2026-05-31 (565 sessions), OOS = 2026-06-01..10-06
(86 sessions).

| cell | TRAIN (n 7996) | OOS (n 1013) | ALL |
|------|----------------|--------------|-----|
| baseline PF (avg pts) | 1.51 (+1.07) | 1.36 (+0.99) | 1.49 |
| G1 MIN15/PTS5 (n 319/27) | 1.37 (+0.67) | 0.95 (−0.14) | 1.32 |
| G2 MIN30/PTS5 (n 491/45) | 1.44 (+0.78) | 0.89 (−0.31) | 1.37 |

- The gated cell underperforms baseline in BOTH periods at every cost level
  ($0.95/$1.90/$3.80 per-side) — the earlier "overfit" verdict from the
  truncated Jan–May 2026 train (n 60/77) is retracted.
- Account sim (eval, $1.90/RT, $100 budget): baseline $11,248 PASS →
  G1-gated $14,156 (+$2,908, dd −1480) · G2-gated $15,094 (+$3,846, dd −1632).
- Honest caveats: OOS n is thin (27/45) and its deficit (~−1.1 pts) is ~3×
  the train deficit (~−0.4); monthly scatter is extreme (n 0–28/month); the
  replay has no overrides/news/tape gates; freed slots were not re-simulated;
  the offline tape still does not reproduce trade 9 itself.

# Bias time-of-day study — when is the daily-bias call most accurate? (2026-10-09)

> Question: *"what is the best time of day to start trading with high
> accuracy of daily bias — we have more information in NY than in London,
> and more in the afternoon than in the morning…"*
> Test: fit the SAME lookahead-free feature set at every session clock-time,
> predict direction out-of-sample, and see whether accuracy actually rises
> as information accumulates. CLI: `web/scripts/biasTimeOfDay.ts`.

## Method

- **Sample:** all 654 archived sessions (2023-12-18 → 2026-10-09), one
  sample per session per start time (n=654 per row).
- **Start times:** hourly 18:05→08:05 ET, the briefing slots 09:15 (pre-open),
  09:35 (post-open), 11:30, 13:30, 16:05, plus 09:05–14:05 ET on the hour.
- **Features (identical everywhere, known through bar T):** chgPct vs
  session open · close position in session range · cumulative delta ÷1000 ·
  realized 1σ (30 closes) · daily/weekly HTF swing structure from the PRIOR
  65 RTH sessions. Same definitions as `biasFit.ts`.
- **Two labels:** `rem` = direction from close(T) to the session close
  (the daily-bias call; horizon shrinks through the day — mean |rem| is
  reported so the shrinkage is visible) · `fwd60` = next-60-minute
  direction (fixed-horizon control that separates "more information" from
  "shorter horizon").
- **Model:** per-start-time logistic regression (L2), train on the first
  70% of dates, evaluate on the last 30% (no shuffle, train-stats
  standardization — the biasFit discipline). Baselines per row: always-up
  (the max of up/down share) and a naive momentum rule (sign of chgPct).
  Wilson 95% CIs on accuracy.

## Results — accuracy by start time (out-of-sample)

|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

| 23:05 | 47.2% | 52.3% | −5.1 | 56.3% | 0 | 0.87% | 50.3% | 53.8% | 52.3% |

| 13:30 midday | 49.2% | 50.3% | −1.0 | 49.7% | 5/654 · 60% | 0.36% | 52.3% | 53.3% | 54.0% |
| 14:05 | 50.3% | 50.8% | −0.5 | 45.7% | 1/654 | 0.32% | 49.2% | 53.3% | 53.8% |
| 16:05 pre-close | 49.2% | 50.8% | −1.5 | 44.2% | **50/654 · 56%** | 0.11% | — | — | 56.2% |

Pooled groups (rem label, test samples):

| group | n | acc [95% CI] | base | lift |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| overnight 18:05–08:05 ET | 2,955 | 49.1% [47.3–50.9] | 52.5% | −3.4 |
| NY open 09:05–10:05 ET | 788 | **54.8% [51.3–58.2]** | 54.3% | +0.5 |
| midday 11:05–13:30 ET | 985 | 50.2% [47.0–53.3] | 51.9% | −1.7 |
| late 14:05–16:05 ET | 394 | 49.7% [44.9–54.6] | 50.8% | −1.0 |

## What this falsifies and what it confirms

1. **"More information later in the day ⇒ more accurate daily bias" is
   FALSIFIED.** Accuracy does not rise through the session — at the fixed
   60-minute horizon it oscillates between ~45% and ~57% with no trend, and
   for the remainder-of-session call it PEAKS at 19:05 / 02:05 / 09:15 and
   DEGRADES through the afternoon (13:05 is the worst cell, 46.2% vs a 51.8%
   baseline). More information does not buy direction accuracy: by the time
   the afternoon arrives, most of the day's drift has already happened
   (mean |rem| collapses 0.93% → 0.11%), so the remaining direction is
   noise-dominated. The "information" the afternoon gives you is information
   about what has ALREADY happened — it doesn't predict the remaining
   direction.
2. **The one place your intuition survives: the pre-open call beats the
   evening-open call by ~10 pts** (09:15 56.3% vs 18:05 46.2%; group level:
   NY-open 54.8% vs overnight-pooled 49.1%, CIs [51.3–58.2] vs [47.3–50.9]).
   The overnight tape genuinely adds predictive value for the rest of the
   session — the 09:15 call has the whole Globex session in hand. Note the
   caveat: per-slot CIs are ±6.7–6.8, so individual adjacent cells are not
   statistically separable; the group-level statement is the robust one.
3. **The evening-open call (18:05) is actively bad** (−7.1% lift — WORSE
   than always-up). A daily-bias call made from prior-day data + HTF alone
   should not be trusted for the day's direction.
4. **The best single-hour windows match the almanac, not the afternoon:**
   the two best remainder-of-session cells are 02:05 (57.9%, +4.1 lift) and
   09:15 pre-open (56.3%, +2.5); the best fixed-horizon cell is 03:05
   (56.9%). That is exactly the overnight-drift leg the seasonal almanac
   found (95% of all drift; prime entry window 3–7 ET with 79.8–83% card
   WR) — the day's direction is most knowable in the small hours and at the
   pre-open, NOT in the NY afternoon.
5. **The fitted model's extreme tail is the only place with a consistent
   tilt** — and only at pre-close (16:05: 50 calls, 56.0% vs 50.8% base),
   matching `biasFit`'s τ=0.10 finding (~56% on the extreme tail). Everywhere
   else the tail is too thin to trade (0–18 calls of 654).

## The operational answer (what "best time to start" really means)

There is no clock-time where the daily-bias call becomes reliably accurate;
the ceiling is ~56–58% on the best cells and a coin flip elsewhere. The
honest, evidence-backed mapping for THIS system:

- **Start trading in the drift leg, not after the information is in.**
  The measured prime window is **02:00–07:00 ET** (best bias cells 02:05 /
  03:05; card WR 79.8–83% at hours 3–7 ET). That is where the day's
  direction is most predictable AND the drift is still ahead.
- **Make the RTH daily-bias call at 09:15 pre-open** (56.3%, the best
  NY-side cell). Do NOT improve it by waiting: 09:35/11:30/13:30 are all
  worse — the opening drive adds noise, not signal.
- **Do not "start trading in the afternoon because you have more
  information."** Afternoon cells are the worst (13:05 46.2%) and the
  remaining move is ~0.1–0.4%. If the afternoon has an edge at all it is
  drift-magnitude effects (hour 13 ET long-drift, hour 14 ET negative
  drift per the almanac), not direction accuracy.
- **Evening open (18:05):** the bias call is worse than always-up — treat
  the first Globex hour as observation, not conviction (their card already
  waits for tape triggers rather than an evening bias).

## Limits

- Single 70/30 date split, one instrument, n=654 per cell (test ≈ 196);
  Wilson CIs ±6.7–6.8 — treat the ranking as structure, not as significant
  pairwise differences. Group-level CIs are the robust statements.
- The `rem` horizon shrinks by construction (mean |rem| reported) — the
  afternoon's coin-flip accuracy is partly "small remaining move", which is
  itself the operational point: there is little left to predict.
- Features are the biasFit six; adding ALN/gap/VIX features (the framework's
  §7 plan) may shift the pre-open cells specifically.

## Rerun note (2026-10-10, consolidated engine)

Migrated to `wilson95` (the engine's single CI implementation), which also
fixed a double-divided denominator in the original local Wilson interval.
Rerun numbers: per-cell CIs are now ±6.8–6.9 (previously ±6.7–6.8), group
CIs widen marginally (NY open 54.8% [51.3–58.3]) — **all conclusions
unchanged**: no clock-time exceeds ~58%, the afternoon is the worst place
to make the daily-bias call, and the 02–07 ET + 09:15 pre-open cells remain
the best. (Direction-accuracy study, not a trade-level study — the T1/T4
tables of BACKTEST-REPORT-STANDARD do not apply; base-rate tables above are
the study's native output.)

## Regenerate

```bash
cd web
node --env-file=.env.local --import ../scripts/ts-loader.mjs scripts/biasTimeOfDay.ts
```
