# Bias fit v2 — do the structure features lift the fitted bias model? (2026-10-09, standard format 2026-10-10)

> Question: *"does extending the fitted model with the structure layer
> (gapPct, ALN, VIX level + term) beat the base model out-of-sample — i.e.,
> does the daily-bias framework graduate from advisory to signal?"*
> CLI: `web/scripts/biasFitV2.ts`.

## Method

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Instrument / session | NQ 1-min · full session (ETH+RTH) |
| Sample | 2023-12-18 → 2026-10-09 · 654 sessions × 6 briefing slots = 3,843 samples |
| Cost model | n/a — direction-accuracy labels, no trades |
| Fill model | n/a |
| Exit model | n/a — labels: next-60-min direction AND remainder-of-session direction |
| Split | 70/30 by date (train 2,669 / test 1,174), no shuffle |
| Significance | Wilson 95% CI on accuracy (engine `wilson95`) |
| Model | per-label logistic regression (L2) · BASE 6 features vs EXTENDED 10 features (adds gapPct, aln (P3+1/P4−1, ≥08:05 ET only), vixLevel, vixTerm — all lookahead-free) |
| CLI | `web/scripts/biasFitV2.ts` |

## Results

> **Standard deviation note:** direction-accuracy study, no trades — T1/T4
> do not apply. The verdict below is the τ-sweep comparison on TEST.

| Model | TEST acc | τ=0.05 tail | τ=0.10 tail |
|---|---|---|---|
| BASE 6 feat, 60-min | 52.9% (baseline 52.4%) | 48.7% (n=298) | 50.7% (n=67) |
| EXT 10 feat, 60-min | 51.5% | 52.1% (n=361) | 53.2% (n=79) |
| BASE 6 feat, remainder-of-session | 53.5% (baseline 52.6%) | **62.0%** (n=276) | **64.3%** (n=42) |
| EXT 10 feat, remainder-of-session | 53.6% | 61.7% (n=355) | 65.6% (n=61) |

Extended coefficients (remainder label, standardized): `gapPct −0.063 ·
aln −0.061 · vixLevel +0.036 · vixTerm +0.081` — weak and partly negative
(the P3/gap lean tilts slightly AGAINST the next move: pullback-from-
strength, the same signature biasFit found for weekly HH/HL).

`VERDICT: edge unproven · significance — · stability extended ≈ base on
both labels · holdout n/a · viability n/a (no trades — direction study)`

## What this falsifies and what it confirms

1. **Falsified: the structure features lift the direction model.** Extended
   ≈ base on both labels; the framework does NOT graduate — `systemVerdict`
   weights unchanged, chips stay advisory.
2. **Confirmed: the remainder-of-session tail is stronger than the 60-min
   tail** (~62–66% vs ~53%) — the daily-bias call from the extreme tail is
   the more predictable label, but the BASE model already reaches it
   (small n = 42–61: a tilt, not an edge).
3. **Adopted:** the structure factors stay where they belong — level/target
   facts (90–97% hit rates) as display-only chips, never gates.

## Honest bounds

- Single 70/30 split; the base model's own numbers differ slightly from the
  original `biasFit` run because the archive grew (654 vs 649 sessions) and
  the date split shifted — the valid comparison is within-run.
- VIX features use the latest CBOE close known at the session open (close
  day ≤ prior calendar day) — a live system cannot know newer.
- ALN is zeroed for slots before 08:05 ET (London completes 08:00 ET) —
  strict lookahead guard.

## Wired (display-only, advisory)

`lib/biasChips.ts` (pure ALN/gap/prior-day/VIX-gate + sideLean one-sided
cells, unit-tested) → `macroWatch.ts` bias block → briefing snapshot
`watch.biasChips` + prompt line + deterministic chip line →
`scripts/biasChips.ts` CLI.

## Regenerate

```bash
cd web
node --env-file=.env.local --import ../scripts/ts-loader.mjs scripts/biasFitV2.ts
```

# Daily Bias Framework — the highest-precision way to frame today's direction (2026-10-09)

> The question: *"what is the best way to frame a daily bias, so we can
> confidently say today is likely bullish or bearish — with high precision?"*
> Answer researched end-to-end: what our own archive says, what the external
> evidence says, and what free sources can feed the call. The headline is
> uncomfortable and useful: **a naked "today is up/down" call tops out around
> 55–60% even in the best tail — precision comes from WHERE the drift lives,
> WHICH days are structurally strong, and WHEN to not force a call.**
>
> Companion evidence (repo): `docs/research/BIAS_FIT.md` · `seasonal-almanac-2026-10-05.md` ·
> `htf-trend-filter-research.md` · `docs/data/MACRO_DASHBOARD_USEFULNESS.md` ·
> `docs/data/DATA_SOURCE_AUDIT_2026-10-03.md` · **`daily-bias-research-2026-10-09.md`**
> (the 49-citation external-evidence companion: per-factor evidence grades,
> backtest protocols, bias traps). CLI: `web/scripts/biasFit.ts`,
> `web/scripts/seasonalAlmanac.ts`, `web/scripts/rthDayBias.ts`,
> `web/scripts/counterBiasVeto.ts`, `web/scripts/alnStructureStudy.ts`.

---

## 0. The honest precision ceiling (our own measurements first)

**Our fitted model (`biasFit.ts`, 649 sessions, walk-forward, no lookahead):**
direction over the next ~60 minutes from the tape is barely predictable.

| Metric (out-of-sample) | Value |
|---|---|
| direction accuracy (all slots) | **50.6%** (always-up baseline 51.6%) |
| mean fwd move when predicted up | +0.10 bp |
| mean fwd move when predicted down | −0.68 bp |
| strongest τ=0.10 tail (10% of briefings) | **56.3%** |

The model's own coefficients say momentum features are weak and mixed-sign
(positive change barely predicts continuation; weekly HH/HL leans slightly
AGAINST the next hour — a pullback-from-strength tilt). Pre-open and post-open
carry the biggest forward moves (±44 bp) yet are the hardest to call (46–56%).

**Our seasonal almanac (same archive):** the drift is not uniform —
95% of all NQ drift lives in the **overnight leg** (57.7% up, +20.9 pts mean);
the **RTH leg is a coin flip** (52.7% up, +0.7 pts). Monday +80.2 pts/65% up,
Thursday −14.5 pts/45.1%. FOMC cells are extreme: 24h pre-FOMC 71.4% up
/+94.2 pts; FOMC-day card 83.8% WR / PF 5.16; pre-FOMC day the worst cell
(67.4% / 1.64). This replicates the Lou–Polk–Skouras overnight anomaly on our
own tape.

**External cross-checks (measured, not folklore):**

| Fact (NQ, 2020→mid-2026, n≈1,660–1,670 sessions) | Number |
|---|---|
| RTH takes out an overnight extreme (Steady Turtle) | **94.7%** (high 63.2% · low 56.3% · both 24.8%) |
| Hits PDH or PDL (Steady Turtle) | **89.5%** (PDH 55.2% · PDL 44.3% · both 10.1% · inside day 10.5%) |
| RTH-open gap fills (Steady Turtle) | 60.3% base · **96.4% for gaps <10 pt** · **38.1% for ≥80 pt** |
| ALN pattern → NY breaks London high/low | P3 partial-up (41% of days): H 81.3% vs L 67.5% · P4 partial-down (30%): flips to L 74.5% vs H 67.9% |
| ICT "Midnight Opening Gap" retracement claim (MNOG working paper, Zenodo) | 60–65%, author states it is NOT standalone — needs HTF confluence |

Academic anchors: daily index-return predictability is tiny (R² ≈ 1%),
the overnight vs intraday split is the strongest daily-frequency effect
(Lou–Polk–Skouras), and a systematic evaluation of ICT/SMC rules in G10 FX
exists ([SSRN 7430998 — "Smart Money or Costly Folklore?"](https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=7430998);
abstract page is bot-blocked, findings consistent with: some rules carry
structure, none are high-precision standalone signals).

**Consequence for framing:** "high precision" must be bought with
**selectivity + structure**, not with a bigger/better indicator. The best
daily-bias framework is a four-layer stack where each layer answers a
different, measurable question:

1. **Calendar layer** — which days are structurally strong/weak (highest precision, smallest n).
2. **Structure layer** — which levels/magnets get tagged today (94.7% / 89.5% base rates — level-precise, direction-leaning).
3. **Regime layer** — what asymmetry the day trades under (VIX percentile, GEX sign, HTF structure, curve, COT).
4. **Tape layer** — the fitted 60-min model (advisory; only its extreme tail tilts).

---

## 1. Layer 0 — Calendar gates (highest precision, from our own 649-session measurements)

Check first, in this order. These are the only cells our own data found that
are stable across train/test (2026-01-01 split) with a mechanism:

| Check | Read | Action (chip today; gate only after walk-forward) |
|---|---|---|
| FOMC decision day | card 83.8% WR / PF 5.16 (n=99), train 81.7 / test 89.3 — best cell in the almanac | **Trade the full plan; do not skip.** `FOMC DAY` |
| Day before FOMC | 67.4% / PF 1.64 (n=138), train 71.7 / test 53.1 — worst cell | **Stand aside or half size.** `PRE-FOMC` |
| Day-of-week | Mon 65% up / +80 pts · Thu 45.1% / −14.5 (close-to-close, both windows agree) | Lean-long Monday, lean-flat/short Thursday at day level. Caveat: the academic literature says the classic Monday effect is dead in index futures (Kamara 1997) — our local measurement is NQ 2023–2026 specific and is a tint, not a gate |
| Entry hour | 3–7 ET 79.8% WR / PF 3.27 (n=904, train/test agree) · hour 13 ET best long-drift hour · hours 9–10 and 14 ET negative drift | Prime window = the bias is most actionable there |
| News calendar | CPI/NFP/FOMC/PCE blackouts already enforced by `newsGate` | Extend awareness: Treasury auctions 12:55–13:05 ET (Lou–Yan–Zhang price pressure), OPEX/quad witching (3rd Friday), FOMC minutes days |
| Earnings | NDX mega-cap earnings day (NVDA-class) biases the whole tape | Already in the earnings panel; treat as event-day |

These five checks take 30 seconds from the dashboard's existing panels
(seasonal chips already print on the momentum card).

---

## 2. Layer 1 — Structure (level-precise; the daily "magnet map")

The measured base rates say the day's path is constrained, even when its sign
is not. **First-party verification (2026-10-09): the external tables below
were replicated on OUR 654-session archive with `web/scripts/alnStructureStudy.ts`
— they hold on our own tape** (right column):

| Rate | External (NQ 2020→mid-2026, n≈1,660) | OURS (654 sessions, 2023-12→2026-10) |
|---|---|---|
| RTH breaks ≥1 overnight extreme | 94.7% (high 63.2% · low 56.3%) | **97.1%** (high 66.8% · low 61.9%) |
| RTH breaks BOTH overnight extremes | 24.8% | **31.7%** |
| Hits ≥1 of PDH/PDL | 89.5% (PDH 55.2% · PDL 44.3%) | **88.1%** (PDH 55.8% · PDL 41.0%) |
| Sweeps both PDH+PDL | 10.1% | **8.7%** |
| Inside day (neither) | 10.5% | **11.8%** |
| ALN pattern mix | P1 23% · P2 4–6% · P3 41% · P4 30% | **P1 22.0% · P2 7.2% · P3 40.8% · P4 30.0%** |
| P3 → NY breaks London high vs low | 81.3% vs 67.5% | **77.2% vs 64.4%** |
| P4 → NY breaks London low vs high | 74.5% vs 67.9% | **72.4% vs 69.4%** |
| Gap fill by size | <10pt 96.4% · 40–80 63.8% · ≥80pt 38.1% | **<10 97.4% (n=38) · 40–80 65.5% · ≥80 38.6% (n=368)** |

Operational reads (identical conclusions on both datasets):

- **Overnight range** (18:00→09:30 ET): RTH breaks an overnight extreme ~95–97%
  of days — a near-certain target, not a guess.
- **Asia–London–NY handoff** (the strongest directional lean in the data):
  classify the pattern before the open.
  - P3 partial-engulf-up (~41% of days): NY breaks the London **high** far
    more than the low (77% vs 64% on our tape) → lean long-side bias for the
    first RTH move.
  - P4 partial-engulf-down (~30%): flips (low 72% vs high 69%) → lean short-side.
  - P1 full engulf (~22%): both sides ~70% → expansion/volatility day, bias
    from the tape, not the structure.
  - P2 containment (~7%): rare, quiet — chop day.
- **RTH-open gap vs prior close**: fade only small gaps (<10 pt fill ≈97%);
  large gaps (≥80 pt fill ≈39%) are **continuation** — align the bias WITH a
  large gap, fade a small one. Gap direction itself is a coin flip for
  open-to-close direction (SPY buckets 49–57% — see the evidence doc) — the
  gap sizes the fade-vs-follow choice, not the sign.
- **PDH/PDL**: ~88–90% of days tag at least one prior-day extreme; only ~9–10%
  sweep both. After the first extreme is tagged, the base rate still favors
  the opposite side holding — the "which magnet first" question is the daily
  bias a scalper can actually trade with precision.

Our system already computes every one of these numbers pre-open (session
range, prior-day extremes, gaps via `gapTracker`). The ALN classifier and the
gap-size regime are now measured on our own archive (`alnStructureStudy.ts`) —
wiring them as pre-open computed chips is pure arithmetic over existing data.

---

## 3. Layer 2 — Regime (asymmetry; how the day behaves, not its sign)

Everything here is already collected by `lib/macroWatch.ts` (display-only).
For a daily-bias call, read them as regime, never as signals:

| Gauge (wired) | Read for the day |
|---|---|
| HTF structure (own archive, ~65 sessions) | Daily HH/HL → shorts are the losers in bullish regimes (our htf-short-pullback study: 25% WR, −$305). Weekly HH/HL leans slightly against the next hour (pullback tilt). Counter-bias RTH trades underperform (counterBiasVeto). |
| VIX level + 1y percentile + term (9D vs 3M) | Low VIX + contango → compressed, mean-reversion/chop regime (matches positive-gamma behavior). High percentile + backwardation → expansion. Expected daily range ≈ VIX/16. |
| GEX sign + flip level (live CBOE QQQ feed, in QQQ pts → converted) | Positive gamma = dealers dampen (chop/mean-revert); negative = amplify (trend). The flip level marks where the regime switches intraday. |
| 10Y/2Y + intraday CNBC curve | Yields up = NQ headwind; direction of the daily curve move is a same-day macro lean (delayed ~20 min — regime, not trigger). |
| COT NQ spec net %OI + 52w percentile | Crowded spec long at extremes = fragile tape (contrarian lean); weekly lag — a background tilt only. |
| ES vs NQ relative strength, SOX leadership | SMT-divergence proxy: semis/ES leading or lagging NQ flags who's driving the open. |

---

## 4. Layer 3 — Tape at the briefing slots (the fitted model)

`systemVerdict` (wired, `lib/briefingText.ts:435`) applies the biasFit
coefficients at six slots (evening-open 18:05 · pre-open 09:15 · post-open
09:35 · mid-morning 11:30 · midday 13:30 · pre-close 16:05) using chgPct,
closePos, cumDelta, realized 1σ, HTF D/W. Rules in force:

- |score| ≤ τ (0.10) → **chop** — the honest default; do not force a direction.
- Only the extreme tail tilts (~56% historical accuracy on 10% of briefings).
- The intraday variant (`rthDayBias`/`counterBiasVeto`): first-30-min
  cumulative delta. Global filter is weak (+0.16 pts/trade, discards 62%);
  the veto form (skip counter-bias tickets from 10:00 ET when |bias| ≥
  threshold) is the studied replacement.

The DeepSeek briefing already receives all four layers and makes the final
up/down/chop call with level-referenced watchFors — this document is the
**discipline around that card**, not a replacement for it.

### When to start trading — the time-of-day study (2026-10-09)

`web/scripts/biasTimeOfDay.ts` fit the same six features at every session
clock-time (654 sessions, walk-forward, Wilson CIs) and measured
remainder-of-session direction accuracy. Result: **accuracy does NOT rise
through the day — "more information later" is falsified** (full table:
`docs/research/bias-time-of-day-2026-10-09.md`). The best cells are 02:05
(57.9%), 09:15 pre-open (56.3%), 03:05 fixed-hour (56.9%); the afternoon
is the WORST (13:05 = 46.2% vs 51.8% baseline) because the remaining move
collapses to ~0.1–0.4% and its direction is noise. Operational map:

- **Start trading in the drift leg: 02:00–07:00 ET** (matches the almanac's
  prime window; the day's direction is most knowable there).
- **Make the RTH bias call at 09:15 pre-open and do not "improve" it by
  waiting** — 09:35/11:30/13:30 are all worse; the opening drive adds noise,
  not signal. The pre-open call beats the evening-open call by ~10 pts
  (56.3% vs 46.2%), so the overnight tape is real information for the day.
- **Never start fresh in the afternoon on "more information" grounds** —
  worst bias cells + no drift left. The 18:05 evening call is worse than
  always-up: first Globex hour is observation, not conviction.

---

## 5. The verdict function — when is "high confidence" actually justified?

Two parts: a **score** (from the evidence doc's 12-factor ranking, ±14 max)
and a **four-layer agreement rule**.

### The score (15 minutes, done by 09:15 ET)

| # | Factor | Compute | Score |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Gap size | % of prior close | <0.5%: ±2 fade-against the gap · 0.5–1.5%: 0 · >1.5%: ±2 with-gap only if VIX<25 |
| 2 | ALN pattern | Asia vs London ranges (measured on our archive) | P3 +2 · P4 −2 · P1/P2 0 |
| 3 | Prior-day position | price vs PDH/PDL/PDC/prior VA | above PDH & VAH: +1 · below PDL & VAL: −1 · inside: 0 |
| 4 | Overnight move | overnight % | ≥+0.8%: −1 (RTH fade tilt) · ≤−0.8%: +1 · between: 0 |
| 5 | VIX + term structure | VIX level, VIX3M−VIX | contango & VIX<25: +1 fade-validity · backwardation or VIX≥25: −1 and **cap: no fade trades** |
| 6 | Calendar | FOMC/CPI/NFP/earnings/TOM | FOMC/CPI/NFP/mega-earnings: score 0 but **size×0.5, stops×1.5, no entries 08:25–08:35 & 13:55–14:10 ET** · TOM day-1: +1 |
| 7 | Gamma regime | GEX sign | negative gamma: 0 but expect expansion (stops×1.5, both-sides plan) · positive gamma: 0, fade-valid |
| 8 | AAII extreme | bull-bear spread (Thursday AM release — use release-time data) | >+20: −1 · <−20: +1 · else 0 |
| 9 | Fear & Greed | index level | >80: −1 · <20: +1 · else 0 |
| 10 | COT change | 4-wk Δ non-commercial net (Tuesday snapshot, Friday release) | crowded long: −0.5 · crowded short: +0.5 · else 0 |

Explicitly scored 0 (narrative until proven): DXY, 10Y, crude, BTC, QQQ
flows, news sentiment — they stay in the regime panel as context only.

**Confidence tiers:** strong-bull ≥ +6 · lean-bull +2…+5 · neutral −1…+1 ·
lean-bear −5…−2 · strong-bear ≤ −6.

**Execution hard rules (measured, not scored):** never enter on the first OR
break (49.6/50.2 coin flip, both sides break ~69% of NQ days); expect the
first poke to be faded; gap-fade plans expire at noon (>80% of fills); IB
break by noon on 83% of days — morning sets the day.

### One-sided filters — "only longs/shorts here" (measured on the card, 2026-10-09)

`web/scripts/sideFilterStudy.ts` measured every context cell BY SIDE on the
3,298 replayed card trades (dominance = expectancy gap between sides; full
table + bounds: `docs/research/side-filter-study-2026-10-09.md`). The
highest-certainty statements:

- **ONLY LONGS — gap 0.5–1.5% DOWN + overnight tape + non-FOMC day:**
  88% WR [77–94], +5.19 pts avg, train 88 / test 88 (n=57) — the single
  strongest one-sided cell in the archive. Mid gaps in general are long
  zones (+3.9 to +4.8 pts, both HTF regimes, all hours).
- **ONLY SHORTS — gap ≥1.5% UP:** 78.8% WR, +3.16 pts (n=33); longs in the
  same cell 59.6% / +0.47. The day is priced; the card's failed-breakout
  shorts get paid. Mirror (large down → longs) consistent but thin (n=12).
- **ONLY SHORTS — pre-open 08–09 ET (non-FOMC):** 89% WR, +4.42 (n=38,
  test n=8 — watch-item). Longs 66%.
- **ONLY LONGS — ALN P2 chop containment:** 73.9% / +2.23 (n=46); shorts
  are the ONLY negative cell on the board (−0.47).
- Falsified: "only shorts in HTF-bear" (bear longs 79.6% are the best HTF
  cell), "one side on FOMC days" (both ≈84% — trade everything), "side
  filter in prime 03–07" (dominance 0.12 — the window is the edge, not the
  side).

These are journal chips until they clear a forward-log/walk-forward gate —
the same path every other measured filter had to walk. **Wired 2026-10-09:**
card chips (`lib/sideFilter.ts` → `signalFeed.ts`: P2 longs, P4 23–02
shorts, 08–09 shorts — in-memory cells only) + briefing chips
(`lib/biasChips.ts` `sideLeanChips` → macro watch: the gap/HTF cells) —
labels and journal features only, never gates.

### The four-layer agreement rule

A **STRONG directional call** (the only tier worth the word "confident")
requires all four layers to agree:

1. Calendar cell aligned (FOMC day, Monday, prime window) — no pre-FOMC veto;
2. Structure lean agrees (ALN P3 + long / P4 + short; gap regime consistent);
3. Regime agrees (HTF structure, GEX sign, VIX percentile, curve direction —
   at least 3 of 4 same-side);
4. Tape score outside the τ=0.10 band in the same direction.

Expected frequency: a handful of days per month. That is the point — the
precision is bought by **passing on everything else**. Any day failing the
stack is `LEAN` (card both ways, chips only) or `CHOP` (stand-aside / half
size), which is exactly the house discipline already adopted in the playbook
(labels never gate; cells need train/test agreement before becoming gates).

### The honest accuracy ceiling (academic + our own numbers)

- Our fitted 60-min model: 56.3% in its strongest 10% tail. The best single
  pre-market variable in the literature (gap size) delivers 49–57% — a coin
  flip. Welch–Goyal (RFS 2008): classic predictors fail out-of-sample with
  OOS R² ≈ 0 at the monthly horizon; daily is strictly harder.
- **Realistic target: 55–60% same-day direction on the days the score takes
  a strong stance, 50–55% on neutral days — where correctly standing aside
  is itself the win.** Sustained >62–65% same-day direction claims are
  overfitting/look-ahead red flags.
- The profit engine is asymmetry, not direction: a 53% system with 1.5R
  asymmetry beats a 60% system with 0.8R — stops get probed ~70% of NQ days
  (both-sides OR stat), so stop placement and sizing by regime (VIX/GEX) do
  the heavy lifting the bias score cannot.

---

## 6. Free data stack — what is wired, what to add, verified today (2026-10-09)

> The full live-verified catalog (30 sources, code snippets, ToS flags) is

## 8. One-page answer

**The best way to frame a daily bias with high precision is a four-layer
checklist, not a single indicator:**

1. **Calendar first** (FOMC-day trade / pre-FOMC stand-aside / Monday lean /
   prime 3–7 ET window) — our own highest-precision cells.
2. **Structure second** (ALN pattern + gap-size regime + which of PDH/PDL/
   overnight extremes gets tagged) — 90–95% base-rate magnets with a
   measurable directional lean.
3. **Regime third** (HTF structure, GEX sign/flip, VIX percentile+term,
   curve, COT) — asymmetry and expected range, all already collected free.
4. **Tape last** (the fitted systemVerdict) — advisory; its extreme tail is
   the only evidence-backed directional tilt, ~56%.

A "high-confidence bullish/bearish today" is only declared when all four
layers agree — a few days per month — and everything else is lean/chop. That
is what high precision costs, and it is the only version our own 649-session
archive supports.

## 9. What we learned (the durable lessons)

1. **Direction precision is capped at ~55–60% everywhere** — our fitted
   model's tail (56.3%), the best external single variable (gap, 49–57%),
   the best time-of-day cell (57.9%), and the literature (Welch–Goyal
   OOS R² ≈ 0) all converge on the same ceiling. Precision is bought with
   selectivity (few strong-stance days/month), and profit is made with
   asymmetry (1.5R structures, regime sizing), not with a better indicator.
2. **The magnet map is the precision we can actually trade.** ~90% of days
   tag PDH/PDL, ~95–97% break an overnight extreme, gap size decides
   fade-vs-follow, ALN P3/P4 gives a real first-move lean (77% vs 64% on our
   tape). Level-precise, direction-leaning, first-party verified.
3. **Information accumulates through the day; predictability does not.**
   The best bias cells are 02–07 ET and the 09:15 pre-open; the afternoon and
   the 18:05 open are where bias calls go to die (13:05 = 46.2%, 18:05 worse
   than always-up). "Wait for more information" waits yourself out of the
   only predictable leg — 95% of the drift is overnight.
4. **Calendar routing is the cheapest precision we own:** FOMC day = trade
   the full plan (83.8% card cell); pre-FOMC = stand aside; Monday/Thursday
   tints; 3–7 ET prime window. Days are not exchangeable.
5. **Macro is regime, not signal.** VIX + term structure = sizing and the
   fade-validity gate; GEX sign = amplify-vs-dampen; DXY/10Y/crude/BTC =
   narrative for same-day (score 0); "red folder" is a size rule, not a

# Daily Bias (Bullish/Bearish/Neutral) for NQ Intraday Scalping — Evidence-Based Factor Research

**Date:** 2026-10-09 · **Purpose:** input for a real pre-market scoring system
**Method:** every claim below is either (a) sourced to a specific publication/backtest with URL, or (b) explicitly labeled as a testable hypothesis with a backtest protocol. Guru methods with no published stats are labeled as such.

**Evidence grading used throughout:**
- **[A]** Peer-reviewed academic (journal/NBER/Fed staff).
- **[B]** Large-sample public backtest by a vendor/blog (not peer-reviewed; treat as prior, not proof).
- **[C]** Practitioner/anecdotal or self-published (IG, YouTube-derived frameworks).
- **[H]** Hypothesis — no published stats; protocol given.

---

# 1. ICT concepts (Smart Money Concepts)

## 1.1 Power of 3 (Accumulation → Manipulation → Distribution) as daily bias
**(a) How to measure today:** the ICT framing says each daily candle cycles through three phases: an early-session range (accumulation), a false move that sweeps an obvious liquidity pool — prior day high/low or Asia/London range — (manipulation), then the "real" directional leg (distribution). Pre-market you can only know the *setup*: where price is relative to PDH/PDL/PDC and the overnight (Asia/London) range. The AMD sequence itself is only knowable in hindsight.
**(b) Direction:** bullish bias if the sweep of a *sell-side* pool (PDL, overnight low) reclaims back into range with displacement; bearish for the mirror image. Post-sweep-and-reclaim, trade toward the opposite extreme (PDH).
**(c) Evidence:** **none published.** The only systematic source found that backtests ICT patterns at scale states outright: *"Its predictive power in our data is difficult to isolate from other patterns firing at the same times, so we don't currently backtest it as a standalone signal"* and *"The three-phase model describes a common pattern but not every day cycles through it cleanly. Forcing every chart into the model produces false pattern-matching."* Their adjacent ICT pattern stats are crypto, not NQ (order blocks on BTC 4H: ~45% win rate across 137 instances — near base rate; only high-confluence combos like order-block-after-sweep showed 85%+ on 1H, small samples). A community backtest of Power-of-3 on MES exists but content is JS-rendered (no extractable stats).
**(d) URLs:**
- https://botsfolio.com/learn/ict-trading
- https://pinescriptforge.com/mes/ict-power-of-three/backtest
**(e) How you WOULD backtest it:** define sweep objectively (wicks ≥1 tick through PDH/PDL or overnight extreme; displacement candle = close beyond swept level with body > 0.5×ATR(14,5min)); signal = sweep + 5-min close back inside prior range; measure NQ RTH open-to-close or fixed 1R outcome 2015–present; benchmark against (i) unconditional 53–55% up-day base rate, (ii) a randomized sweep-signal bootstrap. **Grade: [H] for the AMD label itself; [B] for the underlying "levels get swept" mechanics — see 1.2.**

## 1.2 Draw on liquidity: PDH/PDL and Globex extremes as magnets
**(a) How to measure:** PDH/PDL = prior RTH (09:30–16:00 ET) high/low. Overnight (Globex) high/low = extremes from 18:00 ET reopen to 09:30 open. Weekly high/low = same from Monday open.
**(b) Direction:** the "magnets" claim is **statistically well supported as a *target* claim, not a *direction* claim**: hitting a level is near-certain; the reaction at the level is not predictable from the level itself.
**(c) Evidence (NQ, 2020–mid-2026, n≈1,670 sessions, 1-min data, [B]):**
- Price trades back to at least one prior-day extreme on **89.5% of NQ days** (ES 90.8%); both extremes swept same day: only **10.1%** (NQ). PDH hit 55.2% vs PDL 44.3% — mild up-drift tilt. Inside days (touch neither): 10.5%.
- RTH breaks at least one **overnight (Globex) extreme on 94.7% of NQ days**; both overnight extremes: 24.8%.
- **Asia–London–NY handoff patterns carry a real pre-market directional lean:** when London partially engulfs Asia to the upside (P3, ~41% of days), NY breaks the London **high** on ~81% of NQ days vs the London low ~68%; when the partial engulf is down (P4, ~30%), it flips (London low ~75% vs high ~68%). Clean London-engulfs-Asia (P1, ~23%) is the most two-sided.
- Weekly high/low as magnets: **no published stats found** — testable with the same protocol. [H]
**(d) URLs:**
- https://steady-turtle.com/statistics/previous-day-high-low-hit-rate
- https://steady-turtle.com/statistics/overnight-session-break-probability
**Caveat:** ~90% hit rates make these levels *targets*, which is the empirically defensible half of ICT; the "sweep = reversal" half is the part with no published numbers (see 1.1e).

## 1.3 HTF PD arrays (order blocks, fair value gaps)
**(a) How to measure:** order block = last opposite-color candle before a displacement leg; FVG = 3-candle gap where candle-3 range doesn't overlap candle-1 (imbalance zone); on daily/4H charts.
**(b) Direction:** price expected to react at HTF OB/FVG zones; bias = trade from them in the direction of the HTF trend.
**(c) Evidence:** **no peer-reviewed or index-futures statistics found.** Closest quantifiable analogue: TradingView strategy-script collections (self-reported, survivorship-prone, not evidence). The one systematic engine (Botsfolio) reports crypto-only, near-base-rate (~45%) standalone OB win rates. Any NQ-specific OB/FVG win-rate claims in YouTube content are unsourced. **Grade: [H].**
**(d) URLs:** https://botsfolio.com/learn/ict-trading · https://ar.tradingview.com/scripts/fairvaluegaps/
**(e) Backtest protocol:** from each 15m/1H FVG + daily OB on NQ 2015–present, count (i) probability price trades into the zone within N days, (ii) conditional next-1R outcome vs unconditional; require displacement filter (2×ATR candle) to reduce multiplicity.

## 1.4 Liquidity sweep + displacement at 9:30 NY open / London open
**(a) How to measure:** at 09:30, watch whether the first push through the 09:30–09:35 opening range or the overnight high/low is *reclaimed* (close back inside) with an expansion candle.
**(b) Direction:** failed break of OR high → bearish lean; failed break of OR low → bullish lean; *holding* break → continuation.
**(c) Evidence (NQ [B], 2020–mid-2026):** the 5-min opening range breaks on **100% of sessions** (trivially); **both sides break on 68.8% of NQ days** — i.e., the *first* poke out of the OR is fully reversed ~7 days in 10. **First-break direction is a coin flip (49.6%/50.2%)** — there is no directional edge in the first break, only in which break holds. This is the single best empirical grounding for "sweep-and-reverse at the open" and simultaneously the proof that guessing the direction of the 9:30 sweep has no standalone edge. London-open (2–5am ET) sweeps of the Asia range: quantified only indirectly via the ALN patterns in 1.2. **Grade: [B] for reversal frequency, [H] for displacement-based entry timing.**
**(d) URL:** https://steady-turtle.com/statistics/opening-range-breakout-probability

---

# 2. Session logic / day-type frameworks

## 2.1 Initial Balance (first hour, 09:30–10:30) break stats
**(a) How to measure:** IB = first-60-min RTH high/low; available at 10:30 ET (not pre-market — use yesterday's IB as context pre-open).
**(b) Direction:** break of IB high = bullish day-type lean; inside day = range day; both-sides = two-sided/chop.
**(c) Evidence (NQ [B], 2020–mid-2026, n=1,670):** one side breaks on **97.0%** of days (inside day = 3.0%); IB high breaks 63.0%, low 55.6%, both 21.7%; **83.2% of breaks occur by noon** — no break by noon ⇒ rotational afternoon. IB range ≈ 144.5 pts ≈ 57% of the full RTH range. Day-of-week effect on break rate: none (96–98% every weekday). **Grade: [B].**
**(d) URL:** https://steady-turtle.com/statistics/initial-balance-break-probability

## 2.2 Opening Range Breakout continuation vs reversal
**(a) How to measure:** OR = 09:30–09:35 (5-min) or 15/30-min variants; continuation = first break holds to close; reversal = both sides break.
**(b) Direction:** no edge in first break; edge lives in the second/holding break.
**(c) Evidence:** Steady Turtle (1.4 above): both-sides 68.8% NQ / 73.1% ES ⇒ naive "buy first OR break" is a ~50% coin flip with a ~70% chance of being stopped on the other side first. Independent 2026 arXiv-style ORB study (447 out-of-sample trades, ES/NQ context filters): naive ORB long produces T≈0.88 — statistically indistinguishable from zero before context filters. Classic 6,142-day ORB guide exists (tradingstats.net) but page content is JS-rendered. **Grade: [B].**
**(d) URLs:**
- https://steady-turtle.com/statistics/opening-range-breakout-probability
- https://d.repec.org/n?u=RePEc:arx:papers:2605.04004&r=mst
- https://tradingstats.net/orb-breakout-strategy-guide/

## 2.3 Trend day vs range day early detection
**(a) How to measure:** pre-market: gap size + overnight ALN pattern + prior-day type; intraday: IB break timing, both-sides rate, relative volume.
**(b) Direction:** no-break-by-noon, inside prior range = range day (fade extremes); early IB break with volume = trend day (pullback entries).
**(c) Evidence:** the 15%-tail "no IB break by noon" and 10% inside-day rates (above) are the quantified anchors; day-classification systems (QuantLogix, Overcharts) are practitioner taxonomies without published hit rates. **Grade: [B] for components, [C] for full taxonomies.**
**(d) URL:** https://quantlogix.ai/update/trend-days-vs-range-days-2026-05-29

## 2.4 Overnight/Globex range vs prior close
Covered in 1.2 (overnight break rates, ALN patterns) and 6.1 (gap stats). **The ALN P3/P4 lean is the single most useful *pre-market* session-logic factor found.**

---

# 3. Macro cross-asset leading indicators for NQ

**Headline verdicts (what is statistically predictive of same-day NQ direction vs narrative):**

| Asset | Same-day directional evidence | Verdict for pre-market NQ bias |
|---|---|---|
| VIX level | Vol clustering is robust; direction ambiguous (Elm Wealth: buying VIX>30 spikes has Sharpe 0.47 vs 0.50 static, inverse 0.54, momentum 0.59) | **Use for sizing & fade-validity, NOT direction** |
| VIX term structure (VIX3M−VIX) | Regime filter with documented predictive value for SPX forward returns | **Use: contango ⇒ mean-reversion valid; backwardation ⇒ no fades** |
| DXY | Negative corr real but low/time-varying at daily freq; no same-day predictive study found | **Narrative/coincident** [H] |
| 10Y yield | Stock-bond daily correlation time-varying, driven by VIX; sign unstable | **Narrative for same-day; regime tint only** [H] |
| Crude oil | No same-day NQ predictive evidence | **Narrative** |
| EURUSD | None | **Narrative** |
| BTC | Correlated in stress; no robust same-day lead | **Narrative** |

**(a/b/c/d) by factor:**
- **VIX level:** measure today's VIX close/level and its 5-day change. High/rising VIX ⇒ wider two-sided ranges (vol persistence is among the most robust facts in finance), but **not** reliably bearish next-day: [Elm Wealth, S&P 1990–2026] — a "buy when VIX>30" rule *reduces* Sharpe (0.47 vs 0.50 static), while *cutting* exposure when VIX is high (0.54) and simple momentum (0.59) win. https://moontowermeta.com/vix-and-buy-signals/ · https://elmwealth.com/vix-buy-signal/
- **VIX term structure:** compute VIX3M − VIX sign pre-market. Contango (positive) = calm regime, supports gap-fade/mean-reversion postures; backwardation (negative) = stress, fades dangerous. Practitioner framework with data: https://stockwirex.com/education/spy-overnight-gap-strategy-fill-probability/ ; academic basis: https://www.efmaefm.org/0EFMSYMPOSIUM/2017/papers/VIX%20term%20structure%20and%20SP500%20returns_EFM_blind.pdf
- **DXY / 10Y:** the only strong academic result in this neighborhood is that **stock-bond daily return correlation is itself time-varying and driven by uncertainty (VIX)** — Connolly, Stivers & Sun, *Stock Market Uncertainty and the Stock-Bond Return Relation*, JFQA 40(1), 2005. https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/journal-of-financial-and-quantitative-analysis/article/abs/stock-market-uncertainty-and-the-stockbond-return-relation/5AE775460C3CAF695D85D5DD5923FC49 — implication: using 10Y/DXY as a *fixed-sign* daily bias is a specification error; any real edge must be conditioned on the volatility regime. Same-day NQ-specific DXY predictive stats: none found. **Testable hypothesis [H]:** regress NQ RTH open-to-close return on overnight ΔDXY and Δ10Y in (a) VIX<15, (b) VIX 15–25, (c) VIX>25 regimes; expect coefficient significance only in (b)/(c) and unstable sign over decades.
- **BTC/crude/EURUSD:** excluded from the scoring system; keep as optional narrative confirmations only.

---

# 4. Positioning data

## 4.1 CFTC COT (Nasdaq-100 net positioning)
**(a) How to measure:** COT legacy report: non-commercial (large speculator) net = longs − shorts, % of open interest, and its weekly change. **Snapshot is Tuesday; released Friday 15:30 ET** — data is 3 days stale by Monday.
**(b) Direction:** literature consensus is *not* cleanly contrarian: large speculators tend to be trend-followers (net long rises with the market), hedgers/commercials are the contrarians; results at the index level are mixed, with most predictive power found in commodities, not equity indices.
**(c) Evidence:** academic work on COT for S&P 500 exists but finds modest/mixed results: [thesis-level meta-study of COT financial futures] https://epub.jku.at/download/pdf/12001095.pdf ; [COT as trading signal for S&P500] https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S1042443113000723 ; related futures-sentiment evidence (VIX, put-call, TRIN) summarized in https://apps.theifm.org/docs/rfm-special-Issue2011-pubJuly2012.pdf . **Standalone precision for next-week NQ direction: low. Grade: [A] for "weak/mixed," [H] for any strong claim.**
**(d)** Practical use: only as a slow regime tint (speculators extremely net-long = crowded trend), never as a same-day factor; if used, use the *change* over 4 weeks, not level.

## 4.2 Options dealer gamma / GEX regime
**(a) How to measure:** aggregate dealer gamma (GEX) from open interest across SPX/NDX/QQQ option strikes: dealers are short gamma to customers; net negative GEX ⇒ dealer hedging is pro-cyclical (amplifies moves); net positive ⇒ counter-cyclical (dampens). Public sources: CBOE data, vendor GEX charts.
**(b) Direction:** **regime factor, not a direction factor.** Negative gamma ⇒ *larger two-sided ranges and faster velocity*; positive gamma ⇒ chop/compression, "gamma pinning."
**(c) Evidence:** the hedging mechanism is standard market-microstructure theory and empirically documented (dealer delta-hedging feedback): https://zenodo.org/records/20572982 ; https://github.com/iAmGiG/gex-llm-patterns/blob/8eab27a11023dd2b438174fc2006734c7c610652/docs/papers/digital_finance/Regan_Xie_DigitalFinance.pdf ; dealer-hedging lead-lag in VIX/SPX futures: https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1386418123000496 . **No published evidence that GEX sign predicts same-day NQ *direction* — only volatility amplification. Grade: [A] for mechanics, [H] for direction claims.** Use for: expected range sizing, stop width, and "is today likely to trend hard or chop."

## 4.3 Put/call ratio extremes
**(a) How to measure:** equity-only put/call ratio (CBOE), 5-day or 21-day average, z-score vs 1-year history.
**(b) Direction:** contrarian at extremes only: extremely high put volume (fear) = bullish contrarian tilt; extremely low (complacency) = bearish tilt; mid-range = noise.
**(c) Evidence:** Simon & Wiggins (2001) find VIX, put-call ratio and TRIN (trading index) jointly predict S&P 500 *futures* returns (summary: https://apps.theifm.org/docs/rfm-special-Issue2011-pubJuly2012.pdf ); a 2025 practitioner study of total PCR finds weak same-day value and supports extreme-contrarian use only: https://brucewoodcapital.com/2025/09/23/put-call-ratio-excessive-optimism/ . **Grade: [A]/[C] — real but weak; extremes only.**

## 4.4 ETF flows (QQQ daily)
**(a) How to measure:** daily QQQ share creation/redemption ≈ fund flows, % of AUM.
**(b) Direction:** flows are demand shocks that move prices contemporaneously and *increase volatility*, but they do not predict same-day or next-day direction; post-flow reversal is documented.
**(c) Evidence:** Ben-David, Franzoni, Moussawi, *Do ETFs Increase Volatility?*, NBER w20071 / JFE 2018 — ETF flows increase non-fundamental volatility. https://www.nber.org/papers/w20071 **Verdict: skip as a bias factor. Grade: [A] for "doesn't predict direction."**

## 4.5 CME open interest changes
**(a/b)** OI up with price = new money chasing trend (momentum tint); OI up with falling price = fresh shorts (bearish tint) — classic OI-price confirmation.
**(c) Evidence:** academic results for futures OI as a return predictor are weak/mixed (e.g., trading activity and price reversals: https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0378426603001201 ). **Use only as a confirmation tint, weight near zero. Grade: [A] weak/mixed.**

# 5. News / calendar-driven bias

## 5.1 Pre-FOMC drift (the strongest calendar anomaly in the literature)
**(a) How to measure:** is today an FOMC day? (8 meetings/yr; since 2019 all have press conferences.) Compute the 24h window from prior-day open to announcement.
**(b) Direction:** **statistically bullish** for the 24h *before* the 14:00 ET statement — the premium accrues overnight, unrelated to the announcement's actual content.
**(c) Evidence [A]:** Lucca & Moench (NY Fed): 1994–2011, ~50bp average excess return in the 24h pre-FOMC (equity only, not Treasuries); post-2011, ~40bp concentrated before press-conference meetings (from prior-day open to announcement-day lunch); returns before the announcement contain **no information about the direction of the announcement reaction**. Post-statement reaction: coin flip with extreme vol.
**(d) URLs:** https://libertystreeteconomics.newyorkfed.org/2018/11/the-pre-fomc-announcement-drift-more-recent-evidence/ · https://conference.nber.org/conf_papers/f66717.pdf

## 5.2 CPI / NFP announcement days ("red folder")
**(a) How to measure:** is an 08:30 ET CPI or NFP release today? (CPI monthly, NFP first Friday.)
**(b) Direction:** **the direction of the print reaction is not predictable; the day's volatility is.** The documented equity *premium* on announcement days is a risk premium earned for holding through the event, not a scalping signal.
**(c) Evidence [A]:** Savor & Wilson (JFQA 2013) — excess returns average ~11.4bp on scheduled macro announcement days vs ~1.1bp on other days; a large share of the total equity premium accrues on announcement days; elevated returns concentrated in the pre-announcement window (Wachter & Zhu, "A Model of Two Days"); FOMC/NFP/CPI releases show statistically elevated equity risk/returns: https://conference.nber.org/conf_papers/f218782/f218782.pdf
**(d) URLs:** https://homsy-staging.cambridgecore.org/core/journals/journal-of-financial-and-quantitative-analysis/article/abs/how-much-do-investors-care-about-macroeconomic-risk-evidence-from-scheduled-economic-announcements/C6A48B33065D93550C87FEB53C029A0B · https://rodneywhitecenter.wharton.upenn.edu/wp-content/uploads/2021/10/Wachter-A-Model-of-Two-Days_-Discrete-News-and-Asset-Prices.pdf
**Scalper's verdict:** "flat pre-event" is defensible *as a scalping rule* (you can't capture a 10–50bp overnight premium by scalping the 08:30 print; you only take two-sided slippage risk). But note the honest nuance: the *statistical bias* for the 24h window is bullish, not neutral — "red folder" is a volatility/size rule, not a bearish signal. Action: **halve size, widen stops 1.5–2×, no entries 08:25–08:35 ET and 13:55–14:10 ET; trade the post-print displacement only.**

## 5.3 Mega-cap earnings concentration (NVDA etc.)
**(a) How to measure:** which Nasdaq-100 mega-caps report today/after-close; combined weight of today's reporters in the index.
**(b) Direction:** ex-ante direction of the reaction is not predictable; expect elevated implied vol and dealer-gamma concentration into the print.
**(c) Evidence [A/H]:** within-firm returns are predictably elevated *around recurring events like earnings* (Hartzmark & Solomon, "Recurring Firm Events and Predictable Returns: The Within-Firm Time Series," Annual Review of Financial Economics 2018) — predictability is at the firm level, not the direction of the print; index-level effect is an untested hypothesis for NQ. https://www.annualreviews.org/content/journals/10.1146/annurev-financial-110217-022605 **Action: same size rule as red folder; no directional bias.**

# 6. Statistical / quant approaches

## 6.1 Overnight gap statistics (NQ/ES/SPY)
**(a) How to measure:** gap = RTH open − prior RTH close, in NQ points and as % of price; bucket by size.
**(b) Direction:** gap size is a **near-coin-flip directional signal** but a **powerful fade-vs-follow filter**:
- SPY 2017–2026: open-to-close "up" rate by gap bucket stays 49–57% vs 53–55% unconditional — no directional edge; only 1–2% upside gaps reach ~60% (and ~40% of those still close lower).
- Same-day fill: gaps <0.5% fill 70–80%+ (SPY); 0.5–1% fill ~43–60%; >1.5% fill only 30–40%, ~50% still open after 5 sessions. Gap-downs fill slightly more (69% vs 59%). **>80% of fills happen before noon.**
- NQ points buckets (2020–mid-2026): 0–10 pts → 96.4% fill; 10–20 → 86.2%; 20–40 → 82.7%; 40–80 → 63.8%; **80+ pts → 38.1%**. Overall NQ fill 60.3%; gap up 59.8% vs gap down 61.0% (not tradable).
**(c) Grade: [B] but large-sample, NQ-specific, and the most actionable hard stats in this report.**
**(d) URLs:** https://stockwirex.com/education/spy-overnight-gap-strategy-fill-probability/ · https://steady-turtle.com/statistics/gap-fill-probability
**Use:** small gap (<0.5%) ⇒ fade back to prior close magnet (bullish-if-gap-down, bearish-if-gap-up); large gap (>1.5% or NQ >80pts) ⇒ continuation regime, don't fade without VIX confirmation.

## 6.2 Overnight vs intraday returns ("Tug of War")
**(a) How to measure:** overnight return = open/prior-close; RTH return = close/open.
**(b) Direction:** firm-level and strategy returns exhibit **overnight continuation and intraday reversal** — momentum-type profits accrue overnight and are partially *offset* intraday; overnight direction tends to persist into the open while RTH acts as a counterweight. Implication for bias: **same-day RTH return is weakly negatively autocorrelated with the overnight move; treat big overnight moves as already-priced, not as fresh RTH fuel.**
**(c) Evidence [A]:** Lou, Polk, Skouras, *A Tug of War: Overnight Versus Intraday Expected Returns*, JFE 134(1) 2019. https://researchonline.lse.ac.uk/id/eprint/87481/ · cross-stock intraday↔overnight momentum spillovers: https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/journal-of-financial-and-quantitative-analysis/article/decoding-momentum-spillover-effects/EB6BE5A096753108881E1514E54035DF

## 6.3 Intraday momentum (same-day signal, available at 10:00 ET)
**(a) How to measure:** SPY/QQQ return 09:30–10:00 ET (measured from prior close).
**(b) Direction:** **first half-hour return positively predicts the last half-hour (15:30–16:00) return** — statistically and economically significant; stronger on high-vol, high-volume, recession, and macro-news days.
**(c) Evidence [A]:** Gao, Han, Li, Zhou, *Market intraday momentum*, JFE 129(2) 2018. https://ideas.repec.org/a/eee/jfinec/v129y2018i2p394-414.html **Note: not pre-market — it is your first same-day bias update at 10:00 ET.**

## 6.4 Time-series momentum
**(a) How to measure:** sign of trailing 12-month return (Moskowitz-Ooi-Pedersen) or shorter lookbacks.
**(b) Direction:** TSMOM sign = trend-following bias **at monthly horizons**; for next-day NQ direction the published 12-month TSMOM is effectively irrelevant (it's a monthly strategy across 58 futures, not a daily index signal). Shorter-horizon daily momentum evidence exists mainly at the cross-sectional/intraday level (see 6.2/6.3).
**(c) Evidence [A]:** https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0304405X11001937 (JFE 104(2) 2012) · AQR data page: https://www.aqr.com/Insights/Datasets/Time-Series-Momentum-Factors-Monthly **Verdict: do not include 12-month TSMOM in a daily bias score.**

## 6.5 Seasonality: day-of-week and turn-of-month
**(a) How to measure:** calendar day; trading-day-of-month 1–3 (and last day).
**(b) Direction:** 
- Turn-of-month: S&P 500 returns significantly higher during TOM window; **post-ETF-era the effect is concentrated on the first trading day of the month** (Chen & Chua, JFP 2011). Mild bullish tint on day 1.
- Day-of-week: the classic Monday effect (negative Mondays) is **dead or reversed** in large caps/futures since the late 1980s (Kamara 1997: Monday effect vanished in S&P 500 futures after index futures introduction; later work documents a "reverse weekend effect"). Recent replication literature says weekly seasonality fails to replicate robustly. Weight ≈ 0.
**(c) Evidence [A]/[B]:** https://www.financialplanningassociation.org/article/journal/APR11-turn-month-anomaly-age-etfs-reexamination-return-enhancement-strategies · https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/New-Evidence-on-the-Monday-Seasonal-in-Stock-Kamara/dd9226108b2821ff2405b6828b5813034159e272 · https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S1057521903000115 · https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1057521926001651

## 6.6 VIX term structure
Covered in §3 (regime filter). Use VIX3M−VIX sign.

# 7. Sentiment

## 7.1 AAII survey
**(a) How to measure:** weekly AAII bull/bear/bull-bear spread (released Thursday AM for the week through Wednesday — data lag); use the spread and its z-score.
**(b) Direction:** **contrarian at extremes:** extreme bullishness ⇒ lean bearish for the coming week; extreme bearishness ⇒ lean bullish.
**(c) Evidence [A]:** Gómez-Martínez et al., IREF 2026 — 25 years of weekly AAII on E-mini S&P 500, cost-adjusted backtest: high-threshold contrarian rules generate positive net profits and materially better expectancy/drawdown efficiency, **but no strategy beats the passive long Sharpe** — i.e., sentiment timing improves *when-you-trade* quality, not risk-adjusted total return. Abstract: https://econpapers.repec.org/article/eeereveco/v_3a111_3ay_3a2026_3ai_3ac_3as1059056026008014.htm · journal: https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1059056026008014
**Use:** ±1 point in the score only when the bull-bear spread is beyond ~±15–20 pts (roughly top/bottom decile); otherwise 0.

## 7.2 Fear & Greed Index
**(a) How to measure:** CNN Fear & Greed composite 0–100; extremes <20 / >80.
**(b) Direction:** contrarian tint at extremes; relationship **decaying**.
**(c) Evidence [A]:** Farrell & O'Connor, *Finance Research Letters* 2025: F&G Granger-causes S&P 500, Nasdaq Composite and Russell 3000 returns in 2011–2020; **the effect weakens materially in 2021–2024 and is driven mainly by pre-2014 data** — treat as a weak, regime-decaying contrarian tint. https://research.ucc.ie/en/publications/the-cnn-fear-and-greed-index-as-a-predictor-of-us-equity-index-re/ · https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S1544612324015216

## 7.3 Retail positioning (IG client sentiment)
**(a) How to measure:** IG publishes % long of its retail clients per instrument.
**(b) Direction:** claimed contrarian (retail heavily long = bearish signal).
**(c) Evidence:** **IG's own marketing/education pages only; no independent peer-reviewed validation of NQ-specific predictive value found.** DailyFX/IG internal research is FX-centric. **Grade: [C]/unverified.** Use at most as an extreme-contrarian tiebreaker (e.g., >75–80% retail long = one bearish point, and vice versa), or exclude entirely. https://www.ig.com/uk/trading-strategies/_how-to-trade-using-ig-client-sentiment-240912

## 7.4 Twitter/news sentiment
**(a/b)** headline-sentiment z-scores; contrarian or momentum depending on the vendor.
**(c) Evidence:** no robust, replicable same-day NQ predictive evidence found. **Exclude from the scoring system.** [H] if ever pursued: event-study on headline sentiment vs RTH open-to-close, with multiple-testing correction (Harvey-Liu-Zhu).

# 8. Market profile / TPO

## 8.1 Prior-day value area, POC, single prints, VAH/VAL acceptance
**(a) How to measure:** from prior RTH session's 30-min TPO/volume profile: POC (heaviest price), value area (70% of volume around POC), VAH/VAL, single prints. Pre-market: mark where today's overnight price sits relative to prior VAH/VAL/POC.
**(b) Direction (practitioner rules):** open above prior VAH = bullish acceptance (VAH becomes support); open below VAL = bearish; inside value = balance (two-sided); POC = magnet; single prints = fast zones where price "should" retrace.
**(c) Evidence:** **no peer-reviewed backtests of prior-day VA/POC predictive value were found.** The methodology originates in Dalton's *Mind Over Markets* (Wiley) — methodology, not evidence: https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/pdf/10.1002/9781118659724.app1 · https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/9781118659724 (ch.4). The *indirect* empirical support is strong: prior-session levels in general get revisited ~90% of days (PDH/PDL hit rates, §1.2) and prior close acts as the gap-fill magnet (§6.1). **Grade: [C] as taught; [H] for VA-specific claims.**
**(d) Backtest protocol [H]:** on NQ 2015–present, bucket RTH open vs prior VAH/VAL (above/below/inside); measure (i) P(open-to-close up), (ii) P(price touches prior POC that day), (iii) P(VAH holds as support conditional on opening above); compare vs unconditional; walk-forward with roll-adjusted continuous contracts.

# RANKED: the 12 highest-signal factors for a pre-market NQ bias score
Ordered by estimated *incremental precision contribution* (not raw win rate; rank 1–4 carry the hard NQ-specific numbers):

1. **Gap size + fill regime** (NQ-specific [B]). Compute: (RTH open − prior RTH close) / prior close, in % and NQ points. Bias: <0.5% ⇒ fade toward prior close (direction = opposite of gap); >1.5% (NQ >~80pts) ⇒ continuation regime (direction = with gap, only if VIX confirms); 0.5–1.5% ⇒ no default direction, defer to factor 2/3. Supporting data: 96.4% fill <10pts vs 38.1% >80pts; SPY buckets 49–57% direction.
2. **Overnight Asia–London structure (ALN pattern)** [B]. Compute at 09:00 ET: Asia range (20:00–02:00), London range (02:00–08:00). P3 (London partial-engulf up) ⇒ bullish lean (London high breaks ~81% vs low ~68% on NQ); P4 ⇒ bearish lean (mirror); P1 ⇒ two-sided/neutral; P2 ⇒ rare, neutral. This is the best *pre-market directional* stat found.
3. **Position vs prior-day structure + POC/VA** [B base + C]. Compute: is the overnight price above/below PDH/PDL/PDC and prior VAH/VAL? ~90% of days touch one prior extreme ⇒ nearest un-swept PDH/PDL is a *target*; direction lean = toward the nearest unswept level *once the open confirms*, not blindly.
4. **Overnight return sign/magnitude ("tug of war")** [A]. Compute overnight % move. Big overnight move ⇒ RTH tends to consolidate/partially reverse (intraday reversal tendency); small overnight move ⇒ RTH has room to trend. Bias: dampen overnight direction for RTH expectations.
5. **VIX regime + term structure** [A/B]. Compute VIX level (calm <15, elevated 15–25, stress 25–35, panic >35) and VIX3M−VIX sign. Bias: contango+calm ⇒ mean-reversion bias valid (fade extreme opens); backwardation or VIX>25 ⇒ no fades, expect expansion, direction not predictable — size down. (Direction-neutral but highest-value *volatility* input; wrong-size trades are how bias systems die.)
6. **Calendar premium/red folder** [A]. Compute: FOMC day? CPI/NFP? mega-cap earnings? FOMC day ⇒ statistically bullish 24h window but 14:00 reaction is a coin flip (flat into it); CPI/NFP ⇒ elevated vol, direction unpredictable (flat 08:25–08:35, half size); TOM day-1 ⇒ mild bullish tint. Never let the calendar score override a size cap.
7. **Dealer gamma/GEX regime** [A mechanics]. Compute GEX sign/magnitude (vendors or CBOE OI). Negative ⇒ wide two-sided ranges (expect both OR sides broken; size for expansion); positive ⇒ compression/pinning (fade rails, tighter targets). Direction-neutral; feeds sizing and fade-vs-trend choice.
8. **AAII extreme (weekly)** [A]. Compute bull-bear spread; ±1 point only beyond ~±15–20 (top/bottom decile), contrarian sign. Weekly scale — it tints, never dominates, a daily score.
9. **ORB/IB conditional stats (post-open update)** [B]. At 09:35/10:30: first OR break has ~50% edge (do NOT bias on it); a *reclaimed* break flips lean; IB broken by 10:30 with volume ⇒ trend-day; both-sides early ⇒ chop-day. At 10:00 ET add factor 6.3 (first-half-hour return → last-half-hour prediction) as a same-day momentum tint [A].
10. **Turn-of-month day-1** [A/B]. Compute trading-day-of-month. +0.5 point if day 1 of month (significant positive average return post-1993). Day-of-week: weight 0 (effect decayed/dead).
11. **Fear & Greed extreme** [A, decaying]. ±1 point only at <20/>80, contrarian. Evidence weakening post-2021 — keep weight small.
12. **COT net-positioning change (weekly)** [A, weak/mixed]. Compute 4-week change in non-commercial net % of OI (remember Tuesday-snapshot/Friday-release lag). Crowded extreme = contrarian tint ±0.5. Lowest-ranked inclusion; defensible to drop.

**Excluded (narrative-only until proven):** DXY, 10Y (unconditioned), crude, EURUSD, BTC, QQQ flows, Twitter/news sentiment, 12-month TSMOM, CME OI changes, IG sentiment (unverified).

# Pre-market scoring framework (~15 minutes, done by 09:15 ET)

Weights tuned so structural/hard-data factors dominate and unverifiable factors can't flip the tier. Total possible: ±14.

| # | Factor | Compute | Score |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Gap size | % of prior close | <0.5%: +2 fade-against (or −2 fade-against) · 0.5–1.5%: 0 · >1.5%: ±2 with-gap only if VIX<25 |
| 2 | ALN pattern | Asia vs London ranges | P3 +2 · P4 −2 · P1/P2 0 |
| 3 | Prior-day position | price vs PDH/PDL/PDC/VA | above PDH & VAH: +1 · below PDL & VAL: −1 · inside: 0 |
| 4 | Overnight move | overnight % | ≥+0.8%: −1 (RTH fade tilt) · ≤−0.8%: +1 · between: 0 |
| 5 | VIX + term structure | VIX level, VIX3M−VIX | contango & VIX<25: +1 fade-validity · backwardation or VIX≥25: −1, **cap: no fade trades** |
| 6 | Calendar | FOMC/CPI/NFP/earnings/TOM | FOMC/CPI/NFP/mega-earnings: score 0 but **size×0.5, stops×1.5, no entries 08:25–08:35 & 13:55–14:10** · TOM day 1: +1 |
| 7 | Gamma regime | GEX sign | negative gamma: 0 but expect expansion (stops×1.5, both-sides plan) · positive gamma: 0, fade-valid |
| 8 | AAII extreme | bull-bear spread | >+20: −1 · <−20: +1 · else 0 |
| 9 | Fear & Greed | index level | >80: −1 · <20: +1 · else 0 |
| 10 | COT change | 4-wk Δ non-commercial net | extreme crowded long: −0.5 · crowded short: +0.5 · else 0 |

**Confidence tiers:**
- **Strong-bull ≥ +6** (e.g., small gap-down + P3 + below PDL + contango): only long setups; full size; first target = prior close/PDC, second = PDH.
- **Lean-bull +2 to +5:** long setups preferred; counter-trend shorts need A+ displacement entry and half size.
- **Neutral −1 to +1:** default = range logic; fade extremes toward POC/prior close; first OR break has no edge — wait for reclaim or holding break; half size.
- **Lean-bear −5 to −2:** mirror of lean-bull.
- **Strong-bear ≤ −6:** mirror of strong-bull.

**Execution layer (not scored, hard rules):** first OR break is a coin flip (49.6/50.2) — never enter on it; both sides break ~70% of NQ days — expect the first poke to be faded; IB break by noon 83% — morning is where the day's direction gets set; >80% of gap fills occur before noon — gap-fade plans expire at lunch.

**15-minute completion order:** (1) 09:00 ALN pattern + gap + prior-day levels [5 min] → (2) VIX/VIX3M, GEX, calendar [4 min] → (3) AAII/F&G/COT glance [2 min] → (4) tally score, set tier [2 min] → (5) write levels & size caps [2 min] → trade the reaction, not the prediction.

# The honest answer: maximum realistic same-day directional accuracy

- **Base rate:** SPY closes up 53–55% of days (unconditional drift). Any system must beat this before costs. https://stockwirex.com/education/spy-overnight-gap-strategy-fill-probability/
- **The best single pre-market directional variable found (gap size) delivers 49–57% across buckets** — indistinguishable from the base rate except in rare >1% gap sessions (~60%). If a single obvious variable can't beat a coin flip, a score of many weak variables will also struggle; expect **small, regime-dependent** improvements, not breakthroughs.
- **Published R² of return prediction:** Welch & Goyal show the classic predictors (dividend yield, ratios, rates) fail **out-of-sample** — OOS R² near zero or negative, most *hurt* a real investor: https://www.nber.org/papers/w10483 (RFS 2008 version: https://ideas.repec.org/a/oup/rfinst/v21y2008i4p1455-1508.html ). Campbell & Thompson confirm only marginal OOS gains: https://ideas.repec.org/a/oup/rfinst/v21y2008i4p1509-1531.html . That literature is monthly; **daily index return prediction is strictly harder** (lower signal-to-noise). Published daily anomalies (overnight momentum, intraday momentum) are economically meaningful *in aggregate* but explain a small share of daily variance (single-digit R² at best).
- **Realistic target for a well-built pre-market system: 55–60% same-day direction on the days it takes a strong stance; 50–55% on neutral days (i.e., correctly choosing to stand aside is itself the win).** Sustained >62–65% same-day direction claims should be treated as red flags for overfitting, look-ahead, or selection bias.
- **Reframe:** for NQ scalping, direction accuracy is not the profit engine. The profit engine is *asymmetry* — cutting losers fast, holding winners (the both-sides OR stat shows stops will be probed ~70% of days), trading with the liquidity regime (gamma/VIX), and sizing by realized range. A 53% direction system with 1.5R asymmetry beats a 60% system with 0.8R asymmetry.

# Explicit warnings (bias traps in what traders teach)

1. **Hindsight labeling (Power of 3, "distribution leg").** AMD phases are only identifiable after the day completes; every day can be retrofitted ("that was the manipulation"). The only operational form is the *pre-market setup* (price relative to pools + reclaim rules) — which, as shown in §1.4, has no directional edge in the first break itself. Anyone showing "obvious" AMD examples is showing survivorship.
2. **Survivorship in guru/vendor stats.** TradingView strategy lists and ICT "win rate" screenshots are selected. The one systematic engine found reports ~45% standalone OB win rates (near base rate) in crypto — the honest base expectation for unfiltered SMC patterns on NQ too.
3. **Look-ahead in data:**
   - COT: Tuesday snapshot, Friday 15:30 release. Backtests that align Tuesday positions with Tuesday prices cheat; you can only trade it from Friday close.
   - AAII: survey week ends Wednesday, published Thursday morning — next-week tests must use Thursday+ data.
   - Initial Balance, POC, VA, VAH/VAL, ORB rails are not knowable at 09:30; systems that "bias at the open" using them are leaking the first 60 minutes.
   - Gap definitions on continuous futures must be roll-adjusted; using unadjusted contracts inflates gap stats.
4. **"Red folder = bearish" is wrong.** The announcement premium is *positive* (Savor-Wilson; Lucca-Moench). Flat/small pre-event is a volatility-management rule, not a bearish bias. Framing it as bearish is narrative.
5. **Narrative macro (DXY/10Y/BTC/crude) dressed as signal.** Correlations are time-varying and regime-dependent (Connolly-Stivers-Sun); fixed-sign rules silently curve-fit the current regime (e.g., 2022's "yields up = NQ down"). Condition on VIX regime or drop them.
6. **"VIX high = buy" survivorship.** From all-time-high vantage every dip looks like a sale; risk-adjusted tests (Elm Wealth 1990–2026) show buying VIX spikes *reduces* Sharpe vs static — the popular rule has it backwards at the portfolio level. For scalpers VIX's real signal is *range and sizing*, not direction.
7. **"The gap always fills" is false in the tails.** ~60% overall, but >80pt NQ gaps fill only 38% — the fade rule that prints in calm years blows up exactly on repricing days (2020, 2022, Aug-2024 style). Size fades by the fill-probability bucket and kill them before noon (>80% of fills).
8. **Multiplicity/data-snooping.** With dozens of candidate factors, some will look significant by chance; apply Harvey-Liu-Zhu-style thresholds (t>3) or bootstrap; validate walk-forward on NQ specifically, not ES-proxied stats, with costs (NQ round-trip ≈ 2–3 ticks) included.
9. **Vendor stats are marketing-adjacent priors.** Steady Turtle / tradingstats / stockwirex numbers are plausible, large-sample, and NQ-specific, but use proprietary data and sell indicators; treat as [B] priors to be replicated on your own data before weighting heavily. (Your repo already has NQ data infra — replicate the gap/PDH/ALN tables first.)

# Seasonal almanac — every calendar window, measured

> First measurement pass over the full NQ archive: **649 sessions** (2023-12-18
> → 2026-10-02), canonical split 2026-01-01 (471 train / 177 test days).
> Machinery: `web/scripts/seasonalAlmanac.ts` — day-level windows (Part A),
> hour-of-day drift (Part B), and the same windows sliced across the momentum
> card replay (Part C, esStudy discipline: MOM_PROD flush + EXP_PROD,
> sequential one-trade-at-a-time, pessimistic same-bar exit, 0.5 pt cost,
> 60-bar exit, Wilson CIs).
>
> Conventions: session date = RTH calendar date; day return = close-to-close
> of the session's last traded minute (weekend/halt gaps count); hours in ET;
> NQ points. FOMC = Fed decision days (official calendar), holidays = CME
> full-close days, early closes flagged separately.
>
> **Headline:** the card's edge is NOT uniform across the clock or the
> calendar. FOMC days are the best cell in the whole overlay (83.8% WR, train
> 81.7 / test 89.3), the day *before* FOMC is the worst (67.4%, test 53.1),
> entry hours 3–7 ET run 79–83% WR with train/test agreement, and 95% of all
> NQ drift lives in the overnight leg — the RTH leg is a coin flip. Everything
> below is lift-vs-baseline on cells, never a standalone signal.

---

## 1. Session legs — the overnight anomaly, measured on NQ

Close-to-close day return split into three legs (n = 648/649):

| Leg | n | up% | mean pts | Σ pts | train | test |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| preRTH (17:00 CT → 08:30 CT) | 648 | 57.7% | +20.9 | **+13,542** | +21.5 | +19.4 |
| RTH (08:30 → 14:59 CT) | 649 | 52.7% | +0.7 | +461 | −3.7 | +12.4 |
| tail (14:59 → 15:59 CT) | 649 | 46.4% | +0.3 | +206 | +0.5 | −0.1 |

**95% of the archive's total drift (+14,209 pts) sits in the overnight leg.**
The RTH leg is a coin flip (52.7% up, mean +0.7). This is the Lou–Polk–Skouras
overnight anomaly replicated on NQ futures with our own data — and it is the
single strongest *validation of the Globex-only execution window* in the whole
playbook. It also explains why the momentum card produces **zero RTH entries**
in Part C (all 3,266 trades are Globex): the card's tape conditions simply
don't form during the dead-leg hours.

**Adopted as evidence for the existing constraint — no change needed.**

## 2. Day-of-week (close-to-close drift)

| Day | n | up% | mean pts | train | test |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Mon | 120 | **65.0%** | **+80.2** | 67% / +72.8 | 60% / +102.5 |
| Wed | 137 | 56.9% | +50.2 | 59% / +49.1 | 53% / +53.1 |
| Fri | 127 | 56.7% | −10.3 | 58% / −8.8 | 54% / −14.3 |
| Tue | 131 | 52.7% | +6.7 | 53% / −1.6 | 51% / +29.4 |
| Thu | 133 | **45.1%** | −14.5 | 45% / −20.5 | 46% / −0.1 |

Monday is the strongest day (lift 1.18, positive in both windows); Thursday is
the only consistently negative day (lift 0.82). The Monday effect is a known
Globex phenomenon — the Sunday-evening reopen gap lands in Monday's
close-to-close. n ≈ 120–137 per cell, Wilson CIs ±8.

**Day-level: informative only (long-only bias). For the card: see §6 — no
dow cell moves the card's WR meaningfully (all 74.7–77.6%).**

## 3. Month-of-year (close-to-close drift)

| Month | n | up% | mean pts | train | test |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Jun | 52 | 65.4% | +57.5 | 72% / +90.0 | 55% / +5.5 |
| Sep | 57 | 61.4% | +55.9 | 62% / +53.6 | 60% / +60.2 |
| May | 58 | 60.3% | +92.9 | 57% / +65.0 | 67% / +154.9 |
| Apr | 63 | 60.3% | +50.4 | 55% / −12.4 | 71% / +176.1 |
| Jul | 61 | 45.9% | −35.1 | 55% / +1.9 | 29% / −105.6 |
| Mar | 57 | 47.4% | −37.9 | 53% / −27.6 | 35% / −62.1 |

n ≈ 46–63 per cell and the train/test columns disagree in both directions —
exactly the month-effect noise the S&P folklore predicts (and why the video's
out-of-sample warning matters). September's positive drift here is the
**opposite** of the classic "worst month" claim: do not import SPX calendar
folklore into NQ directly.

**Not adopted at day level.** The card-level month cells (§6) tell a cleaner
story: Jan strong, Jun weak — consistent across train/test.

## 4. Event windows (close-to-close drift)

| Window | n | up% | mean pts | train | test |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| FOMC day | 21 | 66.7% | +68.3 | 75% / +116.6 | 40% / −86.3 (n=5) |
| pre-FOMC day | 21 | **38.1%** | **−70.4** | 44% / −31.4 | 20% / −195.3 |
| **24h pre-FOMC** (13:00 CT → 13:00 CT) | 21 | **71.4%** | **+94.2** | 63% / +99.0 | 100% / +78.9 (n=5) |
| pre-holiday | 28 | 60.7% | +36.1 | 62% / +37.6 | 57% / +31.6 |
| OPEX day | 33 | 60.6% | +30.6 | 63% / +35.3 | 56% / +18.3 |
| quarter-turn | 57 | 52.6% | −31.3 | 55% / −11.6 | 47% / −86.4 |

The **24h window into the FOMC announcement is positive on NQ** (+94 pts,
71% up) — the Lucca–Moench pre-announcement drift replicates here. The full
pre-FOMC *day* is negative because the drift starts mid-session; the
close-to-close day includes the drag before it. Quarter-turn shows nothing.
The FOMC-day row itself flips in test (n=5) — too thin at day level; the
card-level FOMC cells (§6) are the real signal.

**Not adopted at day level (small n); the actionable FOMC findings are in §6.**

## 5. Hour-of-day drift (long 1h, open-to-open; the MatFinOg measurement on NQ)

n = 649 per hour; net = gross − 0.5 pt. Strongest hours:

| Hour ET | up% | gross | net | train | test |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **13** | 53.8% | +6.35 | **+5.85** | +5.36 | +9.00 |
| 3 | 53.6% | +3.50 | +3.00 | +3.64 | +3.14 |
| 20 | 54.5% | +2.72 | +2.22 | +1.69 | +5.47 |
| 2 | 53.6% | +2.31 | +1.81 | +1.09 | +5.57 |
| 6 | 57.2% | +2.04 | +1.54 | +1.30 | +4.01 |
| 14 | 48.8% | −3.80 | **−4.30** | −1.57 | −9.75 |
| 10 | 51.9% | −2.33 | −2.83 | −3.96 | +2.04 |
| 9 | 51.9% | −2.11 | −2.61 | −2.51 | −1.04 |
| 0 | 50.7% | −1.43 | −1.93 | −1.47 | −1.34 |
| 22 | 49.0% | −2.06 | −2.56 | −0.07 | −7.35 |

Contrast with the video's ES 2018–2026 result: on NQ 2023–2026 the overnight
drift concentrates at 2–3 and 6 ET, the single best hour is **13 ET** (not in
the video's list), and hour 21 ET shows the classic fake-bias signature
(train +4.4 / test −5.1). Hours 9–10 ET (the video's "worst hour to be long")
are negative here too. Hour 14 ET is the most consistent short-drift hour.

**Adopted as context only.** Per-hour raw drift is not a trade; it is the
regime the card trades inside. The overlay in §6 turns it into card-level
facts.

## 6. The momentum-card overlay — where the money is

3,266 sequential trades, baseline **76.8% WR / PF 2.92 / avg +2.38 pts**
(train 75.6% / 2.59, test 79.6% / 3.67). Cells that beat baseline **and
agree across train/test**:

| Cell | n | WR | PF | train | test |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **FOMC day** | 99 | **83.8%** | **5.16** | 81.7% / 4.05 | 89.3% / 9.90 |
| **entry hour 4 ET** | 122 | 82.8% | 4.35 | 80.9% / 3.43 | 87.9% / 7.86 |
| **entry hour 7 ET** | 183 | 81.4% | 3.57 | 79.4% / 2.98 | 88.1% / 5.86 |
| **January** | 317 | 82.3% | 4.20 | 82.1% / 3.76 | 82.6% / 4.70 |
| hour 5 ET | 219 | 79.9% | 3.36 | 79.6% / 2.88 | 80.6% / 4.54 |
| hour 3 ET | 168 | 79.8% | 3.17 | 78.0% / 2.77 | 84.4% / 4.08 |
| pre-holiday | 175 | 79.4% | 3.33 | 78.6% / 2.93 | 82.9% / 4.93 |
| month last-day | 173 | 80.9% | 4.18 | 77.1% / 2.94 | 92.9% / 15.21 (n=42) |
| month first-3 | 490 | 78.4% | 3.35 | 76.7% / 3.00 | 82.5% / 4.16 |

Cells that underperform **with agreement**:

| Cell | n | WR | PF | train | test |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **pre-FOMC day** | 138 | **67.4%** | **1.64** | 71.7% / 1.90 | 53.1% / 1.17 |
| **June** | 274 | 71.9% | 2.27 | 71.9% / 1.99 | 71.8% / 2.57 |
| entry hour 16 ET | 78 | 66.7% | 1.92 | 62.3% / 1.56 | 82.4% / 6.33 (n=17) |
| post-holiday | 132 | 72.7% | 2.31 | 70.7% / 2.26 | 76.0% / 2.37 |
| OPEX week | 656 | 73.8% | 2.52 | 71.2% / 2.08 | 78.5% / 3.46 |

Day-of-week on the card: flat (Tue 74.7% ↔ Thu 77.6%) — the day-level Monday
drift does not translate into card edge, which is expected: the card already
selects its tape.

### Verdicts

- **FOMC-day tier-up: ADOPT as a journal chip** (`FOMC DAY` label on the
  card, like the ES chips — never a gate). Best cell in the study, 99 trades,
  train/test agree, and the day-level FOMC drift explains *why* it should hold.
- **Pre-FOMC stand-aside: ADOPT as a chip with caution** (`PRE-FOMC` label).
  The day before FOMC is the worst cell (PF 1.64 vs 2.92 baseline) and the
  day-level pre-FOMC day is negative — two independent measurements agree.
- **Entry hours 3–7 ET: ADOPT as the prime window label.** Four consecutive
  hours at 79–83% WR with train/test agreement, sitting exactly on the
  overnight-drift leg. Not a filter (the card is thin at other hours and the
  trade still pays), but the hours worth highest conviction.
- **January strong / June weak: journal-only seasonal chips.** The only two
  month cells stable across train/test; both are well-known NQ seasonality
  (tax-loss + rebalance vs. mid-year chop).
- **Month last-day (92.9% test, n=42) and hour 16 ET (66.7%): monitor, do not
  adopt.** Test cells are tiny; the honest read is "unstable".
- **OPEX week: no adoptable edge** (train below baseline, test above — split
  in the middle).

**Implemented 2026-10-05:** the three adopted chips live in
`web/lib/seasonal.ts` (`seasonalChips()`, 13 unit tests) and print on the
momentum card via `web/lib/signalFeed.ts` in the same chip line as the ES
chips — labels only, never gates. `PRE-FOMC` prints only when the day is not
itself a decision day (mutually exclusive by construction). PLAYBOOK.md
carries the chip inventory.

## 7. Method notes and limits

- **Multiple testing:** ~150 cells were measured. The adopted cells are the
  ones with train/test agreement and a mechanism (FOMC drift, overnight
  anomaly), which is the practical substitute for a formal FDR pass; run one
  before any cell becomes a *gate*.
- **Single split, one instrument, 2.8 years.** Month cells especially are
  n ≈ 46–63 — seasonality numbers always need the longest archive available.
  The ES twin can be added with the same script (`loadEsMinutes`).
- The video's lesson reproduced on our own tape: cells that look great
  in-sample and die out-of-sample are everywhere (hour 21 ET, day-level FOMC
  day, month last-day drift). Only train/test agreement survives.

## Regenerate

```bash
cd web
GC_REMOTE_URL=$(grep GC_REMOTE_URL .env.local | cut -d= -f2) \
  node --import ../scripts/ts-loader.mjs scripts/seasonalAlmanac.ts \
  --dump /tmp/almanac.json
```

# ALN / structure study — external base rates replicated on our archive (2026-10-09, standard format 2026-10-10)

> Question: *"do the Steady Turtle structure tables (overnight breaks,
> PDH/PDL hit rates, ALN patterns, gap-fill buckets) hold on OUR 654-session
> archive?"* CLI: `web/scripts/alnStructureStudy.ts`.

## Method

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Instrument / session | NQ 1-min · full session; bars in CT |
| Sample | 2023-12-18 → 2026-10-09 · 654 sessions |
| Cost model | n/a — base-rate study, no trades |

| Split | n/a — descriptive base rates (external-vs-ours comparison) |
| Significance | count-based rates; CIs omitted (n=654 per rate — ±3.8 pts at 50%) |
| CLI | `web/scripts/alnStructureStudy.ts` |

## Results

> **Standard deviation note:** descriptive base-rate study, no trades — the
> T1 core-quality and T4 prop-viability tables do not apply; the comparison
> table below is the study's native output.

| Rate | Steady Turtle (NQ 2020→mid-2026) | OURS (654 sessions) |
|---|---|---|
| RTH breaks ≥1 overnight extreme | 94.7% (H 63.2% · L 56.3%) | **97.1%** (H 66.8% · L 61.9%) |
| breaks BOTH overnight extremes | 24.8% | **31.7%** |
| hits ≥1 of PDH/PDL | 89.5% (PDH 55.2% · PDL 44.3%) | **88.1%** (PDH 55.8% · PDL 41.0%) |
| sweeps both PDH+PDL | 10.1% | **8.7%** |
| inside day (neither) | 10.5% | **11.8%** |
| ALN mix P1/P2/P3/P4 | 23% / 4–6% / 41% / 30% | **22.0% / 7.2% / 40.8% / 30.0%** |
| P3 → NY breaks London H vs L | 81.3% vs 67.5% | **77.2% vs 64.4%** |
| P4 → NY breaks London L vs H | 74.5% vs 67.9% | **72.4% vs 69.4%** |
| gap fill <10pt / 40–80 / ≥80pt | 96.4% / 63.8% / 38.1% | **97.4% (n=38) / 65.5% / 38.6% (n=368)** |
| gap fill overall | 60.3% | **57.6%** (653 gapped sessions) |

## What this falsifies and what it confirms

1. **Confirmed: every structural base rate holds on our tape.** The only
   systematic difference (ON-low break 61.9% vs 56.3%) is the 2023–2026
   up-drift, not disagreement.
2. **Confirmed: the ALN P3/P4 directional lean replicates** — P3 favors the
   London high by ~13 pts, P4 flips to the London low (both datasets agree
   on direction). This is the strongest pre-market directional stat in the
   external audit, now first-party.
3. **Falsified: nothing.** The vendor tables are credible priors that
   survive replication — the daily-bias framework's structure layer is
   first-party verified.

## Honest bounds

- Gap opens use the mid fallback (the archive's first-RTH opens are sparse);
  a true-open run would tighten the small-gap buckets (n=38 for <10 pt).
- No ES twin pass yet — the same script runs on `loadEsMinutes` if needed.
- Not a trade study: base rates only, no replay/P&L. The actionable form
  (tag-and-react at these levels) is the next study.

```bash
node --env-file=.env.local --import ../scripts/ts-loader.mjs scripts/alnStructureStudy.ts
```
