# A+ plan hardening — making a blow ~impossible without losing the month (2026-10-05)

## The question

*What can we change so blowing the eval becomes virtually impossible (needs an
abnormal streak), while keeping time-to-pass reasonable (≈1 month)?*

Method: the A+ plan's day engine (`web/lib/apPlan.ts`) swept over its own knobs
(risk cap, daily stop, profit arm, target R) plus two state-aware protection
layers (drawdown-aware and streak-aware half-sizing), replayed over all 650
sessions and pushed through the exact Rapid EOD 50k eval gates (10,000 random
day orderings per config). Re-run: `web/scripts/apPlanSweep.ts`.

The blow mechanism first: the MLL is **end-of-day trailing** — you blow when
cumulative P&L sits $2,000 below the running peak. So blow risk is about the
DEPTH OF RED STREAKS, not any single day. `streak2blow` below = how many
straight worst-case days it takes from any peak; `longestRed` = the longest
consecutive red-day streak that ever actually occurred in 2.5 years.

## Results (ranked by blow probability)

| Config | P(blow) | Med days | p25–p90 | ≤60d | Worst day | streak2blow | longestRed | Chrono |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **100/-300/1R** | **0.0%** | 28 | 23–43 | 99% | −$410 | 5 | 4 | PASS day 30 |
| **100/-250/1R** | **0.0%** | 29 | 23–45 | 99% | −$361 | 6 | 4 | PASS day 30 |
| 100/-200/1R | 0.0% | 30 | 24–46 | 98% | −$325 | 7 | 4 | PASS day 30 |
| dd600→half /-250/1R | 0.0% | 30 | 24–48 | 97% | −$361 | 6 | 4 | PASS day 30 |
| **125/-250/1R** | **0.1%** | **24** | 18–38 | 100% | −$392 | 6 | 4 | PASS day 27 |
| 125/-200/1R | 0.1% | 24 | 19–39 | 100% | −$352 | 6 | 4 | PASS day 28 |
| dd600→quarter /-250/2R | 0.0% | 42 | 25–97 | 69% | −$374 | 6 | 6 | PASS day 109 |
| dd600→half /-250/2R | 0.2% | 37 | 24–78 | 79% | −$374 | 6 | 6 | PASS day 52 |
| dd800→half /-250/2R | 0.3% | 35 | 23–73 | 82% | −$374 | 6 | 6 | PASS day 52 |
| 100/-250/1.5R | 0.6% | 32 | 23–56 | 93% | −$374 | 6 | 6 | PASS day 50 |
| red2→half /-250/2R | 1.6% | 35 | 24–66 | 86% | −$374 | 6 | 6 | PASS day 51 |
| 100/-250/2R | 3.0% | 32 | 23–59 | 91% | −$374 | 6 | 6 | PASS day 52 |
| **current 100/-300/2R** | **~3–4%** | 31 | 22–58 | 92% | −$422 | 5 | 6 | PASS day 69 |
| 150/-250/2R (speed ref) | 15.2% | 28 | 19–52 | 95% | −$423 | 5 | 6 | PASS day 30 |

## Readings

1. **The 2R target is the root cause of the blow risk.** At 2R the A+ win
   rate collapses from ~75–80% (native targets) to ~50%, which is where the
   deep red streaks come from. At **1R the same setups win ~3 of 4**, the day
   series smooths out, and **0 of 10,000 orderings blow** — while the median
   time-to-pass IMPROVES (28–29 trading days vs 31–32) and the chronological
   path passes on day 30 instead of day 69. Lower target = less variance, not
   less edge: per-trade expectancy in R is ~0.55R at 1R vs ~0.51R at 2R.
2. **The streak proof of "virtually impossible"**: at 100/-250/1R, blowing
   needs **6 consecutive near-worst days** (−$361 each) from a peak; the
   longest red streak the archive ever produced is **4 days** — and those were
   not worst days. Even 4 straight worst days (−$1,444) stays $556 above the
   floor. To blow you need a streak that has never existed in the data.
3. **Bigger size is poison, not a shortcut.** 150/-250/2R passes a hair
   faster (28 days) but blows 15% of the time. The only safe way to buy speed
   is 100→125 at 1R: median drops 29→**24 trading days (~5.5 weeks)** at
   0.1% blow (1 in 1,000, still needing a 6-straight-worst-day streak vs a
   realized max of 4).
4. **If you insist on keeping 2R**: the drawdown-aware half-size rule
   (trade half size once the challenge drawdown from peak hits $600, resume
   full at $300) brings blow to ~0.2% — but pass slows to ~37 days / 8.5
   weeks (chrono day 52). Keeping 2R costs you the month.
5. **Why this matters right now**: the current plan's actual chronological
   path came within **$118 of the trailing floor on 2025-06-03** (the funded
   phase, the same date the no-rules variant breached). The eval would have
   passed (2024-04-15), but the 2R variance nearly killed the funded account
   a year later.

## The recommendation

**Trade the A+ pool at 1R with the −$250 daily stop and the $100 cap**
(same setups, same sizing math, tighter stop, 1R target):

- blow: 0 in 10,000 random orderings (needs a 6-day worst-case streak; max
  ever observed: 4)
- pass: median **29 trading days (~6.5 weeks)**, p75 37, p90 45, 99% within
  60 trading days; chronological path passes on day 30
- if you want the fastest safe variant: **$125 cap, −$200 stop, 1R** —
  median **24 trading days (~5.5 weeks)**, p90 39, 0.1% blow

Honest limit: with A+ setups ONLY, no config reaches a 1-month MEDIAN
(≈22 trading days) — the 1R space tops out around 24–29. The only levers that
get under a month are adding more daily edge (e.g. trading the regular RTH
card alongside A+) or accepting the 15% blow risk of bigger size — neither is
in this table by design; ask for the A+ + RTH-card variant if you want it
measured.

## Caveats (standing)

Mid-bar archive entries, pessimistic first-touch scoring, 0.5 pt cost +
commissions, no news gaps, every signal taken when flat; MC destroys serial
correlation (brackets any start date, not just Dec 2023). State-aware rules
switch at day boundaries — exact, since the floor itself only trails at
closes. The 0.0% figures are 0 in 10,000 samples, not mathematical zeros.

*Educational research only — not financial advice.*

# A+ daily-rules backtest — $100 risk · 2R · −$300 day stop · +$400 one-more-trade (2026-10-05)

## The plan under test

The owner's day plan, backtested exactly as stated, on A+ setups only:

1. **Dollar risk capped at $100/trade** → `contracts = floor(100 ÷ (riskPts × $2))`,
   floored at 1 MNQ ($2/pt).
2. **Profit target $200 (2R)** → target = entry ± 2 × structural stop distance.
3. **Daily stop**: if the day loses $300, stop trading for the day.
4. **Daily profit rule**: once the day makes $400, ONE more trade is allowed;
   a win grants one more; the FIRST loss after crossing +$400 ends the day.
5. **A+ setups only** — the two A+ tiers the live cards print:
   - **mom A+** — momentum trigger + expansion trigger on the SAME bar
     ("A+ both triggers", Globex hours only) — `web/lib/signalFeed.ts` §checkMomentum
   - **rth A+** — RTH continuation with ≥65% one-sidedness
     (breakFrac ≥ 0.65 long / ≤ 0.35 short, 9:30–16:00 ET) — `web/lib/signalFeed.ts` §checkRth

Replay: `web/scripts/apRulesStudy.ts` over all 650 usable sessions
(2023-12 → 2026-09, 597 sessions with A+ signals). Mechanics shared with
every other study in this repo: signals globally sequenced
one-position-at-a-time, first-touch scoring with the pessimistic stop-first
rule, 0.5 pt round-trip cost, 60-bar hold (RTH capped at the 15:00 bar),
$0.95/contract/side commission. The mom-A+ representative is the expansion
signal of the overlap (the established A+ convention from
`momentumStudy --mode overlap`); the live card's momentum stop differs by
<1 pt on the same bar.

## 1. The A+ pool under 2R mechanics

| Pool | Signals | Sessions | 2R WR | Stop % | Med risk | Med MNQ | Net $ |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| mom A+ | 1,336 | 502 | **50.5%** | 49.1% | 4.4 pts | 11 | +$25,240 |
| rth A+ | 1,460 | 466 | **49.2%** | 50.6% | 7.1 pts | 7 | +$35,207 |

The 2R target trades win rate for R: the same A+ tiers measure **78.9%**
(mom, 1R) and **80.1%** (rth, 0.75R) at their native targets. At 2R the
win rate halves to ~50% but the edge survives — net expectancy stays
positive in every full year (see §3).

Trade anatomy (base, n = 2,796): median win **+$162**, median loss **−$121**.
The "$200 target" is gross: the median gross 2R target is $190 (cap sizing
rounds contracts down), and 0.5 pt cost + commission bring realized wins to
~$160. Realized stop-outs exceed $100 by the same costs (~$120).

## 2. The rules, one layer at a time

Same pool, same sizing, only the rules differ:

| Variant | Trades | WR | Net $ | Median day | Worst day | P(≥$400) | Halted days | Eval sim | Funded |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| base (no rules) | 2,796 | 50% | **+$60,447** | +$72 | **−$912** | 15% | 0 | **BREACH 2025-06-03** | breach |
| loss-300 only | 2,555 | 50% | +$57,747 | +$71 | −$422 | 15% | 70 | PASS 2024-04-12 | 112 payouts |
| profit-400 only | 2,591 | 50% | +$57,261 | +$77 | −$912 | 14% | 58 | BREACH 2025-06-03 | breach |
| **full plan** | 2,362 | 51% | **+$54,343** | +$71 | **−$422** | 13% | 127 (69+58) | **PASS 2024-04-15** | 105 payouts |

- **The −$300 stop is the account-saving rule.** It costs ~$2,700 over 2.5
  years (4.5% of the edge) and converts the MyFundedFutures Rapid EOD 50k
  eval from BREACH to PASS. The base breach is NOT a single bad day — the
  worst day (−$912) is well inside the $2,000 MLL. It is a multi-day bleed
  into the END-OF-DAY trailing floor (2025-06-03); capping each red day at
  ~−$420 keeps the cumulative drawdown above the trailing floor.
- **The +$400 one-more-trade rule is profit protection, not account
  protection.** It costs ~$3,200 (5%), fires on ~1 day in 7 (111 of 597),
  and ends 58 of those days at median +$392 (worst +$274) instead of letting
  them run — it trims the best-day tail ($1,600 → $1,158) but leaves the
  worst day untouched. On its own it still breaches.
- **The full plan keeps 90% of the total edge** (+$54,343 vs +$60,447),
  halves the worst day (−$912 → −$422), passes the eval on 2024-04-15 with
  consistency ✓, and pays out 105 times in the funded sim.

## 3. Per year (full plan vs base)

| Year | Base | Full plan |
|---|---|---|
| 2023 (Dec only) | −$1,153 | −$1,006 |
| 2024 | +$24,095 | +$20,379 |
| 2025 | +$13,215 | +$12,820 |
| 2026 (out-of-sample) | +$24,290 | +$22,151 |

The edge survives the rules in every full year, including the 2026
out-of-sample window. 2025 is the weak year in both.

## 4. How full-plan days end (597 trading days)

| Ending | Days | Median P&L | Worst |
|---|---|---|---|
| session end, no halt | 470 | +$81 | −$285 |
| halted: loss rule (−$300) | 69 | −$372 | −$422 |
| halted: profit rule (+$400) | 58 | +$392 | +$274 |

Two honest asymmetries worth knowing:

- A halted red day ends BELOW −$300 (median −$372): the trade that crosses
  the line finishes, and halted days can no longer recover — so the share of
  days closing ≤ −$300 ROSE from 7% (base) to 12% (full). The rule buys a
  shallow worst day, not a shorter list of red days.
- Profit-halt days all end ≥ +$274 — the rule locks the day in near the
  +$400 peak, at the cost of the big green tail (best day $1,600 → $1,158).

## 5. Challenge timing — how long to pass the eval

`web/scripts/apChallengeTiming.ts` feeds the full plan's 597 day P&Ls
(median +$71, best +$1,158, worst −$422) through the exact Rapid EOD 50k
eval gates from a fresh start ($3,000 target, EOD trailing MLL $2,000
locking at $100, 4 min days, best-day ≤ 30% at pass). 10,000 random day
orderings ≈ any start date; the archive runs ~4.4 sessions/week.

| Scenario | P(pass) | P(blow) | Med days | p25 | p75 | p90 | ≤20 days | ≤60 days | Med calendar |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| full plan | 97% | 3% | **32** | 22 | 44 | 58 | 19% | 92% | ~7 weeks |
| ×0.5 (live lags) | 100% | 0% | 63 | 49 | 81 | 100 | 0% | 45% | ~14 weeks |
| ×0.25 (conservative) | 100% | 0% | 129 | 109 | 152 | 176 | 0% | 0% | ~29 weeks |
| base, no rules | 96% | 4% | 30 | 21 | 42 | 55 | 23% | 94% | ~7 weeks |

- **The actual chronological path** (starting 2023-12-18, through that
  month's −$1,006 hole): pass 2024-04-15 — **69 trading days, ~119 calendar
  days (~17 weeks)**, equity $3,626 at pass, consistency ✓. One path; the MC
  median is the better "typical" estimate.
- **The consistency gate rarely binds in expectation** (median equity
  required at pass = $3,000 exactly); it only bites when the +$1,158 best
  day lands before the target — then you need $3,860 total instead of
  $3,000.
- Blow risk (~3%) is the EOD trailing MLL doing its job: a random run of red
  days deep enough to sit $2,000 below the running peak. The −$300 daily
  stop is what keeps that probability near zero instead of compounding
  (base's chronological path actually breached in 2025-06-03).
- The ×0.5 / ×0.25 rows bracket live underperformance (the live bot has
  historically trailed the backtest — `docs/research/live-vs-backtest-2026-10-05.md`):
  half the edge ≈ double the time (~14 weeks); a quarter ≈ ~29 weeks.

Follow-up: `docs/research/ap-plan-hardening-2026-10-05.md` sweeps the plan's
knobs (target R, daily stop, risk cap, drawdown-aware sizing) — the 1R
target turns blow into 0/10,000 while passing FASTER (29 vs 32 days median).

## Caveats (same standing ones as every study)

1. Archive entries are mid-bar (no true closes); live enters at the real
   close. First-touch scoring is pessimistic (stop first when both sit in
   one bar). The 0.5 pt cost is charged; real slippage in thin hours varies.
2. No news gaps, no execution misses — every A+ signal is taken when flat.
3. The mom-A+ ticket is the expansion signal of the overlap; the live card's
   momentum stop differs by <1 pt. Risk and contracts are therefore within
   1–2 micros of the live ticket.
4. Payout totals are sim numbers under the repo's account model; read the
   RATIOS (rule cost %, worst-day reduction, pass/breach), not the absolute
   dollars.

## Re-run

```bash
cd web && node --import ../scripts/ts-loader.mjs scripts/apRulesStudy.ts \
  [--offline] [--dump /tmp/aprules.json]
cd web && node --import ../scripts/ts-loader.mjs scripts/apChallengeTiming.ts \
  [--offline]
```

*Educational research only — not financial advice.*

| **current 100/-300/2R** | **3.1%** | 15 d | **73.9%** | 15.0% | 9 d | −$428 | 5 |

Longest consecutive red-day streak in 2.5 years of realized data: **4**
(1R configs) vs 6 (2R). The 1R configs need a 6-straight-worst-day streak
to blow from any peak — a streak the data has never produced.

## The recommendation

1. **Trade the full pool (regular + A+).** It is what makes the timeline
   work: eval median 10–15 trading days (~2–3 weeks), p90 ≤ 27 days.
2. **Drop the target from 2R to 1R and tighten the daily stop to −$250.**
   Same setups, same $100 sizing, −$250 stop, 1R target: funded blow
   **0.3% over 2.5 years** (0.1% within 90 days) vs 73.9% at 2R, first
   payout in ~6 trading days, chronological eval pass on day 16.
3. **Optional belt-and-suspenders:** the drawdown-aware rule — trade at
   half size ($50) whenever the challenge drawdown from its peak ≥ $600,
   back to full at $300. That takes funded blow to **0.0% in 10,000
   orderings** with the same ~10-day eval.

The 2R target is the funded-killer: it halves the win rate to ~50% and
produces the red clusters that feed the trailing MLL. Keeping 2R forces a
choice between blow safety and speed (the dd-quarter 2R row: 0.1% blow
but 18-day median) — 1R wins both.

## Caveats (standing)

Mid-bar archive entries, pessimistic first-touch scoring, 0.5 pt cost +
commissions, no news gaps, every signal taken when flat; MC destroys
serial correlation (brackets any start date). State-aware rules switch at
day boundaries — exact, since the floor only trails at closes. 0.0% means
0 in 10,000 samples, not a mathematical zero. The eval floor-lock-at-
starting-balance assumption should be confirmed with MFF support.

*Educational research only — not financial advice.*

# Sizing dynamics — Option A vs Option B (2026-10-02)

The question: keep the same size in drawdown and SHRINK as the day's profit
climbs (Option A — the live tiers), or shrink as we lose and GROW as we win,
never risking more than the day's P&L (Option B — house-money scaling)?

Method: the same trade stream as the risk-stack study (momentum + expansion
+ RTH + open drive, globally sequenced one-position-at-a-time, fixed 1R-style
exits, 0.5 pt cost + $0.95/side commissions), give-back halt ON for every
scheme so ONLY sizing differs. Runner: `scripts/sizingDynamicsStudy.ts`,
649 sessions, MFF Rapid EOD 50k sim (eval + funded).

## The table

| Scheme | Trades | Total | Med day | Worst | DayVol | P≥$500 | P≥$900 | >$900d | avgC | $/vol |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| flat (same size always) | 13,802 | +$533k | +$775 | −$1,372 | $738 | 61% | 43% | 277 | 12.2 | 723 |
| **tiers (OPTION A, live)** | 14,453 | +$378k | +$687 | −$1,372 | **$418** | 64% | **24%** | **156** | 9.4 | **905** |
| lossHalve (×0.5 per loss) | 14,052 | +$509k | +$733 | −$1,306 | $704 | 60% | 40% | 260 | 11.1 | 723 |
| lossQuarter (×0.75 per loss) | 13,836 | +$523k | +$753 | −$1,382 | $727 | 59% | 41% | 268 | 11.7 | 720 |
| winScaleRaw (×1.5 per win) | 11,659 | +$570k | +$566 | **−$1,678** | **$964** | 52% | 41% | 265 | 14.6 | 591 |
| winScale (×1.5 + day-P&L cap) | 5,368 | +$256k | −$20 | −$249 | $880 | 25% | 20% | 128 | 14.1 | 291 |
| greenBudget (day-P&L cap only) | 6,444 | +$250k | −$16 | −$249 | $743 | 31% | 23% | 147 | 11.9 | 336 |
| floorFractional (8.5% of equity−floor) | 12,765 | +$520k | +$563 | **−$1,125** | $847 | 52% | 38% | 247 | 12.6 | 614 |
| **b-full (OPTION B verbatim)** | 5,368 | +$253k | −$20 | −$249 | $869 | 25% | 20% | 127 | 13.9 | 291 |
| tiers+lossHalve (A + B's drawdown leg) | 14,843 | +$371k | +$669 | −$1,306 | $393 | 63% | 19% | 124 | 8.5 | **943** |

## Findings

1. **Option A wins.** Tiers have the best risk-adjusted return (total ÷ daily
   volatility: 905 vs 723 flat), the lowest dayVol (−43%), and cut >$900 days
   277 → 156 and P(≥$900) 43% → 24%. The cost is known and accepted: −29%
   of total vs flat, the price of the $900 consistency cap. Nothing in this
   study beats the adopted scheme on risk-adjusted terms.

2. **Option B breaches the funded account — invisibly.** winScale and b-full
   both breach 2026-04-28 (equity ≈ $203k) even though their worst single day
   is only −$249. The day-P&L ceiling protects each DAY; it does nothing
   against the rule that actually matters — the EOD **trailing** max loss,
   which breaches on a >$2,000 drawdown from the peak accumulated across any
   number of small capped-red days. The kill is invisible at the daily level.
   The eval "passes" only because the pass-stop ends the eval at +$3k; the
   funded stage trades on and dies. This is the trap in "never risk more than
   the day's P&L": per-day floors don't compose into a trailing-drawdown floor.

3. **Shrinking after losses buys ~nothing (IID confirmed).** lossHalve keeps
   95.5% of flat's total with a worst day of −$1,306 vs −$1,372 — a 4.5%
   donation of income for a 5% tail trim. lossQuarter keeps 98% with a
   WORSE worst day. Loss streaks don't predict losses, so loss-based sizing
   just scales edge down. Consistent with the stop-after-N-losses study.

4. **Growing after wins is leverage in disguise.** winScaleRaw makes +7%
   more total than flat — but avg contracts rise 12.2 → 14.6, worst day
   worsens −$1,372 → −$1,678 (22%), dayVol rises to the table's highest
   ($964), and $/vol falls to 591. Anything it "adds" is just more size on
   winning days, which the give-back halt then has to contain. If more money
   is wanted, raise the base budget — the same exposure with fewer moving parts.

5. **The house-money ceiling is the most expensive floor ever bought.**
   greenBudget caps the worst day at −$249 but keeps only 47% of flat's
   total and 46% of flat's $/vol. Compare the give-back halt: same day-floor
   intent at 10–24% cost. The ceiling costs ~53%.

6. **The one new idea that pays: floorFractional.** Risk = 8.5% ×
   (equity − EOD floor) per trade keeps 97.5% of flat's total while cutting
   the worst day to −$1,125 (−18%) — the best tail in the uncapped table.
   It shrinks exactly and only when the account approaches the MLL, which is
   where a shrink actually has value. $/vol (614) is below flat (723), so it
   is still a smoothing trade, not a free lunch — but it is the cheapest
   drawdown insurance measured so far. Candidate for the funded stage.

7. **tiers+lossHalve is a marginal upgrade of Option A**: $/vol 943 vs 905,
   >$900 days 124 vs 156, worst day −$1,306 vs −$1,372, at −2% total. Adding
   the loss-halving leg ON TOP of the tiers is the only place loss-shrinking
   shows any (small) value — the tiers already cap the upside, so the halving
   only touches the red tail.

## Recommendation

Keep Option A (tiers) as the live scheme. Do not adopt Option B — its day
cap cannot protect the trailing drawdown that is the actual account rule, and
the funded sim breaches. If deeper drawdown insurance is wanted, the measured
candidates are, in order of cost: tiers+lossHalve (−2% total), floorFractional
(−2.5% total, best tail), give-back halt (already live). Growing size into
wins is rejected: it adds variance faster than return.

# Overfitting-validation pipeline — DSR / PBO / CPCV (2026-10-04)

The backtests stopped having to *argue* they are not overfit: every family's
grid sweep now gets a multiple-testing-corrected audit computed from the same
replay data. This doc is the pipeline contract; the per-family numbers live
in `web/app/api/backtest/validation/reports/<family>-*.validation.json` (committed) and the `/backtest` page.

## Pipeline (three stages, one direction)

```
web/scripts/exportSweep.ts      TS grid replay (SAME detectors as live)
  --family momentum|expansion|rth --cost 0.95
  → gcdata/data/sweeps/<family>-<stamp>.json
      per config: per-session netUsd/riskUsd/trades/wins (1 MNQ)
      + appends web/app/api/backtest/validation/reports/trials.json (the trial ledger)

gcdata/validate_sweep.py        purgedcv audit (Python 3.14 venv)
  --holdout-last 40 = frozen single-use holdout (pinned in data/holdouts.json)
  → web/app/api/backtest/validation/reports/<sweep>.validation.json: PBO (CSCV) · DSR · PSR · MinTRL · MinBTL
      · per-year table · concentration · Sharpe heatmap · top-20 · pick series
      · holdout result + verdict · stamps the trial ledger entry

gcdata/optuna_view.py           viewer-only Optuna study (no search)
  → gcdata/data/optuna/<family>.db   (optuna-dashboard <db>)
```

Run (from `web/` for the sweep, from `gcdata/` for the rest):

```
export GC_REMOTE_URL=<r2 url from web/.env.local>
node --import ./tests/ts-loader.mjs ./scripts/exportSweep.ts --family rth --cost 0.95
../gcdata/.venv/bin/python validate_sweep.py ../gcdata/data/sweeps/rth-*.json --pick s0.45_t1.75_x45 --holdout-last 40
../gcdata/.venv/bin/python optuna_view.py ../gcdata/data/sweeps/rth-*.json --pick s0.45_t1.75_x45
../gcdata/.venv/bin/optuna-dashboard sqlite:///../gcdata/data/optuna/rth.db
```

## Frozen holdout (single-use)

`--holdout-last N` reserves the last N sessions (2026-08-06 → 2026-10-02 for
N=40) as a single-use out-of-sample window:

- The FIRST run that declares a holdout for a family pins `{N, pick}` in
  `web/app/api/backtest/validation/reports/holdouts.json` — the pin is immutable; later runs must reuse
  the same window and pick (goalpost-moving is refused with a warning).
- DSR / PBO / PSR / MinTRL / MinBTL / trial Sharpes / heatmap are all
  computed on the PRE-holdout sessions only; the pick is chosen on
  pre-holdout data (argmax when no `--pick` is given).
- The holdout result is reported separately (n, WR, net, Sharpe) and added
  to the verdict line and the `/backtest` card. Selection never sees it.
- Declaration order matters: the pick must be frozen BEFORE the holdout
  result is looked at. All three families were declared 2026-10-04 with
  their pre-existing picks (momentum/rth from the docs, expansion argmax on
  pre-holdout data).

## Metrics and thresholds

| Metric | What it answers | Pass band |
|---|---|---|
| **DSR** (deflated Sharpe) | is the pick's Sharpe beyond what `n_trials` configs produce by luck? | ≥ 0.95 strong, 0.80–0.95 moderate |
| **PBO** (prob. backtest overfitting, CSCV) | how often the IS-best config lands below the OOS median? | ≤ 0.20 stable, 0.20–0.40 gray |
| **slope** (IS vs OOS perf) | does in-sample strength carry out-of-sample? | only diagnostic when PBO > 0.20 |
| **PSR** | P(true Sharpe > 0) | ≥ 0.95 |
| **MinTRL** | sessions needed to establish the observed Sharpe at 95% | ≤ nSessions |
| **MinBTL** | years below which the annualised Sharpe is selection luck | advisory — per-session returns are far from iid-normal |
| **concentration** | share of net from the top-10 sessions | ≤ 15% good, ≤ 30% gray |

Units: one observation = one session; returns are per-session return-on-risk
(netUsd / riskUsd, 0 when the config did not trade). Trial Sharpes are computed
on the full history (in-sample), so `effective_n_trials` (autocorrelation
heuristic) is used for the deflation — raw count is also reported.

## Known interpretation traps (all observed on real data)

1. **Negative slope + tiny PBO is mechanical, not overfit.** When selection is
   stable the IS-best config is the *same* config in every CSCV combo, so its
   IS and OOS Sharpes are complementary halves of a fixed total — the
   regression slope goes negative by construction. The validator only flags
   the slope when PBO > 0.20.
2. **MinBTL is pessimistic for scalping.** Per-session return-on-risk has
   ~0 autocorrelation and high kurtosis; the iid-normal assumption behind the
   annualised null-max inflates the required years. Read it as a ceiling, not
   a gate.
3. **DSR can be 1.000 while selection is unreliable (momentum case).** The
   family has real edge (observed Sharpe far above the deflated benchmark),
   but the *argmax* config does not transfer — pick on plateaus, not peaks.

## First results (2026-10-04, 649 sessions, 0.95pt, 225 configs each, holdout = last 40)

| Family | Pick | DSR | PBO | observed SR | trials (eff/raw) | holdout (40 sess) | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| momentum | s0.35_t2.25_x60 (live) | **1.000** | 0.242 | 0.512 | 11/225 | +$328 · 101t · 65.3% · SR 0.48 | edge real · selection gray · holdout PASS |
| expansion | s0.4_t1.75_x45 (frozen argmax) | **1.000** | **0.001** | 1.060 | 25/225 | +$802 · 207t · 72.5% · SR 1.08 | edge real · selection rock-stable · holdout PASS |
| rth | s0.45_t1.75_x45 (doc pick) | **1.000** | **0.003** | 1.153 | 23/225 | +$1,587 · 223t · 74.4% · SR 1.59 | edge real · selection rock-stable · holdout PASS |

All three families pass the frozen single-use holdout. RTH and expansion
selection is far more stable than momentum's (PBO ~0.001-0.003 vs 0.242) —
the higher-frequency families' extra trades pay for themselves in selection
reliability. Momentum's edge is real but its argmax is not — keep
plateau-picking for that family. All three pass concentration (momentum
11.8% top-10; expansion 6.7%; rth 4.7%).

## What still needs work

- **Regime slicing**: per-year is in; add VIX/trend-regime buckets.
- **Ledger count integrity**: raw configs tried (225) understates the real
  trial count — every historical study in `docs/research/*` that swept this
  grid also counts. Decide per family whether pre-pipeline sweeps count
  toward `n_trials` and record the decision in the ledger entry.
- **Holdout re-declaration protocol**: the window is single-use per family;
  when a family's config changes materially, declare a NEW holdout window
  (the old pin documents what it was tested against).

# Fill-model integrity — what the backtest engine is, what broke, and the new discipline (2026-10-08)

The two 2026-10-08 incidents forced a reckoning with the RTH family's
validation. This document separates what is solid from what was wrong,
and sets the discipline going forward.

## The principle

**You trade your fill model, not your signal.** A backtest is only as
real as its assumptions about how orders actually fill: entry drift,
crossed-limit marketability, stop slippage, fees, partial fills. A
config whose profit lives inside an idealized part of the fill model is
not validated — it is a bet on the assumption.

## What is solid (the engine)

- **Archive replay** — 652 sessions of real footprint/OHLC data; the
  detectors reproduce live tape exactly (proven again by the open-drive
  live fix, 2026-10-05).
- **Account simulator** — eval rules, daily floor, drawdown halving,
  consistency cap, sizing math. Pure mechanics, unit-tested.
- **Fees** — $1.90/RT measured from real fills.
- **Methodology** — train/OOS splits, walk-forward, cost ladders, year
  stability.

## What was wrong (two fill assumptions, in the RTH studies)

1. **Entry side:** crossed-limit dispatches were scored as if the bracket
   worked at the signal price — a short filled above its own stop books
   an instant *win* in the model, while live the stop is rejected
   (`InvalidPrice`) or compressed. Phantom profit.
2. **Exit side:** stop-outs fill at the trigger, zero slippage. Live, a
   stop is a market order that fills at the next traded price — and in
   the flush tape this family trades, that is routinely 1–2 pts beyond.

Neither is an engine bug: the engine faithfully computed the
consequences of wrong assumptions. The RTH family was hit hardest
because its edge was *concentrated* in exactly those blind spots — its
best trades were crossed-dispatch moves, and its tight stops live inside
the tape that runs them.

## The numbers (same config, assumptions peeled)

RTH s0.5 stop / t2.5 target, resting-limit entries, 652 sessions,
$1.90/RT, $100 budget:

| Model | Result |
|---|---|
| Original validation (10-06, went live) | **+$13.8k PASS** (train +$8.1k / OOS +$5.7k) |
| + crossed cards gated (honest execution) | +$9.9k, dd −$2.5k **BREACH** |
| + stop slippage modeled | **−$26.2k BREACH** |
| + slippage capped at 2 / 5 / 10 pts | **−$26.2k at every cap** |

The slip-cap result falsifies the "black swan" story: capping the tail
changes nothing, because every slipped fill in the archive was already
≤2 pts past the stop. The bleed is thousands of routine small slips on
stop-outs of a 3-pt stop inside flush tape. It is structural, not tail.

## What remains trustworthy — audited per study (2026-10-08)

- **Guards, sizing, fees** — account-rule mechanics, independent of fill
  assumptions.
- **Entry-side realism:**
  - `retraceSlippageStudy` / `entryQualityStudy` — realistic entry fills
    (limit-or-better + gap-through, next-bar-open market fills,
    fill-anchored brackets, drift gates); the 10-04 tape-lag lesson
    applied.
  - `momentumStudy` / `sizingOptimizer` (the older momentum generation)
    — entries at the SIGNAL price with zero drift: an entry-side
    idealization (small impact: immediate dispatch), still an assumption
    to close.
- **Exit-side (stop slippage): modeled NOWHERE before this incident.**
  Every scorer in the codebase exits at the stop PRICE; the best
  available was a flat ~0.5 pt/RT cost. The RTH treatment in
  `rthDriftOptimizer.ts` is the FIRST stop-side slippage model. The
  blind spot is systemic; its impact scales with stop tightness — RTH's
  3-pt stops worst, momentum's wider structural stops less, but
  UNMEASURED, not absent. Pending: apply the slippage model to the
  momentum/open configs and calibrate the parameter with the live
  stop-fill journal (the slippage alarm's data).
- **Anything downstream that consumed RTH trades** (parts of the day-plan
  / risk-stack sweeps) inherits the RTH phantom edge and should be
  re-checked once RTH is re-validated.

## The new discipline (applies to every study from now on)

1. **Declare the fill model on BOTH sides** — entry drift/marketability
   AND stop-out slippage — in the study header. A config is only trusted
   within its declared model's validity.
2. **Sweep the assumptions** — every idealized parameter gets a
   sensitivity sweep (the crossed-gate / slip-cap / contract-cap grid in
   `scripts/rthDriftOptimizer.ts` is now the template).
3. **Calibrate from live data.** The slippage alarm + protection registry
   journal every stop's trigger vs actual fill from this point on. The
   routine-slip magnitude becomes a *measurement*, not a proxy — the
   model's bar-close assumption (fill at the close when the bar closes
   through the stop) is reasonable but unverified for routine stop-outs.
4. **Reconcile live vs model continuously** — if live diverges, the model
   is wrong, never the market.

## The fill-model audit — every live family, honest fills (2026-10-08)

`scripts/fillAudit.ts` replays all 652 sessions with each family's LIVE
mechanics (momentum: market entry, signal-anchored brackets, no time
exit; expansion: retrace limit 1 pt behind the close, fill-anchored 1R
brackets; open: market entry, signal brackets) × entry-lag brackets
(signal close ≈ live dispatch vs next-bar open ≈ 1-min lag) × stop
slippage off/on. $100 budget, $1.90/RT, eval sim:

| Family | Entry | Stop slip | Net $ | dd $ | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| momentum | ≈live (close) | N | +29,752 | −986 | **PASS** |
| momentum | ≈live (close) | **Y** | **+21,282** | −1,382 | **PASS** |
| momentum | 1-min lag (open) | any | ≈ −66k | −23k | BREACH |
| open drive | ≈live (close) | Y | +6,067 | −291 | **PASS** |
| open drive | 1-min lag | any | ≈ −2.5k | −1.5k | PASS (negative) |
| expansion retrace | limit mechanics | N | −53,508 | −7,938 | BREACH |
| expansion retrace | limit mechanics | Y | −67,543 | −15,000 | BREACH |

Conclusions:
1. **Momentum and open survive honest fills** — momentum +$21k with stop
   slippage at live dispatch speed (PASS). Their edges are LAG-SENSITIVE:
   a ~1-minute entry lag flips momentum to −$66k. Live dispatch is
   immediate, so they sit in the healthy column — the crossed-limit gate
   keeps them there.
2. **Expansion retrace is negative in this audit** (−$53k) and contradicts
   the published redesign validation (+$58k). The prime suspect: the
   published number validated the scale-out LADDER (bank 2/3 + runner
   ladder), while live runs the single-leg 1R path (CROSSTRADE_SCALEOUT
   is off). This needs a dedicated reconciliation — the live expansion
   path is NOT validated until then.
3. The RTH result stands (−$26k, the only family with the tight 0.5× stop
   inside flush tape).

## The bounded live experiment (the owner's "keep the config" proposal, done properly)

Keep RTH's config, keep all execution protections, cap size
(`MAX_MICRO_CONTRACTS=8`), run N days / M cards, and use the journaled
stop-fill data to fit the REAL slippage distribution. Then re-run the
study with the measured parameter:

- If measured routine slip ≈ 1 tick → the model was too harsh; RTH is
  back on the table.
- If ≈ 1–2 pts → the model was right; the config is retired or
  re-studied with different mechanics (wider stop → smaller size →
  fewer runs).

That is the execution-layer countermeasure taken as far as physics
allows, plus the one assumption tested with evidence instead of a proxy.
live-vs-backtest:
# Live vs backtest divergence — why the account is down $1,405 (2026-10-05)

> Diagnosis of the live bleed against the backtests, from the reconciled
> data: CrossTrade account snapshot, Neon `trades`/`signals`/`manual_trades`,
> the archived session tape, and the live engine's bar-building code.
> Machinery: `web/scripts/liveRescore.ts` (live cards re-scored under three
> bracket sets), `web/scripts/stopMultCalibration.ts` (the owner's own
> sweep), plus inline comparisons of live-written bars vs the archive.
>
> **Account truth (CrossTrade snapshot, MFFUEVREOD706880006): realized P&L
> −$1,405.50 · netLiq $49,852.20.** The bot is the loss source — manual
> trades are net positive (+$1,417.5 across 10 imported trips).

## The four divergences, in order of size

### 1. The live tape is not the backtest tape (root cause)

The backtests replay the archived GoCharting footprint candles (complete,
server-side buy/sell attribution). The live engine builds its bars from the
**tick stream** (`lib/live.ts` `applyTickTo`): every print classified by its
`side` field, with the fallback `ltp >= lastLtp ? buy : sell` (up-tick = buy)
when side is missing, size defaulting to 1 when `l_sz` is absent. A lossy
websocket cannot reproduce the vendor's aggregated candles.

Measured on 2026-10-01 (the session the executor traded 28 cards):

- The live card at 21:18 fired on a "76% buy" breakout bar (card text,
  TRADE_REVIEW_2026-10-02). The archive bar for 21:18 is **41% buy**
  (30 buy / 43 sell). 22:50: live 82% sell vs archive 63%.
- Consequently the backtested detector (MOM_PROD/EXP_PROD on the archive)
  generates **1 momentum + 1 expansion signal** for the whole of 10-01;
  the live engine fired **7 + 4** that day. RTH: archive detector finds 7,
  live fired 17.
- The live cards, re-scored on the archive tape, go **2W/8L under every
  bracket set** (profile, structural 1R, structural + wide target). The
  backtested edge simply does not exist for signals that only the live
  tape qualifies.

Every WR/PF number in PLAYBOOK.md and docs/research applies to a strategy
the live executor never actually trades. This is the single biggest "wrong
thing from the backtests": **the backtest data-generating process ≠ the
live data-generating process.**

### 2. The backtests trade ~1/3 as often as live

Every study replays one-position-at-a-time and skips any signal within
60 bars of the previous entry — **even when the previous trade already
closed** (`openUntil = entryIdx + HOLD_BARS`). The live feed takes every
card past the ≥5-bar gap.

| Day | backtest plan (archive, taken) | live cards |
|---|---|---|
| 09-30 | EXP 4 / RTH 5 | — |
| 10-01 | MOM 1 + EXP 1 + RTH 3 | 7 mom + 4 exp + 17 rth = 28 |
| 10-02 | MOM 5 + EXP 6 + RTH 4 | 18 rth + … |

3× the trade rate ⇒ 3× the commissions ($325 on 10-01 alone, against $165
gross) and the marginal cards are the losers. The plan that was validated
was "~5 cards/day"; the plan that runs is "every card".

### 3. The live stop profile is WR-optimal, points-suboptimal, and friction-fragile

Live profiles (`lib/profile.ts` defaults): MOM stop 0.35× / target 2.25R;
RTH stop 0.45× / target 1.75R. The owner's own sweep
(`stopMultCalibration.ts`, same targets, 649 sessions):

| MOM flush (2.25R · 60-bar) | pts | RTH (1.75R · 45-bar) | pts |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0.35× (live) | 2,632 | 0.45× (live) | 11,477 |
| 0.8× | 3,661 | 0.9× | 15,013 |
| 1.0× | 3,456 | 1.0× | 14,422 |

The optimizer picked the tight stops for their win rate, but at the live
targets **wider stops make more points**, and the stop-run rate is **96–99%
at every multiple** — nearly every loss is a run-back that a wider stop
would have survived. The profile was validated at 0.5 pt cost and perfect
close-price fills; live pays ≈0.95 pt round-trip **plus** a median −1.75 pt
adverse entry drift on losers (max −6.5, from `trades.entry_adverse_pts`),
plus quote-anchored brackets (the 01:27 case alone swung ~$300). On a
1.2–3.5 pt stop those unmodeled frictions are a large fraction of the
trade — the exact fragility `sizing-optimizer-2026-10-04.md` flagged and
shipped anyway.

### 4. Validation shortcuts + sizing beyond the envelope

- RTH's pick was selected by a **full-history filter** because the
  train/test split failed on regime-dependent drawdown
  (`rth-optimizer-2026-10-05.md` admits this) — weaker than the momentum
  walk-forward, and live RTH is running 58.1% vs the modeled 70.7%.
- Live sizing exceeds the backtested $170/trade budget: the 10-04/05 fills
  include 26-micro trades (≈$312 risk). The ×2 size the optimizer chose is
  "the max the account can bear" **at perfect fills**.
- Live outcomes to date: mom flush 4W/14L (28.6% vs 66.8–76% modeled),
  RTH 18W/31L (58.1% vs 70.7% modeled), expansion 8W/9L.

## What the backtests did NOT get wrong

The account drawdown (−$1,405.50) is *inside* the modeled tail (momentum
×2 @ 0.95 pt: max dd −$1,589; RTH ×2: −$1,943). The models were honest
about the tail; they were wrong about the **mean** because the live plan
is not the modeled plan (divergences 1–3 above).

## Recommended sequence

1. **Halt live execution now** (`EXECUTE_LIVE=0` on the VPS Coolify env —
   needs the owner's explicit approval; the Mac is already 0).
2. **Fix the tape first.** Drive the live detectors off the same
   GoCharting candle feed the archive is built from, or add a
   bar-confirmation gate (fire only when the vendor's completed candle
   agrees with the tick-built bar). Until live bars == archive bars, no
   backtest transfers.
3. **Re-validate the live plan with honest semantics**: gap-only replay
   (every card, not one-position-at-a-time), 0.95 pt cost, modeled −1.75 pt
   adverse drift on losing entries, walk-forward + MFF account sim. Expect
   the current profile to fail; measure the structural-bracket variant
   before re-enabling anything.
4. **Stop multiples**: the sweep favors 0.75–1.0× at the live targets —
   re-validate with frictions, then flip `MOM_STOP_MULT`/`RTH_STOP_MULT`
   via the EXEC_CHANGE_POLICY path.
5. **Size at ×1** ($170/trade, 30-micro cap) until the friction fixes land.
6. **Shadow-trade first**: cards print with `EXECUTE_LIVE=0` for a week
   and the live-bar vs archive-bar diff is journaled nightly.

*Educational research only — not financial advice.*

# Backtest report standard — the canonical study format (applies to every study)

> Why this exists: study reports were coming back with a different ad-hoc
> table every time, so the same numbers could not be compared across
> studies. From now on **every study report follows this skeleton and uses
> these five tables with these exact column orders.** A study that deviates
> must say why in its Honest bounds section.

---

## 1. What an edge is — the metric hierarchy (the direct answer)

**An edge is positive expectancy per unit risk, net of ALL costs, measured
out-of-sample, statistically distinguishable from zero, and stable across
time segments.** Nothing less. No single metric below is an edge by
itself; the verdict is a conjunction of all of them.

| Metric | What it answers | Is it an edge metric? |
|---|---|---|
| **Expectancy** (per trade, in pts **and** in R) | how much the system earns per trade, per unit risked | **YES — the edge itself.** Primary number. |
| **Profit factor** (gross win ÷ gross loss) | the same information as expectancy, as a gross ratio | Yes, but only net of costs and only with n (a PF of 2.5 on 40 trades is noise; 1.3 on 2,000 is real). |
| **Win rate** | how often trades close green | **Never alone.** 40% WR can be excellent (payoff 3:1); 70% WR can bleed (payoff 0.4:1). Only meaningful next to payoff. |
| **Payoff** (avg win ÷ avg loss) | how big wins are vs losses | The other half of WR. Breakeven WR = 1 ÷ (1 + payoff). |
| **SQN** (Van Tharp) | expectancy ÷ σ(R) × √n — quality with sample-size awareness | Yes — the best single "how good is this system" number. |
| **Max drawdown** | worst peak-to-trough on the equity curve | **Not an edge metric — but under prop rules it is THE deployment metric.** Edge and DD are orthogonal: edge asks "does it make money per trade", DD asks "can the account hit the profit target before the max-loss floor". A positive-expectancy system that breaches the MLL before reaching the target is a *real edge you cannot harvest* — it fails deployment even though it passes edge. In the prop context both questions are mandatory: edge (T1) decides *whether to trade it*, viability (T4) decides *whether the account survives to the payout*. |
| **Sharpe (per session)** | return-on-risk per session, volatility-adjusted | Edge-adjacent: smoothness/consistency of the edge. Pipeline unit: per-session netUsd ÷ riskUsd. |
| **Concentration (top-10 share)** | is the edge the system, or 3 lucky sessions? | Yes — an edge concentrated in <10% of sessions is fragile. |
| **DSR / PBO / PSR / MinTRL** | is the edge real after N configs were tried? | Yes — the multiple-testing firewall (validation pipeline, only when a grid was swept). |
| **Train/test agreement + frozen holdout** | does the edge survive unseen data? | **YES — the single most important check.** IS-only numbers are curve-fitting. |

The relationships to keep in one line:

- `expectancy = WR × avgWin − (1−WR) × avgLoss`
- `payoff = avgWin ÷ avgLoss` · `breakeven WR = 1 ÷ (1 + payoff)`
- `PF = (WR × avgWin) ÷ ((1−WR) × avgLoss)` — same info as expectancy,
  but insensitive to n and to cost rounding.
- `SQN = (E[R] ÷ σ(R)) × √n` — rewards edge × breadth × consistency.
- **A study that reports only WR and PF has not reported edge** — it has
  reported two of the ten numbers.

## 2. What a solid backtest requires (the 10 checks)

1. **No lookahead** — every feature at bar T is known through bar T;
   location from the PRIOR day's sheet only (house rule already in the
   replay harness).
2. **Realistic costs and fills** — 0.5 pt round-trip cost on every trade,
   pessimistic same-bar exit, stop-first when target and stop are in the
   same bar. Pts-only scratch sweeps are input, not validation (house rule).
3. **Sample size** — ≥ 100 trades before PF/WR stabilize, 200+ to trust
   them; below 50, PF is noise. Per-cell: n < 30 gets a † footnote, n < 8
   is never claimed.
4. **Out-of-sample discipline** — pick/train on the first 70% of dates,
   evaluate on the last 30%; frozen single-use holdout where the family
   has one (pinned in `web/app/api/backtest/validation/reports/holdouts.json`).
5. **Multiple-testing correction** — grid sweeps report DSR / PBO / PSR /
   MinTRL from `validate_sweep.py`; pattern mining reports FDR q-values.
   A swept grid without these numbers is a lottery ticket, not evidence.
6. **Distribution, not just the average** — top-10-session concentration,
   best-trade dependence, maxDD; a PF of 1.6 built on one outlier is a
   different system than the same PF built on 200 similar wins.
7. **Stability across time** — per-year table + early/late halves; a
   direction that flips across halves is demoted (house rule already in
   the pattern layer).
8. **Cost sensitivity** — the adopted claim stated at 0.5 pt and checked
   one step wider (1.0 pt) so a cost-haircut claim is visible.
9. **Baseline always shown** — the claim is a LIFT over the right
   baseline (always-up/momentum/base rate, or the unfiltered cohort), and
   the opposite side / vetoed group is reported next to the rule.
10. **Reproducible** — a `## Regenerate` block with the exact CLI, and
    the script committed under `web/scripts/`.

## 3. The fixed report skeleton (every study, in this order)

1. `# Title — question (date)` — one line naming the question asked.
2. `## Method` — the T0 study card (table below), then prose.
3. `## Results` — the T1 core quality table FIRST, always; then T4
   (prop-account viability) in every trade-level study; then T2/T3 as the
   study needs.
4. `## What this falsifies and what it confirms` — numbered findings.
5. `## Honest bounds` — sample limits, CI widths, thin cells, what the
   test cannot claim.
6. `## Regenerate` — the CLI.

**The T1 table appears in every trade-level study, in exactly this column
order, before any custom table.** Custom tables may follow but must reuse
the T2 row format for any cell/segment comparison.

## 4. The four canonical tables

### T0 — Study card (fixed fields, always in this order)

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Instrument / session | e.g. NQ 1-min · ETH/RTH |
| Sample | date range, n sessions, n trades |
| Cost model | 0.5 pt round-trip (state if different) |
| Fill model | market-entry replay · pessimistic same-bar exit · stop-first |
| Exit model | target / stop / 60-bar time exit |
| Split | 70/30 by date (train < date ≤ test) + frozen holdout if any |
| Significance | Wilson 95% CI on WR · DSR/PBO if swept · FDR if pattern-mined |
| Model (if any) | per-start-time logistic L2 / none |
| CLI | `web/scripts/<name>.ts` |

### T1 — Core quality table (THE table; identical columns in every study)

| cohort | n | WR [CI95] | avg win | avg loss | payoff | exp (pts) | exp (R) | PF | SQN | maxDD (pts) | Sharpe (sess) | conc top10 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| all | … | … | … | … | … | … | … | … | … | … | … | … |
| train | … | … | … | … | … | … | … | … | … | … | … | … |
| test | … | … | … | … | … | … | … | … | … | … | … | … |
| baseline (if filter study) | … | … | … | … | … | … | … | … | … | … | … | … |

Units: wins/losses in pts net of cost; **exp (R)** = exp pts ÷ mean stop
distance (risk); SQN on per-trade R-multiples; maxDD on the 1-contract
(MNQ) equity curve in pts; Sharpe = per-session netUsd ÷ riskUsd (the
validation-pipeline unit). PF is `—` when there are no losses.

### T2 — Segment / cell comparison table (every multi-cell or rule table)

| # | rule / cell | n | WR [CI95] | PF | exp (pts) | train/test WR | baseline or opposite side |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

- n is the FIRST column after the label, always.
- The comparison column shows the same metric for the vetoed group /
  opposite side / unfiltered cohort — dominance is the gap, never one side
  alone.
- Pass-band values bolded; thin cells footnoted († n<30, ‡ n<8 never claimed).

### T3 — Sweep validation table (only when a grid was swept; reuse the
pipeline columns from `validate_sweep.py`)

| pick | DSR | PBO | observed SR | trials (eff/raw) | holdout (n sess) | verdict |

### T4 — Prop-account viability table (mandatory in every trade-level study;
both replay harnesses feed `simulateAccount` on every run, so these fields
are always available)

| stage | rules | n trades | trading days | total profit | best day | consist | min-days | breach | pass | payouts | outcome |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| eval | Rapid EOD 50k | … | … | $… | $… | ✓/✗ | ✓/✗ | — or date ($eq) | — or date ($eq) | — | `PASS d9 · consist ✓` / `no-pass` / `BREACH d3` |
| funded | Rapid EOD 50k | … | … | $… | $… | — | — | … | — | n | `payouts 2 · floor locked` / `BREACH d3` |
| eval (guarded) | + day-plan guard stack | … | … | … | … | … | … | … | … | — | guard halts in the notes |

`outcome` is one line from the sim: breach day and equity, pass day with
the consistency + min-days gates, or payouts + floor state for funded.
Add `(guarded)` rows whenever the run used `--guarded` (day-plan halts,
dd600 half-sizing) — the guard stack models the live executor, the bare
rows are the historical baseline.

### §4.1 — The prop-firm viability question (the drawdown's real job)

The deployment question is first-passage, not magnitude: **does the
account reach the profit target before the EOD-trailing floor is
breached?** The sim answers it empirically by replaying the daily P&L
series through the MFF Rapid EOD 50k rules ($3,000 target vs $2,000
trailing MLL, floor locks at $100, 4 min days, 30% consistency). Report:

1. **The T4 table** — the single replay of the actual order of days.
2. **P(pass before breach)** — share of *reshuffled* re-sequences of the
   daily P&L (bootstrap over day order) that pass before breaching. This
   is the number that says how much of the outcome was the system vs the
   luck of day ordering. Per-session returns have ~0 autocorrelation
   (validation pipeline), so reshuffling is defensible; say when it isn't.
3. **The sizing check** — maxDD pts × $2/pt × contracts → dollars, against
   the MLL: the DD number from T1 only means something once it is
   converted through the prop sizing rules into floor distance.
4. **Time-to-pass** — median trading days to reach the target vs the min
   days + consistency gates: a system that passes slowly but breaches fast
   is a deployment failure with a real edge.

Example verdict slot: `viability PASS (P=0.93, median 11 days)` /
`viability FAIL (P=0.41 — edge real, unharvestable at this sizing)`.

## 5. Threshold bands (green · gray · red) for THIS system

Tuned to NQ scalping at 0.5 pt cost — not universal gospel; the verdict
still comes from the significance + robustness block, not from any single
band.

| Metric | Green (believe it) | Gray (probe it) | Red (reject it) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Expectancy (R) | ≥ 0.4 | 0.1 – 0.4 | < 0 |
| Expectancy (pts) | ≥ 2.0 | 0.5 – 2.0 | < 0.5 |
| PF (net of cost) | 1.5 – 3.0 | 1.1 – 1.5 · > 3.0 (scrutinize for overfit/thin n) | < 1.1 |
| WR | any — read only with payoff | — | — |
| SQN | ≥ 2.5 good · ≥ 3.0 excellent | 1.6 – 2.5 | < 1.6 (hard to trade) |
| maxDD (pts, 1-contract) | ≤ 40 | 40 – 80 | > 80 (check prop MLL feasibility separately) |
| Sharpe (sess) | ≥ 1.0 | 0.5 – 1.0 | < 0.5 |
| Concentration (top-10) | ≤ 15% | 15 – 30% | > 30% |
| DSR | ≥ 0.95 | 0.80 – 0.95 | < 0.80 |
| PBO | ≤ 0.20 | 0.20 – 0.40 | > 0.40 |
| Train/test WR gap | ≤ 5 pts | 5 – 10 pts | > 10 pts or sign flip |

Prop-viability bands (T4 / §4.1):

| Metric | Green (deploy) | Gray (probe) | Red (reject) |
|---|---|---|---|
| P(pass before breach) | ≥ 0.90 | 0.70 – 0.90 | < 0.70 |
| maxDD$ ÷ MLL | ≤ 40% | 40 – 70% | > 70% (floor has no room for daily noise) |
| Median days to pass | ≤ 20 | 20 – 40 | > 40 (or breaches dominate) |

Notes: PF > 3.0 is *not* automatically overfit here — a high-WR scalper
with small stops can legitimately clear it on large n (the card baseline
is PF 2.93 on n=3,298). What separates it from curve-fitting is DSR/PBO +
concentration + the frozen holdout, which is exactly why T3 exists. The
bands above PF 3.0 point at those checks rather than at the exit.

## 6. The edge verdict line (end of every study)

One line, always the same slots, e.g.:

`VERDICT: edge real · significance PASS (PSR 0.97) · stability stable
(train/test 76.8/76.1) · holdout PASS · viability PASS (P=0.93)`

Slots: edge `{real|unproven|absent}` · significance `{PASS|weak|—}`
· stability `{stable|gray|fragile|—}` · holdout `{PASS|FAIL|n/a}`
· viability `{PASS|FAIL|n/a (P=…)}` — the last slot appears whenever the
study sizes trades under prop rules (which every harness run does).
"Unproven" is an honest result, not a failure — it is what "go log it
forward" means. "Edge real · viability FAIL" is a sizing/plan problem,
not an edge problem: fix the plan or the size, not the signal.

## 7. Worked example (real archive numbers)

The side-filter study's baseline row (`side-filter-study-2026-10-09.md`),
cast into T1 — with the columns that run did not compute left as `—`, which
is exactly the gap this standard closes:

| cohort | n | WR [CI95] | avg win | avg loss | payoff | exp (pts) | exp (R) | PF | SQN | maxDD (pts) | Sharpe (sess) | conc top10 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| all | 3,298 | **76.8%** | — | — | — | **+2.39** | — | **2.93** | — | — | — | — |
| longs | 1,646 | 78.6% | — | — | — | +2.56 | — | 3.26 | — | — | — | — |
| shorts | 1,652 | 75.0% | — | — | — | +2.22 | — | 2.65 | — | — | — | — |

Every study from now on fills the whole row — no dashes except a genuine
no-losses PF. T4 works the same way: the harness already replays the
account on every run, so the eval/funded rows exist — older studies just
never showed them. From now on they are shown, always, with the
`viability` slot in the verdict line.

## 8. Copy-paste template (start every study doc from this)

`web/lib/backtestEngine.ts` is the single home for everything above — one
engine, four layers, unit-tested in `web/tests/backtestEngine.test.ts`:

# Winner/loser atlas — session delta, session-extreme targets, and the loss anatomy

> First measurement pass over the full NQ archive: **649 sessions** (2023-12-18
> → 2026-10-05), the three production families replayed with their live plan
> shapes (MOM failed-flush 1R · EXP huge-bar expansion 1R · RTH soft 0.75R;
> first-touch, 60-bar time exit, 0.5 pt cost, sequential one-trade-at-a-time),
> canonical split 2026-01-01. Machinery: `web/scripts/winnerLoserAtlas.ts`
> (archive replay + per-trade session context, CSV dump at
> `docs/data/winner-loser-atlas-2026-10-05.csv`) and `web/scripts/winnerLoserLive.ts`
> (the same features recomputed on the reconciled live `trades` rows in Neon).
>
> Session context is computed lookahead-free at the entry bar: cumulative
> buy−sell since the session open and the session high/low **at entry time**.
> Cells: "agrees/against" = trade direction vs the sign of session cumΔ;
> "ATH-retest" = |target − session extreme| ≤ 0.5 with the target NOT beyond
> it; "fresh-air" = target beyond the session extreme by > 0.25 pts.
>
> **Headline:** (1) gating a direction against the session cumulative delta
> buys nothing — pooled 79.8% WR / +2.99 pts vs 79.7% / +2.90, and in the
> flush family counter-delta is the *better* cell; (2) the dangerous target
> is not the "not defined" fresh-air high — it is the **exact ATH retest**
> (target sitting on the session extreme, pooled +0.70 vs +2.96 baseline,
> weak in all three families, and *no* exit management — including
> breakeven-at-1R — rescues it); fresh-air targets are fine to best, and
> only MOM's fresh-air cell profits from a BE@1R runner (+0.18); (3) the
> dominant loss mode everywhere is the stop-run — 60–72% of stop-outs print
> a return beyond the entry within 10 bars, and 0% of losing trades ever
> touched +1R first, so breakeven ladders can only ever change winners, never
> rescue losers.

---

## 1. Q1 — should a direction against the session cumΔ be gated? No.

| Cell | MOM flush 1R | EXP expansion 1R | RTH soft 0.75R |
|---|---|---|---|
| ALL | 1,559 · 75.4% · +2.18 | 2,935 · 77.4% · +2.50 | 2,794 · 84.6% · +3.86 |
| agrees w/ cumΔ | 75.1% · +2.15 | 77.2% · +2.52 | **85.2% · +3.97** |
| against cumΔ | **75.9% · +2.21** | **77.8% · +2.48** | 83.8% · +3.72 |
| strongest-against (Δ ≤ −800 vs dir) | 75.3% · +2.16 | 78.5% · +2.61 | 83.3% · +3.67 |
| veto against, \|Δ\| ≥ 400 | Δexp +0.01 | Δexp +0.01 | Δexp +0.12 (test 4.27 → **4.22**) |

Pooled: agrees n=4,198 +2.99 vs against n=3,090 +2.90 — flat. The flush
family is the cleanest statement: a failed-flush long is *by construction* a
counter-delta trade (sellers dominated the session, yet failed to break the
low), and it is the best cell. Even the extreme bands (session delta ≥ 800
against the trade) carry family-average expectancy. The only family with a
visible gap (RTH, +0.25 exp) does not survive the train/test split when the
veto is applied — test expectancy goes **down** (4.27 → 4.22).

The live tape agrees: on 2026-10-01 the session cumΔ ran from −717 to
−7,464, and the 12 winners were mostly counter-delta **longs** (only 4/12
agreed) while 13 of 19 losses were with-delta shorts.

**Verdict: no gate.** Consistent with `counterBiasVeto.ts` (day-bias veto
≈ 0) and the ES Δ− chip being a journal label, never a gate. Keep cumΔ as a
journal chip; do not filter on it.

## 2. Q2 — target at the session high/low: two cells, opposite answers

| Cell | MOM | EXP | RTH | pooled |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **ATH-retest** (target ON the extreme ±0.5) | 27 · 63.0% · +0.75 | 37 · 62.2% · +0.84 | 44 · 70.5% · +0.55 | **108 · 65.7% · +0.70** |
| **fresh-air** (target beyond by > 0.25) | 231 · 77.5% · **+2.81** | 436 · 75.0% · +2.26 | 0 | 667 · 75.9% · +2.45 |
| inside range (baseline reference) | 75.2% · +2.08 | 78.0% · +2.56 | 84.7% · +3.89 | +2.96 (all trades) |

The user's instinct is half right. **"Session all-time high" = the exact
retest** — price has been rejected at that level all session — is a genuinely
weak cell in every family (WR −15 pp, expectancy +0.55–0.84 vs family
baselines of +2.2–3.9). It is rare (~1.5% of trades, n=108 pooled). **The
"not defined high" = fresh air** is the opposite: not dangerous at all, and
for the MOM flush family it is the single best cell in the whole family
(+2.81, PF 3.27).

Management variants on each cell (0.5 pt cost, 60-bar exit):

| Variant | MOM ATH-retest | MOM fresh-air | EXP ATH-retest | EXP fresh-air | RTH ATH-retest |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| base (fixed target) | +0.75 | +2.81 | +0.84 | +2.26 | +0.55 |
| target capped @extreme | +0.71 | +2.65 | +0.80 | +2.22 | +0.54 |
| early bank 0.5R | +0.66 | +1.27 | +0.77 | +1.13 | **−0.11** |
| early bank 0.75R | +0.02 | +2.16 | +0.45 | +1.91 | +0.55 |
| runner BE@1R ladder | **−0.14** | **+2.98** | +0.04 | +1.83 | +0.61 |
| ½ fixed + ½ runner | +0.31 | +2.90 | +0.44 | +2.05 | +0.58 |

- **Nothing rescues the ATH-retest cell.** Capping, early banking, and
  breakeven ladders all leave it at +0.0…+0.8 — and the BE@1R runner makes
  MOM's cell *negative*. The breakeven idea cannot work there because the
  losers never get near 1R: 0% of stop-outs touched +1R first (see §3).
  The right "care" is recognizing the cell and skipping or sizing down —
  it is a ~1.5%-frequency drag of ~0.03 pts/trade overall, so the cheapest
  correct action is journal-awareness, not new machinery.
- **Fresh air needs no extra care.** MOM fresh-air is the family's best
  cell; the only variant that adds to it is the BE@1R runner (+2.98,
  +0.18). EXP fresh-air is mildly below family (+2.26 vs +2.50) and every
  variant makes it worse — leave it at the fixed target. RTH never prints
  a fresh-air target (0.75R target, n=0).
- Breakeven-at-1R is therefore **not a general loss-saver** — see §3.

## 3. Q3 — winner vs loser atlas

**Loss anatomy (the single biggest pattern).** Every stop-out bar in all
three families was checked for a 10-bar return beyond the entry:

| Family | stop-outs | run-back ≤10 bars | touched +0.5R first | touched +1R first |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| MOM flush | 383 | **65%** | 54% | 0% |
| EXP expansion | 659 | **60%** | 62% | 0% |
| RTH soft | 430 | **72%** | 26% | 0% |

Live 2026-10-01: 11 of 19 losses were labeled stop-runs (58%). Two
consequences: (a) the tape runs our stops ~2/3 of the time — this is the
background behind the stop-run studies, and widening stops was already
measured to buy ~0 (the run-back does not convert into expectancy);
(b) **no losing trade ever reached +1R first**, so breakeven-at-1R can only
ever convert *winners* into runners — it is a winner-management tool, not a
loss filter. MOM/EXP losers reach ~half-R then reverse (median MFE +0.54R /
+0.63R); RTH losers mostly die on the very next bar (median held 1 bar, only
26% touched +0.5R).

**Feature medians, winners vs losers** (readable per family in the script
output; the durable signals):

- MOM `deltaFromFlush`: winners **+10** vs losers **−28** — in the flush
  family, losers have order-flow delta *bleeding against the trade* between
  the flush and the entry bar (RTH mirrors: −22 vs −85).
- RTH candle quality: losers have smaller `breakRangeR` (1.23 vs 1.38),
  lower `atr14` (9 vs 10), tighter `riskPts` (7.25 vs 8.38) — the weak-bar
  RTH trades lose; the ≥1.0×ATR gate is doing real work.
- EXP `distToExt`: losers 28.5 vs winners 32.6 — expansion trades fired
  closer to the session extreme lose more often (same story as the
  fresh-air/ATH-retest split).

**Cells:**

- **Shorts are the weaker side only in MOM** (72.9% / +1.90 vs longs 78.0% /
  +2.46); EXP and RTH sides are near-equal (RTH long 85.7% / short 83.5%).
- **Tuesday is the weakest day in all three families** (pooled +2.65 vs
  +3.04 on other days; MOM +2.01, EXP +2.36, RTH +3.28 — each below its
  family mean). Friday is MOM-weak (+1.83) but fine for EXP/RTH. Monday is
  strong for MOM/EXP — consistent with `seasonal-almanac-2026-10-05.md`.
- **After-loss trades are not worse** (pooled +2.92 vs +2.82 after a win;
  MOM +2.57 after a loss vs +2.00 after a win). Longest same-day losing
  streak per family: 3–4. No revenge-trade penalty — shrinking after losses
  buys nothing (matches `sizing-dynamics-2026-10-02.md`).
- **First RTH card of the day is disproportionately good** (+5.33 vs +3.86);
  MOM/EXP first-of-day ≈ average.
- EXP **close bucket** (16:00–17:00 ET) is the family's weak bucket
  (67.1% WR, +1.42, n=74) — already reflected in `ticketVeto.ts`
  (`momentum_expansion/close/short` +0.75); the atlas says the whole close
  bucket is weak, not just shorts.

## 4. Standing caveats

1. This is a **scratch sweep, not a validation**: no account sim, and the
   veto rows are filter-only (the occupancy effect of removing a trade is
   not replayed — same limitation as `counterBiasVeto.ts`).
2. Small cells: ATH-retest n = 27/37/44 per family (108 pooled) — the
   direction is consistent across all three families, but per-family Wilson
   CIs are wide.
3. Same house rules as every replay: first-touch scoring, 0.5 pt cost,
   pessimistic same-bar stop-first exits, mid-price for archive closes.

*Educational research only — not financial advice.*

# 2026-10-08 — two incidents, the protection stack, and the fill-model reckoning

Two separate execution failure classes hit the live RTH family in one
day, each costing ~$1k. This document is the complete record: what
happened, what was built, what the studies now say, and the decisions
left open.

## Incident 1 — naked position (09:48 ET)

The RTH short (7 MNQ, limit 31216.25, stop 31222.75, target 31200.00)
opened with **no stop loss**. The owner caught it and closed manually at
09:52:44 ET @ 31215.50 (+13.75 pts ≈ +$192 gross). Broker evidence
(CrossTrade/Tradovate order lifecycle, ids 688241970704-6):

| Time (ET) | Event |
|---|---|
| 09:49:44.417 | REST limit placed (`muzlfch0-uzi2yu-lmt`); market ≈ 31229.25 — 13 pts above the limit |
| 09:49:44.422 | entry filled instantly @ **31229.25** (a marketable sell limit) — already 6.5 pts past its own stop |
| 09:49:44.427 | **stop leg REJECTED: `InvalidPrice` — "current price is outside the price limits set for this product"** |
| 09:51:28 | watcher logs `limit_filled` — the system believed the trade was protected |
| 09:52:44 | owner closes manually (profit) |

Root causes: (1) ~100 s dispatch lag with no price re-check — the flush
ran the tape 13 pts through the limit, and a marketable limit fills at
the market, not at the limit; (2) the OSO stop is anchored at the SIGNAL
price, so a buy-stop below the market is rejected at placement — and the
entry still fills; (3) nothing verified the bracket legs after placement
(the place response's `oso1Id`/`oso2Id` child ids were discarded).

## Incident 2 — stop slippage (12:17 ET, −$1,027.50)

The RTH short (15 MNQ, limit 31187.375, stop 31190.56 — 3.19 pts, "risk
$96") filled instantly at 31189.75: the limit was marketable, the tape
had moved 2.4 pts through it, and the signal-anchored stop was
**0.81 pts from the actual fill**. The market flushed ~35 pts in 11
seconds; the stop triggered and the stop-market filled at **31224.00 —
134 ticks past the trigger** (15 × 34.25 × $2 = −$1,027.50). The stop
existed and worked; the loss was gap-through slippage on a compressed
stop. Day went +$724 → −$332, recovered to +$882.90 by the owner's
manual 25-lot trade (+$1,262.50 gross) — landing **$17 below the $900
eval consistency cap**.

## The protection architecture (deployed, commits below)

All dry-run-gated by EXECUTE_LIVE, all at the executor choke point —
every order path, current or future, is covered:

1. **Crossed-stop dispatch gate** — refuse a limit whose OSO stop sits on
   the marketable side of the tape (the incident-1 shape).
2. **Crossed-limit dispatch gate** (1-pt threshold) — refuse a limit the
   tape has already moved through (the incident-2 shape). Today's clean
   winners crossed by 0.1 pts; both disasters by 13.0 / 2.4 pts.
3. **BURST verifier** (`verifyBracketsAfterPlace`) — after every
   bracketed placement: one session-orders read at +0.5 s, then every
   1.5 s for up to 20 s (~13 calls/trade), acting on a rejected/cancelled
   stop leg (cancel the resting entry / repair the filled position) and
   running the fill-anchored re-bracket once the entry fills.
4. **Fill-anchored re-bracket** — a drifted fill that compressed the stop
   below 50% of plan re-anchors stop+target to the ACTUAL fill via
   `cancel_and_bracket`.
5. **CrossTrade WebSocket order stream** (`lib/ctStream.ts`,
   `wss://app.crosstrade.io/ws/stream`, origin=tradovate) — pushed
   `orderUpdate` frames make a Rejected stop leg react in **<1 s**, no
   polling. Mid-trade rejections act only when the evidence agrees (no
   working stop covers the tracked position). P&L stream = liveness
   heartbeat; exponential-backoff reconnects under the 5-upgrades/IP/60s
   server limit.
6. **10 s protection watchdog** (`checkProtection`, was 30 s) — while an
   MNQ position is open a working stop must cover it; missing for one
   poll (10 s) → re-arm via `cancel_and_bracket` (stop re-anchored 1 pt
   beyond the tape) or flatten. Untracked (manual) positions are
   alert-only, never touched.
7. **Stop-slippage alarm** (`checkExitSlippage` + `classifyExitFill`) —
   every flat transition compares the exit fill to the intended stop and
   alerts + journals when it lands >2 pts beyond the trigger. This is
   also the live-calibration feed for the fill model (below).
8. **Executor contract cap** (`MAX_MICRO_CONTRACTS`, default 30) — bounds
   slippage × size.
9. **Owner kill switch** (`lib/tradingHalt.ts` + `/api/trading` +
   `TradingToggle`) — a TRADING LIVE/STOP toggle in the dashboard status
   strip. STOP instant, no password; RESUME password-gated when
   ADMIN_PASSWORD is configured. State persists to
   `GC_DATA_DIR/trading-halt.json` and survives redeploys; every flip
   appends a daybook `exec` audit record (`trading_halted` /
   `trading_resumed`).

| Reaction | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| stop-leg rejection detected | ~4 s | **<1 s** (WS) / **~2 s** (burst) |
| naked repair, worst case | ~30–60 s | **~10–20 s** |
| after the burst window | 30 s poll | 10 s watchdog |

## Study results — RTH s0.5/t2.5 across model generations

| Model | Result |
|---|---|
| Original validation (phantom crossed cards + zero stop slippage) | **+$13.8k PASS** |
| + crossed cards gated (honest execution) | +$9.9k, dd −$2.5k **BREACH** |
| + stop slippage modeled | **−$26.2k BREACH** |
| + slippage **capped at 2/5/10 pts** | −$26.2k — **identical at every cap** |

The slip-cap sweep falsifies the "black swan" explanation: capping the
134-tick tail changes nothing because every slipped fill in the archive
was already within ~2 pts of the stop. The bleed is thousands of routine
1–2 pt slips on stop-outs of a 3-pt stop inside flush tape — death by a
thousand papercuts, not a tail event. Full reckoning:
[docs/research/fill-model-integrity-2026-10-08.md](fill-model-integrity-2026-10-08.md).

## VPS outage (13:35–14:05 ET)

After the ADMIN_PASSWORD env change triggered a redeploy, the whole box
wedged (TCP accepted on 22/80/443/8000, no protocol completed — SSH,
HTTP, Coolify alike: a frozen guest). Recovered ~14:05 on its own; the
halt persisted through the outage and re-applied at boot, and the
deploy finished cleanly (`running:healthy`). Lesson: the kill switch's
persistence design is exactly what made the recovery safe.

## Deploy timeline (all pushed to main, auto-deployed)

- `c4884b0` fix(exec): OSO leg verification + naked-position repair
- `539b011` fix(exec): crossed-limit gate, fill-anchored re-bracket, contract cap, slippage alarm
- `9799e6e` feat(dashboard): trading kill switch (halt/resume + daybook audit)
- `31df712` fix(dashboard): kill-switch UX (password dialog, adaptive field, trimmed compare)
- `eba9813` fix(exec): sub-second protection — burst verifier + CrossTrade WebSocket order stream

## Open decisions (owner)

1. **FEED_RTH** — armed (`=1`) underneath the kill switch. Resuming
   re-arms RTH; the honest-fill studies say its config bleeds. Options:
   off, re-study, or a bounded live calibration experiment (see the
   fill-model doc).
2. **MAX_MICRO_CONTRACTS** — currently 30; 8 turns a 33-pt slip into
   ≈ −$528 instead of −$1,027.
3. **Consistency cap** — the day sits +$882.90 realized vs the $900
   30%-of-target rule; no more profit today.
4. **CrossTrade alert channels** — point their `order_rejected` alerts
   at the owner's Telegram (one-time UI action on their side).

# Neon transfer-cap incident — root cause, probes, and the fix (2026-10-08)

## What happened

The `nq-store` Neon project (`summer-poetry-26619129`, org `nq-scalping`,
`free_v3`) was paused with: *"Project nq-store is paused after reaching its
monthly free plan limit."* Every connection failed at handshake with
SQLSTATE `53000` — *"Your account or project has exceeded the quota."* The
journal, ingest, reconcile and every other nightly DB step went blind; only
the DB-less daybook (volume + R2) kept the journal alive.

## Root cause — measured, not guessed

Project meter on 2026-10-08 (Neon API):

| Meter | Value | Cap | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| `data_transfer_bytes` | **5,505,425,989 (5.13 GiB)** | **5 GiB/month (Free)** | **BLOWN — the pauser** |
| `compute_time_seconds` | 114,494 (~32h) | ~190h/month | fine |
| `synthetic_storage_size` | 431,915,008 (~412 MiB) | 512 MiB | fine |
| `consumption_period_end` | 2026-11-01T00:00:00Z | — | **resets Nov 1** |

The 5 GiB went out in ~10 days of the period. Sources, in order of weight:

1. **Nightly bulk re-ingest** (`nightly.sh` → `db/ingest.ts --since <21d>`):
   a 3-week window of `candles_1m` + `footprint_ticks` upserted every night
   (footprint_ticks = per-price-tick clusters, tens of thousands of rows per
   day, ×21 days, every single night).
2. **Live per-minute writes** (`lib/liveStore.ts`): the feed wrote each
   minute's candles AND its tick clusters into Neon all session long.
3. **Dashboard readthrough** (`lib/gcdb.ts` ← `lib/gcdata.ts`): every
   historical read (profile sheets, day bars, footprint charts) hit Neon
   first — whole days of `footprint_ticks` per panel load.

## Account level or project level? — probed empirically

Created two throwaway projects via the Neon API (same key), reset their
role passwords, connected with `postgres.js`:

| Probe | Result |
|---|---|
| New project in the SAME org (`nq-scalping`) | **CONNECTED, `select 1` OK** |
| New project in a different org | **CONNECTED, `select 1` OK** |

→ The transfer allowance is enforced **per project**, not per account/org.
`nq-store` is paused because IT transferred 5.13 GiB; a fresh project starts
at 0 and connects. (Both probes were deleted afterwards.)

## Decision

- **No delete/recreate.** The paused project can't be `pg_dump`ed while
  paused, and its `signals`/`trades` history is only partially recoverable
  from the VPS daybook volume + CrossTrade fills. Recreating now would
  discard that history for a cap reset we get anyway on **2026-11-01**.
- **Wait for the Nov 1 reset** — the project resumes with a fresh 5 GiB —
  and make sure the workload never comes near the cap again (below).

## The fix (shipped 2026-10-08)

1. **Bulk market data left Neon entirely.** `db/ingest.ts`: candles +
   footprint_ticks are now opt-in (`--candles`, default OFF); `nightly.sh`
   ingests only the small operational tables (profile sheets, events). Bars
   and ticks stay where the consumers already read them: gcdata JSON + R2
   (free egress) — the backtest engine and every study already read the
   archive, never Neon.
2. **Live footprint writes stopped.** `lib/liveStore.ts` keeps only the tiny
   ETH candle row per minute; the tick-cluster write is removed (ticks live
   in LiveFeed RAM + the archive).
3. **Readthrough no longer serves partial days.** `lib/gcdb.ts dbLoadDay`
   returns null when a day has bars but no ticks, so `gcdata.ts` falls back
   to the archive instead of rendering footprint-less charts.
4. **Quota watchdog** (`web/scripts/neonQuota.ts`, hooked into `nightly.sh`
   pre/post): reads the project's `data_transfer_bytes` from the Neon API,
   prints GiB/% + reset date every run, and pages the operator via the
   Telegram bot past `NEON_QUOTA_PAGE_PCT` (default 80%). Armed when
   `NEON_API_KEY` is present in the jobs env (a Coolify env addition —
   owner-approved per repo policy).

Net effect: Neon now carries only signals/trades/exec/guard/insights/sheets
— kilobytes-to-megabytes per day, order(s) of magnitude under the cap. The
nightly tapeParity steps were retired with the bulk ingest they diffed
against (kept in git for `--candles` use).

## Recurrence guard

Even with the slim workload, the watchdog is the backstop: if a future
change reintroduces heavy Neon traffic, the operator gets paged at 80% —
with the project's reset date in the message — instead of discovering the
pause when the journal stops updating.

## The rebuild — fresh project `nq-store2` (same day)

Chosen over waiting for the reset: a new project starts with a full 5 GiB
meter immediately. `nq-store` was KEPT (paused projects retain data) for a
post-reset dump of the Neon-only history (pre-10-06 signals/trades).

| Fact | Value |
|---|---|
| New project | `nq-store2` (`proud-waterfall-41356644`, org `nq-scalping`, aws-us-west-2) |
| Meter at cutover | 0.00 GiB / 5 GiB · resets 2026-11-01 |
| Endpoints updated | `nq-dashboard` + `nq-jobs` Coolify env `DATABASE_URL`, `web/.env.local` |

Rebuild pipeline (all idempotent, committed):

1. `scripts/restoreJournal.ts` — pulls the DB-less sources from the live
   dashboard (`/api/daybook`, volume ∪ R2) and rebuilds `signals` (10 rows
   with full 50-key feature vectors), `exec_log` (17), and the 10-06
   `trades` from the dayend summary (9 rows, `source='daybook'`). Applies
   the full `db/schema.sql` + operational-table DDL (incl. the empty
   `manual_trades` `/api/trades` references).
2. `scripts/reconcileTrades.ts --since 2026-09-28` — re-paired CrossTrade
   fills (durable history, both accounts) against the restored signals:
   5 matched + 3 unexecuted (10-07 session) + 23 unmatched fills.
3. `scripts/tradeAnalysis.ts` — anatomy recomputed from the R2 archive
   (refactored off `candles_1m`; per-trade archive-day mapping because the
   bar files are named by the closing NY date while `trades.day` uses the
   daybook trading-day key).
4. `scripts/scoreSignals.ts` — runs, but outcomes stay unscored until the
   VPS nightly (its container holds the collected session files the file
   replay reads).

Verified in production after deploy: `/api/trades` and `/api/trades/table`
both serve `source: db` — 17 trades, 55 variable columns, journal net
+$168.80 (10-06 summary +$500.90 ∔ 10-07 reconcile −$332.10).

Known gaps (accepted): Neon-only history before 10-06 (recoverable when
`nq-store` resumes on 2026-11-01 — then dump + merge); `manual_trades`
rows from the MFF/Tradovate export (re-import when the next export is
pulled); signal outcomes (next nightly).

Open env request: add `NEON_API_KEY` (+ `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN`) to the
`nq-jobs` env so the watchdog's 80% page actually sends on the VPS —
owner-approved per repo policy.

## Watchdog armed (same day, via Coolify API)

- Added `NEON_API_KEY`, `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN`, `TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID` to the
  `nq-jobs` env (bot token + chat id copied from the `nq-dashboard` env,
  values never logged) and redeployed the jobs container.
- Page path verified end-to-end: a test `sendMessage` through the same
  bot + chat returned `ok: true` (the "watchdog credential test" card).
- The nightly now logs the transfer meter pre/post and pages Telegram at
  `NEON_QUOTA_PAGE_PCT` (80%).
