## 6. Where the analogy breaks (stress-test results)

Consolidated from the disanalogies research report. Each item: source +
one-line scalper implication.

### 6.1 Reflexivity — your prediction changes the thing predicted
In language the next token is exogenous (the writer does not observe your
model). In markets the next price is partly *written by your own order*:
Kyle's market maker updates price in proportion to the order flow you send
([Kyle 1985, Econometrica 53(6):1315–1335](https://www.jstor.org/stable/1913210));
Almgren–Chriss decompose your impact into temporary (rate-dependent) and
permanent (size-dependent) components
([Almgren & Chriss 2001, Journal of Risk 3(2):5–39](https://www.risk.net/journal-of-risk/technical-paper/2160718/optimal-execution-of-portfolio-transactions));
Soros's reflexivity generalizes it: participants' biased beliefs alter the
fundamentals they bet on
([Soros 2013, J. Economic Methodology 20(4):309–329](https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/abs/10.1080/1350178X.2013.859415)).
**Implication:** edge must be net of your own impact; size is not a free dial.

### 6.2 Adversarial dynamics — the distribution fights back
Grossman–Stiglitz: equilibrium requires exactly enough inefficiency to pay
for the cost of exploiting it
([AER 70(3):393–408](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grossman%E2%80%93Stiglitz_paradox)).
Empirically, published predictors lose **26%** out-of-sample and **58%**
post-publication (97 predictors)
([McLean & Pontiff 2016, JF 71(1):5–32](https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1111/jofi.12365));
**64%** of 447 anomalies fail out-of-sample replication, 93% of liquidity-based
ones ([Hou, Xue & Zhang 2020](https://www.nber.org/papers/w23394)). At the
scalping horizon the fight is physical: latency-arb races ~once/minute/symbol,
5–10 µs, ~20% of volume, ~0.5 bp tax on all trading, ~$5B/yr, >80% of wins to
six firms ([BIS WP 955](https://www.bis.org/RePEc/bis/biswps/work955.redif));
the market design is a prisoner's dilemma
([Budish, Cramton & Shim 2015, QJE 130(4)](https://academic.oup.com/qje/article/130/4/1547/1916146)).
**Implication:** budget for an edge half-life, not an edge; obvious patterns
are already priced.

### 6.3 Payoff asymmetry — cross-entropy is not P&L
A wrong token at inference costs nothing. A wrong tick pays spread + fees +
impact — to a counterparty who may be better informed: the spread is partly
an adverse-selection premium ([Glosten & Milgrom 1985, JFE 14(1)](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/0304405X85900443)).
Magnitudes swamp typical short-horizon gross edges: the Lopez-Lira–Tang LLM
news strategy collapses from **+650% gross** to ~300% at 5 bp round-trip and
~150% at 10 bp ([arXiv:2304.07619](https://arxiv.org/abs/2304.07619));
an LLM trading agent's Sharpe drops 0.43 → 0.22 under realistic frictions
("The Alpha Illusion," via [Kinlay 2026](https://jonathankinlay.com/2026/08/your-research-agent-is-an-undisclosed-factor-exposure-and-so-is-everyone-elses/));
anomalies with >50% monthly turnover rarely survive costs
([Novy-Marx & Velikov 2016](https://ideas.repec.org/a/oup/rfinst/v29y2016i1p104-147..html)).
ES tick = 0.25 pts ≈ 0.4 bp at 6000
([CME specs](https://www.cmegroup.com/markets/equities/sp/e-mini-sandp500.contractSpecs.html)).
**Implication:** the binding constraint is cost-per-error, not accuracy; most
statistical next-tick predictability is an order of magnitude below the cost
floor.

### 6.4 Non-stationarity — language drifts over decades, markets shift in hours
Index-futures return autocorrelation dies within minutes; squared returns
show power-law memory (exponent 0.37) and anomalous kurtosis scaling
([Cont 1997, arXiv:cond-mat/9705075](https://arxiv.org/abs/cond-mat/9705075));
apparent long-range dependence / IGARCH in volatility is explained by
non-stationarity ([Mikosch & Stărică 2004, REStat 86(1)](https://ideas.repec.org/a/tpr/restat/v86y2004i1p378-390.html));
efficiency is an emergent, regime-conditional property of competing
strategies ([Lo 2004, Adaptive Markets](https://www.pm-research.com/content/iijpormgmt/30/5/15)).
**Implication:** walk-forward re-estimation is mandatory; parameter shelf
life is weeks, not decades.

### 6.5 Data scarcity + non-ergodicity — 15T tokens vs. one history
Llama 3 pretrained on >15T tokens with attention masked across document
boundaries — a huge, roughly-iid sample of a stable process
([Meta 2024](https://ai.meta.com/blog/meta-llama-3/)). ES gives ~10⁷ one-minute
bars since 1997 (arithmetic from
[CME](https://www.cmegroup.com/markets/equities/sp/e-mini-sandp500.contractSpecs.html))
— a ~10⁶× gap — and it is **one single realized path**: no reruns.
Wealth processes are non-ergodic; a positive-ensemble-expectation gamble can
have negative time-average growth
([Peters & Gell-Mann 2016, Chaos 26, 023103](https://arxiv.org/abs/1405.0585)).
The statistical consequence is backtest overfitting with thousands of
researcher degrees of freedom
([Bailey et al. 2014, Notices AMS 61(5)](https://www.ams.org/notices/201405/rnoti-p458.pdf);
[López de Prado, SSRN 3031282](https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=3031282)).
**Implication:** a backtest is one sample from one history with a
multiple-testing discount of hundreds; size for the time average (Kelly),
not the ensemble average.

### 6.6 No ground truth — there is no next token to compare against
Language has an external oracle: the token the human actually wrote. The
price process has none: price is the crowd's computed aggregation of
dispersed knowledge, and your prediction is an input to it
([Hayek 1945, AER 35(4)](https://sites.santafe.edu/~bowles/wp-content/uploads/Hayek-paper-2022-Foundational-papers-in-complexity.pdf));
price = value + noise with value unobservable
([Black 1986, JF 41(3)](https://www.jstor.org/stable/2328481));
prices move far more than subsequent dividends justify
([Shiller 1981](https://www.nber.org/papers/w0456)).
**Implication:** "accuracy" has no meaning at tick level; validation-set
performance is not evidence of live P&L.

### 6.7 The generator is cooperative; the counterparty is strategic
Text is produced to communicate — a process aligned with the statistics you
trained on. Order flow is produced by agents optimizing *against* you: the
insider hides in noise ([Kyle](https://www.jstor.org/stable/1913210)), the
market maker quotes to recoup adverse selection
([Glosten & Milgrom](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/0304405X85900443)),
the HFT race is game-theoretic
([Budish et al.](https://academic.oup.com/qje/article/130/4/1547/1916146)).
Scalping is a stochastic game against adaptive opponents; next-word
prediction is density estimation over a fixed distribution.
**Implication:** model intentions and reactions (queue position, spoofing,
stop runs), not just conditional probabilities.

### 6.8 Evaluation is contaminated — the "test set" is inside the training data
LLMs memorize pre-cutoff financial data; only post-cutoff performance is
informative ([Lopez-Lira, Tang & Zhu, arXiv:2504.14765](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.14765)).
Thinking-LLMs show no net advantage under costs; "next-token prediction
objectives … poorly aligned with heavy-tailed, weakly predictable stock
returns" ([Sodha 2025, arXiv:2511.08608](https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.08608)).
Eight frontier models trading live lost ~1/3 of capital in two weeks
([Citadel Global 2026](https://www.citadelglobal.co.za/markets-arent-algorithmic/)).
LLM signals are crowded by construction: eight independent LLM research runs
produced books correlated 0.62 — "an LLM is a fast, lossy index of the
published anomaly literature"
([Kinlay 2026](https://jonathankinlay.com/2026/08/your-research-agent-is-an-undisclosed-factor-exposure-and-so-is-everyone-elses/)).
**Implication:** leak-free, point-in-time, cost-realistic evaluation is the
hardest problem; popular-model edges are everyone's edges.

## 7. What our own archive says — the analogy, measured on NQ

The repo already contains the three measurements that test the analogy, and
they confirm the *refined* version of it:

| Measurement | Number | Doc |
|---|---|---|
| Unconditional next-60-min direction from the tape (OOS, walk-forward) | **50.6%** (always-up baseline 51.6%; best decile 56.3%) | `biasFit.ts` / `daily-bias-framework-2026-10-09.md` |
| Next-minute direction from candle shape (bar-shape proxies) | **≈50% flat**; "big lower wick" bucket 48% up | `tickMomentumProxyStudy.ts` / `TICK_MOMENTUM.md` |
| **Conditional** setups: failed flush → breakout (market entry) | **77.5% WR, PF 2.98**, 1R target, 3.5–30 pt risk, 4,822 trades | `PLAYBOOK.md` |
| Conditional setups: huge-bar expansion | 78.4% WR, PF 3.14 | `PLAYBOOK.md` |
| Naked daily up/down call ceiling | ~55–60% even in the best tail; precision lives in *which* context (FOMC day 83.8%, overnight leg 57.7% up) | `daily-bias-framework-2026-10-09.md` |

Reading: the *unconditional* next-step stream is a coin flip (low redundancy),
exactly what near-efficiency predicts — the NQ minute stream is nothing like
English, where the next word is predictable at ~50–75% redundancy. But
*conditional on rare, high-constraint order-flow states* (a flush that fails
to break the extreme, then a one-sided breakout bar), the next move is
strongly constrained — **this is the market equivalent of the next word
inside an idiom.** In language, most of next-word predictability is likewise
concentrated in high-constraint contexts ("New ___" → York); free-context
prediction is much weaker. The user's intuition is correct in its structure —
predict the locally constrained continuation, not the free-stream topic — and
the system already implements it: it only ever fires inside measured
high-constraint states, and it deliberately does not trade the unconditional
tape or the naked daily bias.

## 8. Verdict

**The analogy is true in form, true in the horizon direction, and dangerous
in magnitude — and its most useful version is the one our own archive
already proves.**

1. **True in form.** Both problems are conditional next-step prediction over
   a discrete stream; the one-step model is the primitive, and the
   long-horizon prediction is its iterated product with compounding error
   (§2). The machinery transfers so literally that the LOB literature now
   trains perplexity-scored autoregressive models on order-book messages
   (§4.5), and the training objective of a next-word model *is* the growth
   objective of a log-optimal bettor up to an odds constant (§5.2 — Kelly
   1956, Cover & Thomas Ch. 6). "Predict the next symbol, bet proportional
   to the edge, compound" is the same machine in both domains.

2. **True in direction, with a caveat.** For any near-martingale, next-step
   prediction is mechanically the least-hard problem: one-step SNR is
   constant while `k`-step SNR decays like `1/√k` (§2). And empirically, the
   tick/10-event horizon is the *only* place with reliably documented
   out-of-sample directional accuracy far above the coin flip (79–84% vs
   single-digit R² at monthly horizons), decaying with horizon (§4.3). The
   user's "short is easier than long" holds as a *statistical* claim about
   the next move.
   The caveat: markets have **no monotone difficulty gradient** — the
   autocorrelation sign flips across horizons (tick −, weekly +, monthly −,
   3–12mo +, 3–8yr −), and the biggest *economic* anomalies live at
   months-to-years (§4.2). "Next tick easier than next month" is not the
   same as "next word easier than next paragraph."

3. **Dangerous in magnitude — the constant, not the form, is the whole
   game.** Language: redundancy ≈ 50–75%, entropy 0.6–1.3 bits/char
   (Shannon 1951), trillions of near-iid tokens, exogenous cooperative
   generator, wrong predictions free. Markets: near max-entropy, thin
   horizon-decaying structure, one non-ergodic history, adversarial
   generator, wrong ticks cost spread+fee+impact, and the edge equilibrates
   at its cost (Grossman–Stiglitz; HFT Sharpe 4.3 on $0.46/contract). The
   next tick in markets is "easy" the way the market-maker's alternating
   coin is easy — **measurable but not monetizable by anyone who pays the
   spread.** The harvestable bits per symbol differ by an order of
   magnitude (§5.4).

4. **The version that survives — and that our archive proves — is the
   *conditional* one.** In language, most next-word predictability is
   concentrated in high-constraint contexts (the next word inside an idiom
   is near-determined; the next word in free prose is not). In markets the
   same is true: the unconditional NQ tape is a coin flip at every horizon
   we can measure (50.6% next-60-min, ~50% next-minute), while conditional
   on rare order-flow states — a flush that fails to break the extreme
   followed by a one-sided breakout — the next move is strongly constrained
   (77.5% WR at 1R, §7). **Scalping is next-word prediction only inside the
   market's idioms.** The job is not to predict the stream; it is to *wait
   for high-constraint contexts and only then predict the next step* — and
   to charge the spread for the privilege, not pay it (§4.4, §6.7).

5. **The inversion worth keeping.** The durable tick-level income documented
   in the literature is liquidity provision and inventory pricing
   (Avellaneda–Stoikov; Glosten–Milgrom) — the scalper who survives is
   closer to **being the generator others try to predict** (the speaker,
   not the listener) than to being a next-tick predictor (§6, §4.3). For a
   human paying retail/prop spreads, the middle path — trade the rare
   high-constraint states, hold the position one R, size by measured edge —
   is exactly what this system already does.

## 9. What this means for the NQ system

1. **Keep the horizon where the constraint lives.** Our edge is measured at
   1R within minutes on conditional setups (77.5% WR). The unconditional
   next-60-min and daily-bias calls are coin flips (~50.6%, 55–60% ceiling
   in the best tail). The analogy says: do not extend the horizon in search
   of a "topic" prediction — the compounding argument cuts against us, and
   our own data agrees. Existing design is correct; guard it.

2. **The conditional-entropy experiment (the missing measurement).** §5.6:
   no canonical bits/bar number exists for any index. On our archive we can
   compute, per signal state vs. outside it: (a) the entropy rate of the
   1-min NQ stream (permutation entropy / LZ compression); (b) mutual
   information `I(future; past)` at bar horizons 1–30; (c) **the conditional
   entropy of the next bar inside `MOM_PROD`/`EXP_PROD` states vs. the
   unconditional stream** — a direct, in-bits measurement of the "idiom
   effect" this note argues for. That would turn the analogy from metaphor
   into a number in our own tape. (Candidate CLI: `web/scripts/*.ts` +
   a `docs/research/*.md`, same pipeline as `biasFit.ts`.)

3. **Accuracy is not the objective; after-cost bits are.** The Kelly bridge
   says growth = I(future;past) − costs (§5.2). Our backtests already
   include the 0.95 pt cost and pessimistic fills — keep that discipline;
   the literature is full of 79–84% accuracies that die at the spread
   (DeepLOB's own caveat, §4.3). "High directional accuracy and zero
   trading profit are entirely compatible."

4. **Budget for an edge half-life.** McLean–Pontiff: published predictors
   lose 58% post-publication; our edges are private but the *class* of
   footprint/order-flow patterns is not — expect decay, keep the walk-forward
   discipline (§6.2, §6.4), and treat every trained parameter as having a
   shelf life.

5. **The Kelly mode is the bridge, already implemented.** `f* = edge/odds`
   with shrinkage toward priors is exactly the Cover–Thomas prescription
   (bet proportional to the true distribution, pay `D(p‖q)` for model
   error, §5.2) — with the one formal warning from §5.1: overbetting beyond
   `f*` ruins with probability 1, which is why the per-family mult finding
   in `kelly-mode-2026-10-07.md` §5.3 (m0.5 on marginal-edge families)
   matters more than any accuracy improvement.

6. **Do not chase the "language-model everything" version of this.** The
   market-as-language literature transfers *architectures* (LOBERT, Nagy,
   Kronos — §4.5, §5.5), not epistemics: no post-cost, post-impact
   profitability has been established for LLM/LOB-DL trading in fast Western
   markets (§4.4), live LLM trading tests lose money (§6.8), and LLM signals
   are crowded by construction. Our tape-conditioned, cost-aware, rare-state
   approach is the correct reading of the analogy — the LLM-shaped reading
   (train a big model on the stream) is the misreading the literature
   already falsifies.

7. **One formal caution to internalize:** the martingale says the best
   forecast at *every* horizon is "no change." Our setups are not a
   contradiction — they are bets that a rare, high-constraint state makes
   the conditional distribution non-martingale for exactly one step (the
   failed-flush breakout is a one-bar conditional edge), with the position
   sized so that the spread we cross is small relative to the constraint we
   measured. That is the precise sense in which scalping is next-word
   prediction: one step, one constraint, one R — never a topic, never a
   path.

# Naso hypotheses — integration + backtesting plan (2026-10-04)

**Source:** Richie Naso on the Words of Rizdom podcast ("He Exposes The Truth
About Market Algorithms", 2024-12, transcript in `transcripts/`). His claims,
mapped to falsifiable per-trade features. **Every claim is journal-only —
nothing votes, gates, or blocks a signal.** Same contract as the ES and
seasonal chips: features land in `signals.features` jsonb on every live card,
chips print on the card text, and the archive replays decide what is real.

## 1. What was integrated (logging only)

| Naso claim | Module | Features logged | Chips printed |
|---|---|---|---|
| "Algos print round numbers — especially 50. Don't put your stop at 50, put it at 40" | `web/lib/roundNumbers.ts` | `entryToRound50` · `stopToRound50` · `targetToRound50` (signed pts) · `stopAtRound` (±1 pt) · `targetCrossRound` · `entryAtRound` | `STOP @ROUND` · `TARGET CROSSES 50` · `ENTRY @ROUND` |
| "Algorithms come back to gaps — 50% of the gap is filled, if not all" | `web/lib/gapTracker.ts` | `sessionGaps` · `gapInPath` · `gapInPathPts` · `nearestUnfilledGap` · `recentGapFill` | `GAP IN PATH` · `GAP FILLED 30m` |
| "Algos are programmed to go to option strike prices" | `web/lib/wallProx.ts` | `wallAhead` · `wallDistPts` · `wallInPath` · `pastWall` | `WALL IN PATH` · `WALL nPT` · `PAST WALL` |

Wiring: `web/lib/signalFeed.ts` — momentum (main card, news-skip,
override-skip, retrace-arm, record), RTH (same), open family (features only,
no labels). Wall chips degrade silently while the options feed has no
snapshot (in-memory only, no extra network). Gap inventory is computed from
high/low overlap only (no opens/closes), so the live feed and the archive
use the identical definition.

**Why these three:** everything else Naso says is either already a measured
dimension here (VWAP side/distance/slope, premium-discount zones via
`priceaction.ts`) or already measured-and-rejected (stop-runs don't cluster
at POC/HVN — `context-veto-stoprun-2026-10-02.md`; wall-aware stop widening
degrades — `wall-aware-stop-proxy-2026-10-03.md`; round-number touches as
reversal entries are noise — the reversal family closure). The three above
were the only claims with no direct measurement.

## 2. The backtesting plan

### A. Round numbers vs stop-runs — `web/scripts/roundNumberStopStudy.ts`

The exact falsification of "don't put your stop at 50":

- **Harness:** the momentum-card replay (MOM_PROD + EXP_PROD, sequential
  one-trade-at-a-time, first-touch, 0.5 pt cost, 60-bar exit) — identical to
  `stopRunStudy.ts` so every number is comparable to the canonical stop-run
  baseline (stop-runs = 5% of stops, no hour clustering).
- **Phase 1:** baseline recap.
- **Phase 2:** buckets — stop ON a 50-handle (±1 pt) vs off; |stop distance|
  bands (0–1, 1–2.5, 2.5–5, 5–12.5, 12.5–25); target crossing a handle vs
  not; entry on a handle vs not. Reported: n, WR, PF, net, stops, stop-run
  share (depth ≤0.75 pt + ≥1R reversal in 30 bars), mean probe depth.
- **Phase 3:** Naso's remedy — re-score the ON-handle trades with the stop
  moved 1 pt off the number (a real replay, the wider stop fully charged).
- **Acceptance criteria (pre-registered):**
  - Naso supported ⇔ ON-handle stops show a *materially higher* stop-run
    share or mean depth than the off-handle baseline, AND the 1-pt pad on
    the ON-subset improves net by more than the global 1-pt pad does
    (the global pad degrades — `stopRunStudy.ts` phase 2).
  - Anything else → claim falsified on NQ 1-min data; the features stay
    logged as pure journal context, the chips stay labels.
- **40-session smoke run:** ON-handle 72.7% WR / PF 2.14 vs off-handle
  80.0% / 3.15 (n=11 vs 140, 0 stop-runs in slice); pad rescues 2 of 3
  stops (+13 pts). Direction matches Naso but n is nothing — full run
  decides. **Full-run verdict (2026-10-04): NOT supported** — see
  `docs/research/round-number-stoprun-2026-10-04.md` (stop-run share 6% vs
  5%, lower probe depth ON-handle, pad +0.14 pt/trade; the only positive
  cell is `targetCrossRound` — PF 3.41 vs 2.80, n=509 — which needs the
  train/test split before graduating beyond a label).

### B. Gap base rates + gap-ahead outcomes — `web/scripts/gapProximityStudy.ts`

- **Phase 1 (base rates, every session, every gap):** gaps/session, size
  distribution, half-fill/full-fill rates by size band and direction,
  median bars to half-fill. This tests Naso's "50% of the gap is filled"
  as a *statement about the data*, independent of any signal.
- **Phase 2 (signals):** momentum-card outcomes bucketed by `gapInPath`,
  nearest-unfilled-gap distance bands (0, ≤10, 10–30, >30, none), and
  `recentGapFill`. Gap features are computed on the bars known at entry
  (sliced at the entry bar — no lookahead).
- **Acceptance criteria:** a bucket must beat baseline on WR/PF/net with
  n ≥ ~100 and survive a 2026-01-01 train/test split before anything is
  ever considered beyond a label. Even then the first move is a
  `strategyInsights` observation, not a gate.
- **40-session smoke run (structural finding):** at 1-min resolution,
  high/low-overlap gaps are overwhelmingly one-tick (median 0.25 pt) and
  ~99% half-fill within a median of 3 bars — the "gap-fill" trade is
  trivial at this granularity. Multi-point gaps are rare (5 in 40
  sessions). `GAP IN PATH` will rarely print live. **Full-run verdict
  (2026-10-04): confirmed** — see
  `docs/research/gap-proximity-2026-10-04.md` (13,120 gaps: 97.9%
  half-filled in a median of 3 bars; the base-rate claim is true but the
  trade lives on the tick tape, not the minute bar. Signal side: no
  robust effect; `nearestUnfilledGap > 30pt` = 81.8% / PF 3.98, n=368 —
  a hypothesis pending the 2026-01-01 split).

### C. Strike/wall proximity — forward-logging only (no archive)

The CBOE QQQ chain is a live daily snapshot with no historical vendor feed
available — the same limitation that parked the wall-aware stop work
("re-test when historical gamma walls exist"). Plan:

1. **Forward log** (already wired): every card records `wallDistPts`,
   `wallInPath`, `pastWall` in `signals.features` jsonb.
2. **Mine the log:** after ~2–4 weeks of live signals, bucket by wall
   features directly from the `signals` table (a SQL study script, or the
   existing `strategyInsights` feature mining, which already reads the
   features jsonb). n will be small — treat as descriptive only.
3. **Optional archive reconstruction:** if the forward log hints at an
   effect worth the cost, backfill a daily wall snapshot per session date
   from the CBOE endpoint (one fetch/day, gentle) and replay. Explicitly
   deferred until step 2 shows a hint — the wall-aware-stop precedent says
   assume null until then.

## 3. Standing rules

- Chips are labels; features are jsonb; neither can gate. The only paths
  from a measured result to a behavior change are the existing ones:
  a playbook entry + a gate behind a feed flag, both after train/test.
- Every study output gets a `docs/research/*.md` note (negative results
  included — they are the conservation priority).
- The pullback-ticket card (OFF) and the reversal family (retired) do not
  carry the new chips; add them only if those cards ever come back.

# Live fix plan — make the executor actually run the backtested plan (2026-10-05)

> Execution stays ON per the owner's decision. Every step below is
> sequenced to reduce the bleed while conforming live execution to the
> validated plan. Policy path per step: `web/EXEC_CHANGE_POLICY.md`
> (backtest → tag → tests → approval for env).
>
> Grounding evidence: `docs/research/live-vs-backtest-2026-10-05.md`.
> Live facts at plan time (VPS `/api/gc?action=health`): executeLive=true,
> day P&L −$1,065 (dayKey 2026-10-04), giveback guard armed (peak 0 —
> inert on a red day), **live tick feed holds 7% of the session's true
> volume** (accumulatedVol 25,359 vs snapshotVol 355,812).

## F0 — today, zero code: reduce exposure while the fixes land

1. **Verify the VPS profile/size env** (Coolify): confirm
   `MOM_STOP_MULT`/`RTH_STOP_MULT` (expected 0.35/0.45) and
   `MOM_SIZE_MULT`/`RTH_SIZE_MULT` (the 10-04/05 fills at 26 micros ≈
   $312 risk imply ×2). If SIZE_MULT=2 → propose setting to 1 — halves
   per-trade risk with the sizing-optimizer's own cost ladder as evidence
   (at measured 0.95pt costs ×2 is the max PASS cell at *perfect fills*;
   with the measured −1.75pt loser drift it is not). **[env — approval]**
2. **Note the guard gap**: giveback protection (haltAt −250 from the day
   peak) only arms on green days; today's peak is 0 so it is inert while
   the day bleeds. Optional new knob: a hard **daily loss floor**
   (e.g. −$400/day, well inside the ~$885 of remaining drawdown room)
   — small `accountGuard.ts` change + env. **[code + env — approval]**

## F1 — the root fix: candle-synced live bars (code, deploy fast)

The live engine builds completed bars from the tick stream; the stream is
capturing ~7% of true volume, so every buy-frac/cluster/volume gate runs
on a 7% sample — the live cards (2W/8L on the archive tape) are a
different strategy than the backtested one.

- `lib/live.ts`: add a **rolling candle refresh** — every 60s fetch the
  completed minutes from the FOOTPRINT/V2 candle feed (the same feed the
  collector archives) and **overwrite** the tick-built bars (today's
  `seedFromFootprint` only fills gaps at bootstrap and never replaces).
  Mark each bar `source: "candle" | "tick"`.
- `lib/live.ts`: drop prints with no aggressor side instead of guessing
  up-tick = buy / down-tick = sell.
- `lib/signalFeed.ts`: a card may only fire on a candle-source bar;
  tick-source bars log + skip. (Signals fire on completed bars, so this
  costs nothing in the validated flow.)
- `/health`: expose the bar-source mix (candle % of the last 120 bars) —
  the 0.07 ratio becomes a monitored number instead of a silent killer.
- **Policy path**: data-fidelity fix — tag
  `[backtested: scripts/sizingOptimizer.ts --offline scripts/rthOptimizer.ts --offline]`
  (the detectors were validated on candle data; this commit makes live
  use that same data), full `npm test` + `npx tsc --noEmit`.
- **Effect**: live signals = archive signals; the entire validated WR/PF
  corpus applies again. Kills the tick-bar card population.

## F2 — absolute-price brackets (code)

Quote-anchored brackets cost ~$250–300/session (the 01:27 case: stop ran
by 0.25pt on a quote-anchored stop → −$300 swing). The REST path with
absolute `stopLoss`/`takeProfit` at the signal prices already exists
(`lib/crossTrade.ts` `placeCrossTradeOrderREST`) — wire the executor to
use it (or CHANGE-to-structural immediately after the webhook ack).
**Policy path**: cite `[backtested: scripts/retraceSlippageStudy.ts]`
(fill-model study) + tests.

## F3 — honest validation of the every-card plan (research, parallel)

DONE — `web/scripts/gapOnlyValidation.ts`: gap-only replay (every ≥5-bar
card, no position gate), **0.95pt cost**, modeled **−1.75pt adverse entry
drift on losers** (the TRADE_REVIEW measurement), MFF eval account sim,
train/test 2026-01-01, walk-forward 150→30. Grid: rate {gap, flat60} ×
stop mult {0.35…1.0} × drift {none, losers, all} + structural brackets +
first-N/day gates.

**Headline results (the drift=losers column is the honest one):**

| Cell (drift=losers) | exp pts | eval |
|---|---|---|
| MOM/EXP gap, any stop mult | +0.67…+1.14 | ALL breach |
| MOM/EXP flat60, any mult | +0.66…+1.40 | ALL breach |
| MOM/EXP first-1/2/3 structural | +1.29…+1.92 | breach |
| RTH gap s0.45 (current live) | +2.01 | breach |
| RTH flat60 structural (0.75R) | +3.14 | **PASS** |
| RTH first-3 structural | +4.28 | **PASS** |
| RTH first-1/2/3 profile | +4.34…+5.52 | **PASS** |

Walk-forward (gap rate, drift=losers): RTH structural **16/16 windows
PASS** · MOM structural 14/16 · EXP structural 13/16 · RTH profile 11/16 ·
MOM profile 9/16 · EXP profile 4/16.

Reads: (1) the every-card rate itself is NOT the problem — gap adds
positive-expectancy trades at drift=0; (2) the **entry drift is the
killer** — at −1.75pt on losers, every momentum/expansion config breaches
and only RTH structural (0.75R, first-N-gated) survives everywhere;
(3) the momentum family has no safe cell at measured frictions — suspend
until F1+F2 land and the drift is re-measured.

## F4 — stop multiples + sizing (env — approval only, after F3)

Proposed Coolify env changes (each shown to the owner before applying,
per policy rule 4):

| Key | Current | Proposed | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| `FEED_MOMENTUM` | (unset = 1) | `0` | momentum + expansion have no eval-passing cell at measured drift — suspend until re-measured post-F1/F2 |
| `RTH_PROFILE` | (unset = 1) | `0` | structural 0.75R = the 16/16 walk-forward cell (profile 0.45×/1.75R breaches) |
| `RTH_MAX_CARDS_PER_DAY` | (unset = 0) | `3` | first-3 structural +4.28 exp, eval PASS, consistency-safe |
| `DAILY_LOSS_FLOOR` | (unset = 0) | `400` | hard halt at −$400/day (the giveback guard is inert on red days) |
| `RTH_STOP_MULT` | runtime `0.45` (+ stale `0.65` preview) | delete | moot once RTH_PROFILE=0; removes the 2026-10-05 incident remnant |

## F5 — card-rate gate (code, only if F3 shows every-card is negative)

DONE in code, off by default: `RTH_MAX_CARDS_PER_DAY` (env 0 = off) in
`lib/signalFeed.ts`. F3 says the gate is needed for RTH at real frictions
(consistency cap), so F4 turns it on at 3. Momentum family: suspended
rather than gated (no passing cell exists).

## F1/F2 state

- F1 SHIPPED (code): candle-synced live bars — rolling FOOTPRINT/V2
